docs.title: Strategy
docs.text:
• Backend — integration-style tests through the public API (APITestCase), not the internal service classes, so they survive refactors. Written test-first: one failing behaviour test, then the smallest change that makes it pass. CI gates on ruff, ruff format, a missing-migration check, tests with coverage at or above 80%, check --deploy, and mypy strict.
  • Mobile — cubit tests for success, validation error and network failure, plus widget tests for the form. CI gates on dart format, flutter analyze --fatal-infos, and coverage at or above 25%.
  • UAT — a manual pass on staging before 29 Sep, following the checklist in each task plan.

docs.title: Running the suite locally
docs.text: config/settings.py calls load_dotenv(), so a local .env overrides the environment. api/test_security_settings.py (from #20) deletes DJANGO_DEBUG and PILAH_ALLOW_FAKE_GOOGLE_TOKEN and expects both to fall back to False, so it fails if a .env sets them. Pass the CI values as real environment variables instead of a .env when running the full suite.

docs.title: Work Log
docs.text:
What was done, when, and how long it took.

How durations are measured: from the timestamps of the Claude Code session and the commits, grouped into blocks separated by gaps of more than 45 minutes. Times are WIB. Rows marked self-reported use my own figure, and rows marked estimate cover work with no session behind it (for example decisions settled on Discord). The log covers hands-on development work and, from the week of 22 Sep, the team's standups (on Discord every Monday, Wednesday and Friday, 15–30 minutes, counted at 15) and the offline team sessions (UAT); other meetings and offline reading are not included.

docs.text: Situation What verification found Asked to renumber the migration to 0012 before #18 merged It would reference a migration that did not exist yet (NodeNotFoundError) and break every test; we stacked on #18 instead "Re-check before making the PR" Confirmed the branch was current with staging, the diff held only the intended files, and no secrets were committed; found a second PR using the same migration number A test written after its fix Proved it catches the bug by disabling the fix and watching it fail An ordering bug that "seemed fine" Showed it was nondeterministic: 6 of 10 runs passed before the fix, 10 of 10 after Production environment values considered for local testing Not used: they would break tests and point local runs at the production database AI's claim that PR #22's rounding needed a PO decision Corrected after reading #22's code: the policy was already set there

docs.title: Example: correcting the AI's direction on rounding
docs.text:
Review finding 2 was about legacy saldo keeping its sen after a pencairan, while PR #22 rounds sen away on setoran. The AI's first recommendation was to wait: it framed the rounding as a decision for the PO, then suggested holding off until #22 merged, because the shared helper bulatkan_rupiah only exists on #22's branch.

I decided otherwise: the two money flows should be consistent now, and the sen dropped. The AI then:

  1. Implemented the decision without waiting for #22, using the same rule inline (ROUND_DOWN to whole rupiah), and explained why it did not create its own api/kalkulasi.py (it would conflict with #22's file).
  2. Wrote the failing test first ("RED as expected: the 50 sen survive") in 9b135b2, then the fix in 2981176.
  3. Checked that its rounding was identical to #22's (quantize(Decimal(1), rounding=ROUND_DOWN)), so swapping in bulatkan_rupiah later changes nothing.

The follow-up is recorded publicly in the review thread: once #22 merges, the inline rounding is replaced with kalkulasi.bulatkan_rupiah.

docs.title: Programming
docs.text:
Competency level: 3

Standard principles applied and shown in that week's code: single responsibility, a service layer, and extension without modifying existing consumers.

docs.title: Single Responsibility + DRY: BalanceService — 5447710
docs.text:
Two places computed a running saldo by summing setoran only: TransactionDetailSerializer.get_saldo_setelah_transaksi and the Excel export. Instead of fixing the formula twice, the rule "setoran added, pencairan subtracted" lives in one class, used by both.

api/services.py
class BalanceService:
    """Running saldo for a nasabah: setoran added, pencairan subtracted."""

    @staticmethod
    def saldo_at(
        bank_sampah: BankSampah, nasabah_id: UUID, until: datetime, until_id: UUID
    ) -> Decimal:
        setoran = Transaksi.objects.filter(bank_sampah=bank_sampah, nasabah_id=nasabah_id).filter(
            Q(tanggal__lt=until) | Q(tanggal=until, id__lte=until_id)
        )
        # At an equal tanggal a pencairan is ordered after the setoran, so it is
        # excluded here; the export's merge below applies the same rule.
        pencairan = Pencairan.objects.filter(
            bank_sampah=bank_sampah, nasabah_id=nasabah_id, tanggal__lt=until
        )
        masuk = setoran.aggregate(total=Coalesce(Sum("total_nilai"), Decimal("0.00")))["total"]
        keluar = pencairan.aggregate(total=Coalesce(Sum("nominal"), Decimal("0.00")))["total"]
        return cast(Decimal, masuk - keluar)

The serializer is then one line, and the export applies the same ordering rule in its own running-total pass:

api/serializers.py
return BalanceService.saldo_at(obj.bank_sampah, obj.nasabah_id, obj.tanggal, obj.id)

The payoff came with review finding 3: the tie-break at an equal tanggal was wrong, and fixing it meant changing one rule in one place (765f90f) instead of hunting for every place a saldo was summed.

docs.title: Service layer: PencairanService — fbab07b
docs.text:
The business rule (lock the nasabah and saldo rows, check the saldo, record, deduct) sits in PencairanService.create_pencairan, not in the view. The whole operation is one atomic transaction, so a failure anywhere leaves neither a record nor a changed saldo.

api/services.py
class PencairanService:
    @staticmethod
    @transaction.atomic
    def create_pencairan(user: User, payload: Mapping[str, Any]) -> Pencairan:
        bank = user.bank_sampah
        assert bank is not None  # ponytail: views gate on IsActivePengelola
        nasabah = (
            Nasabah.objects.select_for_update()
            .filter(
                id=payload["nasabah_id"],
                bank_sampah=bank,
                is_active=True,
                status=Nasabah.Status.APPROVED,
            )
            .first()
        )
        if not nasabah:
            raise serializers.ValidationError(
                {"nasabah_id": ["Nasabah tidak ditemukan atau tidak aktif"]}
            )

        saldo, _ = Saldo.objects.select_for_update().get_or_create(nasabah=nasabah)
        nominal = payload["nominal"]
        saldo_sebelum = saldo.total_saldo
        if nominal > saldo_sebelum:
            raise serializers.ValidationError({"nominal": ["Saldo nasabah tidak mencukupi"]})
        ...

The view stays thin: validate, delegate, respond. It holds no business rule at all, following the existing TransactionService.create_setoran pattern.

api/views.py
    def create(self, request: Request) -> Response:
        serializer = PencairanCreateSerializer(data=request.data)
        serializer.is_valid(raise_exception=True)
        pencairan = PencairanService.create_pencairan(_user(request), serializer.validated_data)
        return Response(PencairanDetailSerializer(pencairan).data, status=status.HTTP_201_CREATED)

Because the saldo check happens inside the locked transaction, two simultaneous payouts cannot both pass it — the second waits for the row lock and then sees the reduced saldo.

docs.title: Open/Closed in practice: a separate Pencairan model — fbab07b
docs.text:
Adding a PENCAIRAN type to Transaksi with a negative value would have forced changes in every consumer that assumes a transaksi has items: the list serializer, export, dashboard and WhatsApp notifier. A new model extends the system without modifying them.

api/models.py
class Pencairan(TimestampedModel):
    class Metode(models.TextChoices):
        TUNAI = "tunai", "Tunai"
        TRANSFER = "transfer", "Transfer"

    nasabah = models.ForeignKey(Nasabah, on_delete=models.PROTECT, related_name="pencairan")
    bank_sampah = models.ForeignKey(BankSampah, on_delete=models.PROTECT, related_name="pencairan")
    dicatat_oleh = models.ForeignKey(
        User, on_delete=models.PROTECT, related_name="pencairan_dicatat"
    )
    nominal = models.DecimalField(max_digits=14, decimal_places=2)
    metode = models.CharField(max_length=20, choices=Metode.choices)
    # Receipt snapshots at record time; PIL-230 decides how edits affect them.
    saldo_sebelum = models.DecimalField(max_digits=14, decimal_places=2)
    saldo_sesudah = models.DecimalField(max_digits=14, decimal_places=2)

    class Meta:
        db_table = "pencairan"
        ordering = ["-tanggal"]
        indexes = [models.Index(fields=["bank_sampah", "nasabah", "tanggal"])]
        constraints = [
            models.CheckConstraint(
                condition=models.Q(nominal__gt=0), name="pencairan_nominal_positive"
            ),
        ]

PROTECT on all three foreign keys keeps a money record from losing the nasabah, bank or pengurus it refers to, and the check constraint enforces a positive nominal in the database as well as in the serializer. The trade-off is documented in the PR description and the task plan.

docs.title: Consistency with existing rules — 49cd153
docs.text:
Review finding 1 was that pencairan accepted any active nasabah, while setoran already required an approved membership — so a pending member could be paid out but not deposit. The fix makes both money flows resolve the nasabah the same way:

api/services.py — identical in create_setoran and create_pencairan
            Nasabah.objects.select_for_update()
            .filter(
                id=payload["nasabah_id"],
                bank_sampah=bank,
                is_active=True,
                status=Nasabah.Status.APPROVED,
            )
            .first()

One rule, applied on both sides, rather than a second variation of "who may transact".

docs.title: Removing dead code — bd38dc6
docs.text:
PencairanViewSet.list had an unpaginated fallback that could never run, because StandardPagination is the global default, so paginate_queryset never returns None. Six lines became two, and the reason is written down so the next reader does not restore the branch:

api/views.py — bd38dc6
     def list(self, request: Request) -> Response:
-        qs = self.get_queryset()
-        page = self.paginate_queryset(qs)
-        serializer = PencairanDetailSerializer(page if page is not None else qs, many=True)
-        if page is not None:
-            return self.get_paginated_response(serializer.data)
-        return Response(serializer.data)
+        # Pagination is configured globally (PAGE_SIZE), so a page always exists.
+        page = self.paginate_queryset(self.get_queryset())
+        return self.get_paginated_response(PencairanDetailSerializer(page, many=True).data)

The list test stayed green, which is what made the deletion safe rather than hopeful.

docs.title: Security
docs.text:
Competency level: 1

Code prevents OWASP A01 (Broken Access Control) and A04 (Insecure Design), each control guarded by a test.

docs.title: The two controls in code
docs.text:
Every pencairan endpoint carries the permission class, and every query is rooted at the caller's own bank sampah, taken from the session rather than from the request body:

api/views.py
class PencairanViewSet(viewsets.GenericViewSet):
    permission_classes = [IsActivePengelola]
    serializer_class = PencairanDetailSerializer

    def get_queryset(self) -> QuerySet[Pencairan]:
        qs = Pencairan.objects.filter(bank_sampah=_bank_sampah(self.request)).select_related(
            "nasabah", "bank_sampah", "dicatat_oleh"
        )

_bank_sampah reads the bank off the authenticated user, so a caller cannot name someone else's bank:

api/views.py
def _bank_sampah(request: Request) -> BankSampah:
    bank = _user(request).bank_sampah
    assert bank is not None  # ponytail: IsActivePengelola guarantees bank membership
    return bank

Because the filter is part of the base queryset, retrieve on another bank's pencairan finds nothing and returns 404 rather than 403 — the record's existence is never confirmed.

api/tests.py — test_pencairan_detail_is_scoped_to_bank_sampah
        self.assertEqual(
            self.client.get(f"/api/v1/pencairan/{created.data['id']}").status_code, 404
        )
        ...
        self.assertEqual(self.client.post("/api/v1/pencairan", {}, format="json").status_code, 403)

        self.client.credentials()
        self.assertEqual(self.client.post("/api/v1/pencairan", {}, format="json").status_code, 401)

No mass assignment: the write serializer accepts five fields and nothing else. bank_sampah, dicatat_oleh, status and both saldo snapshots are set by the service, so a crafted request body cannot book a payout against another bank or forge a receipt.

api/serializers.py
class PencairanCreateSerializer(serializers.Serializer[Any]):
    nasabah_id = serializers.UUIDField(required=True)
    nominal = serializers.DecimalField(max_digits=14, decimal_places=2, required=True)
    metode = serializers.ChoiceField(choices=Pencairan.Metode.choices, required=True)
    tanggal = serializers.DateTimeField(required=False)
    keterangan = serializers.CharField(
        required=False, allow_blank=True, allow_null=True, max_length=255
    )

The money rules are enforced twice, in the serializer and again in the database:

api/serializers.py
    def validate_nominal(self, value: Decimal) -> Decimal:
        if value <= 0:
            raise serializers.ValidationError("Nominal harus lebih dari nol")
        if value != value.to_integral_value():
            raise serializers.ValidationError("Nominal harus dalam rupiah bulat tanpa desimal")
        return value
api/models.py
        constraints = [
            models.CheckConstraint(
                condition=models.Q(nominal__gt=0), name="pencairan_nominal_positive"
            ),
        ]

And the A04 control — the saldo check runs inside the same locked transaction that writes the record, so two concurrent payouts cannot both pass it:

api/services.py
        saldo, _ = Saldo.objects.select_for_update().get_or_create(nasabah=nasabah)
        nominal = payload["nominal"]
        saldo_sebelum = saldo.total_saldo
        if nominal > saldo_sebelum:
            raise serializers.ValidationError({"nominal": ["Saldo nasabah tidak mencukupi"]})

docs.title: A01 · Broken Access Control

docs.title: 1. What TDD means
docs.text:
Test-Driven Development means writing the test before the code it tests. The test describes the behaviour I want, and the code is written only to make that test pass. Each behaviour goes through a short cycle:

  1. Red: write a test for one behaviour and run it. It fails, because the behaviour doesn't exist yet.
  2. Green: write the least code that makes the test pass.
  3. Refactor: clean up the code while every test stays green.

The cycle repeats, one behaviour at a time, until the feature is done. The tests then stay in the project as a safety net: any later change that breaks a behaviour turns its test red straight away.

In PILAH each step is its own commit, so the order can be checked in the history:

  • test(...): [RED] … adds only the failing test;
  • feat(...): [GREEN] … or fix(...): [GREEN] … adds the code that makes it pass;
  • refactor(...): [REFACTOR] … comes only after green.

A test that already passes when written is committed as a coverage test (test(...): cover …) with no phase tag, so it is never presented as a red.

Each change is logged pilah-be #137 pilah-mobile #174 26 Oct – 17 Nov, over three review rounds 3 Void a setoran (PIL-428) A pengurus cancels a recorded setoran with a reason. docs.title: 6. Positive, negative and corner cases
docs.text:
Case Meaning Positive Valid input: the feature does what it should Negative Invalid input or a forbidden action: the feature refuses it, with an error, and changes nothing Edge One input at the limit of its allowed range: the very first or very last value, or the one right next to it. Bugs hide at the edges, for example < written where <= was meant Corner Several inputs at their limits at the same time. Each limit may work on its own and still fail in combination

Positive and negative say whether the input is valid. Edge and corner say where the input sits in its range. So an edge or corner case can be positive or negative: in the example below, age = 120 is a valid edge (positive), while age = 121 is an invalid one (negative).

docs.title: How edge and corner cases are chosen
docs.text:
One input. Take an input that accepts whole numbers from 1 to 10:

Value Case Why it is tested 5 Positive A normal value in the middle of the range 1 and 10 Edge, positive The first and last values allowed. A < written for <= rejects 10 by mistake 2 and 9 Edge, positive The values just inside the ends, to show the rule is not off by one 0 and 11 Edge, negative The values just outside the range, which must be refused

Two inputs. Take a function calculatePrice(age, quantity), where age is 0–120 and quantity is 1–100:

Type Example input Why Edge case age = 0 One parameter at its limit Edge case quantity = 100 One parameter at its limit Corner case age = 0 and quantity = 100 Both at their limits together

In PILAH. A setoran can be voided only while the saldo stays at 0 or above, both after the void and at the time of every later pencairan. In the void tests, the nasabah has one setoran of 6,000 (2 kg at 3,000). The tests are shown below:

Situation Case Expected Nothing paid out yet: the void leaves the saldo at exactly 0 Edge, positive: one value (the final saldo) at its limit Accepted (200) 5,000 already paid out: the void would leave −5,000 Negative: outside the range Refused (409), and the saldo stays 1,000 A later setoran keeps the final saldo positive, but the saldo at the time of an earlier pencairan would drop below 0 Corner, negative: two saldo values checked together, the one at the end and the one at the pencairan's time Refused (409)

The tests cover the end of the range and a value outside it. A value just inside the end, such as a void that leaves 1 rupiah, is not tested separately.

docs.title: How I write the tests for these cases
docs.text:
The steps, using the void as the example:

  1. Find the limit in the rule. The rule is "the saldo stays at 0 or above, at the end and at the time of every later pencairan". So the limit is 0, and it is checked in two places.
  2. Build dummy data that lands exactly on the limit. setUp records one setoran of 2 kg at 3,000, a saldo of 6,000. Voiding it leaves exactly 0. Because the test makes its own data, the edge is hit on purpose, not by luck.
  3. Write one test per case, named after the behaviour:
    • the edge, accepted;
    • the negative case, refused;
    • the corner case, refused.
  4. Assert the result, and that nothing else changed. A refusal is not just a 409. The test also checks that:
    • the setoran is still tercatat;
    • the saldo is unchanged;
    • the earlier pencairan's snapshot is unchanged.
  5. Commit the test red, before the code:
    • the edge test in f3c3db7, before the green 638cb3f;
    • the negative and corner tests in 99de195, before the green 966c7ba.

The dummy data. setUp builds a bank, a pengurus, a nasabah and one jenis sampah at 3,000 per kg, then records one setoran of 2 kg through the API. Three helpers keep each test short:

  • _setor records a setoran;
  • _cairkan records a pencairan;
  • _batalkan sends the void request.
apps/ledger/test_setoran_void.py (setUp, from f3c3db7)
def setUp(self) -> None:
    self.bank = BankSampah.objects.create(
        nama="Bank Void", alamat="Depok", kota="Depok", no_hp_pic="+628123456789"
    )
    self.pengelola = User.objects.create_user(
        email="void@example.test",
        nama="Pengelola",
        bank_sampah=self.bank,
        is_profile_complete=True,
        is_primary_pengelola=True,
    )
    self.nasabah = Nasabah.objects.create(
        bank_sampah=self.bank,
        nomor="NAS-0001",
        nama="Budi",
        no_hp="+628111111111",
        alamat="Jl. A",
    )
    self.pet = buat_jenis_sampah(
        bank_sampah=self.bank, nomor="PET", nama_sampah="Botol PET", harga_per_kg=Decimal(3000)
    )
    self.client.force_authenticate(self.pengelola)
    self.transaksi = self._setor("2.000")

The edge case: the saldo left at exactly 0 (f3c3db7). It voids the only setoran and expects 200 and a saldo of exactly 0. The row stays, because a void is a soft delete.

apps/ledger/test_setoran_void.py
def test_void_marks_the_setoran_and_takes_it_out_of_the_saldo(self) -> None:
    response = self._batalkan()

    self.assertEqual(response.status_code, 200)
    self.assertEqual(response.data["status"], "dibatalkan")
    self.assertEqual(response.data["alasan_batal"], "Salah nasabah")
    self.assertEqual(response.data["dibatalkan_oleh"], str(self.pengelola.id))
    self.assertEqual(response.data["dibatalkan_oleh_nama"], "Pengelola")
    self.assertIsNotNone(response.data["dibatalkan_pada"])
    self.assertEqual(self._saldo(), Decimal(0))
    # Soft delete: the row and its items stay.
    self.assertTrue(Transaksi.objects.filter(pk=self.transaksi.pk).exists())
    self.assertEqual(self.transaksi.items.count(), 1)

The negative case: below 0 (99de195). 5,000 is paid out first, so voiding the 6,000 setoran would leave −5,000. The test expects 409 and checks that nothing changed: the setoran is still tercatat, and the saldo is still 1,000.

apps/ledger/test_setoran_void.py
def test_void_of_money_already_paid_out_is_rejected(self) -> None:
    self._cairkan(5000, self.transaksi.tanggal + timedelta(hours=1))

    response = self._batalkan()

    self.assertEqual(response.status_code, 409)
    self.assertEqual(self._status(), Transaksi.Status.TERCATAT)
    self.assertEqual(self._saldo(), Decimal(1000))

The corner case: two limits together (99de195). The test builds a timeline in which only one of the two checks fails:

Time Step Saldo T The setoran from setUp 6,000 T + 1 h A pencairan of 5,000 1,000 T + 2 h A second setoran of 6,000 7,000

Voiding the first setoran would leave a final saldo of 1,000. That is positive, so checking only the end would wrongly allow the void. But at T + 1 h the saldo before the pencairan would be 0, so the 5,000 would have been paid from nothing. The test expects 409, the setoran still tercatat, and the pencairan's recorded saldo_sebelum still 6,000.

apps/ledger/test_setoran_void.py
def test_void_that_leaves_a_later_pencairan_unfunded_is_rejected(self) -> None:
    # Saldo ends positive, but the 5.000 pencairan would have been paid from nothing.
    cair = self._cairkan(5000, self.transaksi.tanggal + timedelta(hours=1))
    kedua = self._setor("2.000")
    Transaksi.objects.filter(pk=kedua.pk).update(tanggal=cair.tanggal + timedelta(hours=1))

    response = self._batalkan()

    self.assertEqual(response.status_code, 409)
    self.assertEqual(self._status(), Transaksi.Status.TERCATAT)
    cair.refresh_from_db()
    self.assertEqual(cair.saldo_sebelum, Decimal(6000))

docs.title: Per feature
docs.text:
Scheduled prices

Positive Negative Edge and corner
  • A price changed now.
  • A price changed from a future date.
  • A setoran priced from the version in effect.
  • The app saves a price now or from a date.
  • A backdated date, a date more than 365 days ahead, or a date without a UTC offset.
  • Another bank gets 404; a nasabah gets 403.
  • A price of 0 or below is refused by the database.
  • An unchanged price records nothing.
  • Two versions starting at the same instant: the newest row wins.
  • A scheduled version is invisible before its start.
  • A PUT from an older app with the same price adds no version.
  • The migration's reverse restores the price in effect, ignoring a future one.
  • A local midnight is sent with its UTC offset.
  • An older reload answering last.

Role change before onboarding

Positive Negative Edge and corner
  • Each registration role reached from another: 200, the next step is Lengkapi Profil, and the new token carries the new role.
  • Each change writes one log row.
  • In the app, picking another role drops the old draft and opens Lengkapi Profil, which names the role with "Ganti peran".
  • A completed profile, a bank sampah (pending included) or a linked membership: 409, and the role is unchanged.
  • Anonymous: 401. Superadmin: 403. Asking to become superadmin: 422.
  • A refused change writes no log row.
  • In the app, a refusal shows "Ganti Peran Gagal" with the reason, and the page and draft stay.
  • A registration in progress in another thread: the change waits, then gets 409.
  • An account loaded before a bank was registered: still 409.
  • Re-picking the current role: 200, no log row, and the app keeps the draft.
  • A malformed success response returns a failure instead of crashing.
  • An account past the profile step is sent to login.

Void a setoran

Positive Negative Edge and corner
  • Response 200, with status, who, when and why stored.
  • The saldo is reduced and later pencairan are shifted.
  • In the app, hold a row, then Hapus with an alasan.
  • No alasan gets 422.
  • Another bank's setoran gets 404; a nasabah gets 403.
  • Voiding again, editing, or resending the WhatsApp receipt gets 409.
  • Money already paid out (the saldo would go below 0) gets 409.
  • The app shows "Alasan pembatalan wajib diisi" and sends nothing.
  • Voiding the only setoran takes the saldo to exactly 0, which is allowed.
  • A void that would leave a later pencairan unfunded is refused, even though the final saldo stays positive.
  • An export period with only voided rows has no data.
  • A partial update straight to the database raises IntegrityError.

docs.title: 7. Benefits of TDD, from development data
7.1 Defects caught by a failing test before merge
docs.text:
Each defect below was first reproduced by a red test, then fixed. None of them reached staging, and from then on each was guarded by its test, so it couldn't silently come back.

# Feature Defect How it surfaced Data Red → green 1 Prices The newest-version tie-break worked only because SQLite happened to return rows in that order. Postgres, used in production, makes no such promise My own test passed with no code Made explicit as a refactor, with the reason in the commit 95a62f3 2 Prices Reseeding repriced a historical setoran at today's price Review A 3,500 snapshot became 99,999 857735b → f67a84f 3 Prices When only the new price failed after the other fields saved, the sheet reported a total failure Review — 5a80375 → race test on PostgreSQL c428c32 → d19cb8d 8 Role change Completing the profile next to a role change answered with a stale role Review (Tristan) The red failed on the response's role and, on PostgreSQL, on the role change not waiting 9424d9f, 870224d → 51a631e 9 Role change Re-picking the same role dropped the typed draft, and a real change left the old input in the form Review (Pascal, Heraldo, Tristan) The red: hasProfileDraft false, and "Diketik Untuk Pengurus" still in the name field 26dce38 → 3d0a81b 10 Role change On web, the role page had no way back to Lengkapi Profil Review (Tristan) The red: no Kembali on the page 42d2020 → ef55977 11 Void The Hapus dialog stretched across a desktop window, and a voided detail still showed a saldo Playwright E2E Screenshot run at desktop and phone sizes df1fc4c → 4d16698 12 Void Merging staging replaced the detail sheet with an inline row and silently dropped the Pembatalan section Red test after the merge The red failed with Found 0 widgets with text "PEMBATALAN" 5af4e5d → ef7a0b9

Eight of the twelve came from review. Writing a failing test first made each one cheap to fix and hard to lose:

  • the reviewer could see the bug reproduced, then fixed, in two commits;
  • the eight green commits for the review findings were between +4 and +34 lines each.

docs.title: 7.2 Changing existing code safely (maintenance and iteration)
docs.text:
Each feature had to change code that other features already depended on. The tests are what made those changes safe.

  • Scheduled prices replaced a column the whole setoran flow depended on.
    • The green commit ad352fb touched 14 files (+172 −57) to replace JenisSampah.harga_per_kg with price versions.
    • Its red test, caaceab (+126), drives the migration forwards and backwards. The same migration was also run forwards, backwards and forwards again on a restored copy of the production database.

  • The role-change rule turned out to have five other code paths that can break it, all pointed out in review:

    • bank registration, membership application and invite acceptance (7.1 row 6);
    • Google login (row 7);
    • profile completion (row 8).

    Each got a red race test first, then took the same account lock, which is now one lock_account entry point. - Voiding changed what every report counts. - The red 1aa13a0 (+124) checks five existing reports: the Excel export, dashboard stats, trends, categories and the nasabah statement. - The green commit that made all five pass was only +14 −5. - Refactors with the suite as the safety net:

    Refactor Size Tests before and after ae850a0: every counted-setoran query through one tercatat() method 11 files, +48 −31 898 backend tests, the same result before and after ca2ec7a: the TIPE badge without nested ternaries +18 −17 321 transaksi tests, the same result before and after ee9668d: price selection out of the shared kalkulasi module 2 files, +8 −20 The #79 suite, green before and after

  • The safety net keeps growing. The backend suite had 464 tests after scheduled prices (S1W3) and 898 by the time of the void (S3W1). These are whole-suite counts and include teammates' tests. Each feature was built on top of the tests of the ones before it.

docs.title: 7.3 Cost
docs.text:
• Code written: 2,708 lines of test for 2,107 lines of production code, about 1.29 to 1 (section 3.7).
  • Time: many cycles are only a minute apart, so the timestamps show when the commits were recorded, not how long each cycle took. I make no claim about time per cycle.

What the data does support:

  • each of the 12 defects in 7.1 was fixed in its own red and green commits;
  • none of them needed a fix after merge.

docs.title: 7.4 Limits of this analysis
docs.text:
• There is no control group: I can't show how many of these defects would have reached production without TDD.
  • Eight of the twelve defects were spotted by a reviewer, not by my tests. TDD's part was turning each into a permanent regression test.
  • Test fixtures and race harnesses make the red side heavier. The PIL-451 race test alone is +147 lines.

docs.title: 8. Tools and methods
docs.text: Tool or method What it adds to TDD Where Phase-tagged commits ([RED], [GREEN], [REFACTOR]) The red → green order can be checked from git log alone Section 3 diff-cover Coverage of only the lines a change touches, so a gap can't hide in a large overall percentage Every MR, section 4 SonarCloud quality gate New-code coverage and code issues on every pull request, before review Every MR Mutation checks When a test passes the first time, I break the code it guards and watch it fail, then revert. This proves the test can fail PIL-451's coverage tests (section 3.3); the PIL-304 rounding follow-up (#89): 315600.75 != 315600.00 mocktail (Flutter) Mocks and stubs for one layer at a time, captureAny for the exact request sent Appendix C Completers Decide which async call answers first, so a race is reproduced every run Appendix D StubApi (a fake HTTP adapter) The real data source, repository and notifier run against canned server responses Appendix F Two-thread race tests (TransactionTestCase on PostgreSQL) One thread is paused at a fixed point while the other runs, so a race happens the same way every run PIL-451, 7.1 rows 6–8 Django MigrationExecutor A migration tested forwards and backwards inside the test suite caaceab CaptureQueriesContext Asserts a list costs the same number of queries for 1 row and for 5, catching N+1 queries c2a7c71 The database as the oracle A check constraint is tested by attempting the bad write and expecting IntegrityError Appendix E Postgres 16 locally (pgserver) The suite also runs on the production database engine, not only on SQLite. Behaviour SQLite only happens to show, like the row order in 7.1 row 1, can't pass by luck PIL-304, PIL-451, PIL-428 Playwright E2E Drives the web build at desktop and phone sizes and reads the result back from the database. It found 7.1 row 11 PIL-428

docs.title: 9. Test isolation: stubs, mocks and dummy data
9.1 Stub vs mock
docs.text:
• Stub: a fake dependency that returns pre-set answers, so my code has the data it needs. The test checks my code's output.
  • Mock: a fake dependency that records how my code used it. The test checks that the right calls were made.

Both are test doubles: stand-ins for a real dependency, so a test can run one unit without the units it calls.

Stub Mock What it does Returns a prepared answer when it is called Records how it was called, so the test can check the calls What the test checks The result of the unit under test (its state or its output) The interaction: was the dependency called, how often, with what arguments In mocktail (Flutter) when(() => getHarga.execute()).thenAnswer(...) verify(() => network.post(path, data: captureAny(named: 'data'))) and verifyNever(...) In Python unittest.mock.patch(...) with a return_value mock.assert_called_once_with(...) Example Appendix D: the use case is stubbed to answer from two Completers, and the test checks the price the cubit shows Appendix C: the network service is mocked, and the test checks the body that was POSTed

A third kind, a fake, is a light working implementation of the dependency. An example is StubApi, which answers HTTP requests per route (Appendix F).

docs.title: 9.2 When I use each
docs.text:
• A stub, when the unit needs an input from its dependency. The price cubit needs a list of prices from the use case. The stub hands it a fixed list, and the test checks what the cubit shows.
  • A mock, when the thing I'm testing is the call. The repository must send the right body to the server. The mock captures the request, and the test checks the body, down to the UTC offset of a local midnight. Another example: on invalid input nothing may be sent at all, which verifyNever checks.
  • Neither, when the dependency is the behaviour under test. The backend tests run against a real test database, because row locks, check constraints and the saldo replay only exist in the database. A mocked database would pass while the real query is wrong.

docs.title: 9.3 Why use stubs and mocks
docs.text:
1. Isolation. When a test fails, the failure is in the one unit under test, not somewhere in the layers below it.
  2. No slow or unavailable dependencies. App tests don't need a running server, a network or a signed-in Google account.
  3. Situations that are hard to make for real. A stub can return a 409 conflict, a timeout, a malformed response, or two responses in reverse order. Defect 7.1 row 4 could only be reproduced this way.
  4. Checking side effects that have no return value, such as a request being sent once, or not at all.
  5. Building test-first, top down. A cubit can be built and tested before the repository below it exists, by stubbing the repository.

docs.title: 9.4 Why dummy data, not real data
docs.text:
A test that reads real data depends on something it doesn't control. Real data is whatever happens to be in the production database, or on a server, right now. That dependency breaks tests in four ways:

Problem with real data What happens to the test With dummy data It changes. Someone records a setoran, and a saldo moves The same test passes today and fails tomorrow, with no code change The test creates its own data, so the input is always the same It may not contain the case. No nasabah has a saldo exactly equal to the setoran I want to void The corner case can't be tested at all The test creates exactly the case it needs: one setoran of 6,000, so voiding it takes the saldo to exactly 0 It belongs to others. Tests that write would change or delete real records, and other tests share them Tests interfere with each other and with real users Each backend test runs in its own test database, rolled back after every test It is personal. Real nasabah have names, phone numbers and saldo Personal data ends up in test code, logs and CI Dummy values: "Bank Void", nasabah "Budi", void@example.test, +628111111111

Dummy data does for data what a stub does for code: it removes the dependency, so the test depends only on itself. In PILAH:

  • Backend: each test's setUp creates its own bank, pengelola, nasabah and jenis sampah, then records a setoran through the API (test_setoran_void.py). Everything runs in a test database Django creates fresh for the run.
  • App: tests feed canned JSON through mocks or StubApi.

The one place real data is used is a manual check outside the test suite: the PIL-304 migration was run on a restored copy of the production database, because the question there was precisely "does this work on the real data?"

docs.title: 10. The F.I.R.S.T. principle
docs.text:
Five properties of good unit tests:

Letter Meaning In PILAH Fast Tests run in milliseconds, so they can run after every change App tests use mocks and StubApi, with no server. Backend tests roll back a transaction instead of rebuilding the database Independent No test depends on another test or on the order they run in Each test creates its own data in setUp and shares nothing with the others Repeatable The same result every run, on any machine, at any time
  • Time is injected (now: () => DateTime(2026, 10, 7, 10)), so a date test doesn't depend on today.
  • Completers fix the order of async answers instead of timing them.
  • Race tests pause one thread at a fixed point, so the race happens the same way every run (7.1 row 7).
Self-validating The test decides pass or fail by itself; nobody reads its output Every test asserts exact values: the status code, the saldo, the request body. Mutation checks show the assertions can fail Timely The test is written at the right time: before the code The red commit comes before the green one (section 3). Tests written after the code are labelled as coverage tests

docs.title: 11. Mapping to the rubric
docs.text: Level Criterion Evidence Status 1 TDD on at least one feature, or explain the TDD process Section 1, section 3 Met 2 TDD on at least 3 features (backend and frontend counted separately, CRUD as 1), with positive and negative cases 3 features × 2 sides = 6, sections 2–3, section 6 Met 2 Explain how test cases are designed Section 3 (one behaviour per cycle) and section 6 Met 3 Disciplined commits and high coverage; Part B TDD ≥ 3 for at least a month Sections 3–5 Met 3 Positive, negative and corner cases for every feature Section 6 Met 3 Explain how corner cases are identified Section 6 Met 3 Explain best practices and test isolation (mock/stub) Section 9 and section 10 Met 4 A written analysis of TDD's benefits, based on concrete development data Section 7 Written; not claimed 4 Tools or methods that make TDD more efficient and thorough Section 8 Written; not claimed

docs.title: Appendix: test code
docs.text: Excerpts from the commits named, as committed. Lines removed for length are marked ….

docs.title: Appendix A: a stale account object (role change, backend)
docs.text:
From bf3a529. The request loaded the account before a parallel request registered a bank sampah, so it holds a stale object. The role must still stay locked. The test passed when written, so it is a coverage test. Against a check-then-save version of change_role it failed with "AuthServiceError not raised", which proves it guards the code.

apps/authentication/test_role_change.py
def test_a_bank_registered_after_the_account_was_loaded_still_keeps_the_role(self) -> None:
    user = self._fresh(User.Role.PENGELOLA)
    # Loaded by this request before a parallel one registered a bank sampah.
    stale = User.objects.get(pk=user.pk)
    bank = BankSampah.objects.create(
        nama="Bank Baru",
        alamat="Depok",
        no_hp_pic="+628111111111",
        status=BankSampah.Status.PENDING,
    )
    User.objects.filter(pk=user.pk).update(bank_sampah=bank)

    with self.assertRaises(AuthServiceError) as refused:
        AuthService.change_role(stale, User.Role.NASABAH)

    self.assertEqual(refused.exception.code, "role_locked")
    user.refresh_from_db()
    self.assertEqual(user.role, User.Role.PENGELOLA)

docs.title: Appendix B: a void at the edge of the saldo
docs.text: The edge, negative and corner tests for the void, with their setUp, are in section 6, How I write the tests for these cases.

docs.title: Appendix C: a mock that captures the request
docs.text:
From c7fa0b5. NetworkService is a mocktail mock:

  • when(...) stubs its answer;
  • verify(...).captured mocks it, checking the exact body the repository POSTed, with no server involved.
test/features/harga/data/harga_repository_impl_test.dart
class _MockNetworkService extends Mock implements NetworkService {}

void main() {
  late _MockNetworkService network;
  late HargaRepositoryImpl repository;

  setUp(() {
    network = _MockNetworkService();
    repository = HargaRepositoryImpl(HargaRemoteDataSourceImpl(network));
  });

  group('ubahHarga', () {
    const path = '/api/v1/jenis-sampah/j-1/harga';

    setUp(() {
      when(() => network.post(path, data: any(named: 'data')))
          .thenAnswer((_) async => _ok(path));
    });

    test('posts a scheduled price with its local start time and offset',
        () async {
      final tengahMalam = DateTime(2026, 10, 15);

      final result = await repository.ubahHarga(
        UbahHarga(id: 'j-1', harga: 5000, berlakuMulai: tengahMalam),
      );

      expect(result, const Right<NetworkException, void>(null));
      final data = verify(
        () => network.post(path, data: captureAny(named: 'data')),
      ).captured.single;
      expect(data, {
        'harga_per_kg': '5000',
        'berlaku_mulai': isoDenganOffset(tengahMalam),
      });
    });

    test('leaves berlaku_mulai out so the price applies now', () async {
      await repository.ubahHarga(const UbahHarga(id: 'j-1', harga: 4000));

      final data = verify(
        () => network.post(path, data: captureAny(named: 'data')),
      ).captured.single;
      expect(data, {'harga_per_kg': '4000'});
    });
  });
  // … a third test checks that PUT no longer sends harga_per_kg
}

docs.title: Appendix D: a late reply, made deterministic
docs.text:
From ece524b, review defect 7.1 row 4. The use case is stubbed to answer from two Completers, and the test decides the order: the newer reload answers first, the older one last. The cubit must keep the newer price.

test/features/harga/presentation/harga_cubit_test.dart
test('an older reload that answers late never overwrites a newer one',
    () async {
  // Saving a price change reloads after the PUT and again after the POST;
  // the first GET can answer last, with the old price.
  HargaEntity jenis(int harga) => HargaEntity(
        id: 'j-1',
        kodeSampah: 'PLS-001',
        name: 'Plastik PET',
        price: harga,
        // …
      );
  final lama = Completer<Either<NetworkException, List<HargaEntity>>>();
  final baru = Completer<Either<NetworkException, List<HargaEntity>>>();
  final jawaban = [lama, baru];
  when(() => getHarga.execute())
      .thenAnswer((_) => jawaban.removeAt(0).future);

  final pertama = cubit.loadHarga();
  final kedua = cubit.loadHarga();
  baru.complete(Right([jenis(5000)]));
  await kedua;
  lama.complete(Right([jenis(3500)]));
  await pertama;

  final loaded = cubit.state as HargaLoaded;
  expect(loaded.jenisSampahList.single.price, 5000);
});

docs.title: Appendix E: the database as the test oracle
docs.text:
From 31b3ee4. .update() skips the service and the serializer, so only the database can refuse these half-recorded voids. The test is the reason the backend does not mock the database (section 9.2).

apps/ledger/test_setoran_void.py
def test_database_refuses_a_void_without_who_when_and_why(self) -> None:
    setengah: list[dict[str, Any]] = [
        {"status": Transaksi.Status.DIBATALKAN},
        {"status": Transaksi.Status.DIBATALKAN, "dibatalkan_oleh": self.pengelola},
        {"alasan_batal": "x", "dibatalkan_pada": timezone.now()},
    ]
    for fields in setengah:
        with self.subTest(fields=fields), self.assertRaises(IntegrityError):
            with transaction.atomic():
                Transaksi.objects.filter(pk=self.transaksi.pk).update(**fields)

docs.title: Appendix F: a fake backend at the HTTP boundary
docs.text:
From d511208. StubApi is a fake: the real data source, repository, use case and notifier run, and only the server is replaced. The tests cover three cases:

  • the positive case;
  • the negative case (a 409 refusal, whose message is shown as written);
  • a tercatat detail that is not voided.
test/features/transaksi/presentation/providers/transaksi_batal_test.dart
const _path = '/api/v1/transaksi/t1/batalkan';

void main() {
  late StubApi api;
  setUp(() => api = StubApi());

  test('voiding posts the trimmed alasan and returns the voided detail',
      () async {
    api.on('POST', _path, json: _dibatalkan());

    final result = await buildTransaksiNotifier(api)
        .batalkanTransaksi(TransaksiBatalRequest(id: 't1', alasan: ' Dobel '));

    expect(api.last.method, 'POST');
    expect(api.last.path, _path);
    expect(api.last.json, {'alasan': 'Dobel'});
    final detail = result.detail!;
    expect(result.error, isNull);
    expect(detail.isDibatalkan, isTrue);
    expect(detail.alasanBatal, 'Dobel');
    expect(detail.dibatalkanOlehNama, 'Pengelola');
    expect(detail.dibatalkanPada, DateTime.utc(2026, 10, 6, 2, 30).toLocal());
  });

  test('a refused void hands back the backend message as written', () async {
    const pesan =
        'Setoran ini tidak bisa dibatalkan karena sebagian saldonya sudah dicairkan';
    api.on('POST', _path, status: 409, json: {'error': pesan});

    final result = await buildTransaksiNotifier(api)
        .batalkanTransaksi(TransaksiBatalRequest(id: 't1', alasan: 'Dobel'));

docs.title: Following the agreed workflow
docs.text:
The workflow is in the workspace's WORKFLOW.md:

  1. Branch and worktree.
  2. Test-first commits.
  3. A PR.
  4. Review and QA.
  5. Merge after approval.
Step My record (20 Sep – 23 Nov) Branch named after the Linear issue 25 of 33 branches use feature/pil-<n>, and one more PR names its issue in the title. The other 7 are small follow-up fixes with no issue of their own Commits Conventional Commits with the TDD phase, e.g. test(harga): [RED] …, feat(harga): [GREEN] … Pull request All 33 have a Testing section with the commands run and the coverage Review Each finding answered in its own thread, with the fix commit linked Merge 33 of 33 merged, after approval. docs.title: How disciplined tool use helps the team
docs.text:
• Issue ↔ branch ↔ PR. Anyone can go from a Linear issue to its code, or from a PR back to the requirement, and Linear's status stays current without asking.
  • The same branch name in both repos. A feature that spans backend and app, such as feature/pil-451, is found and reviewed as one unit.
  • Phase-tagged commits. A reviewer can check the TDD order from the commit list alone.
  • A Testing section in every PR. The reviewer sees what was run before starting the review.
  • SonarCloud before review. Code smells and coverage gaps are fixed before a teammate spends time on them.
  • Replies in the finding's thread. The reviewer sees each point closed where they raised it.

docs.title: Concepts applied this week
docs.text: # Concept Applied in Evidence 1 End-to-end testing of Flutter web through its semantics tree, with assertions. Flutter web draws on a canvas, so a browser tool can only reach it through the accessibility (semantics) layer. Last week I only explored this: screenshots, nothing asserted. This week the checks wait on labels instead of fixed pauses, assert outcomes, measure where elements sit, and handle labels that Flutter merges into one node. PIL-341 slice 3 (#127), and both QA fixes (#153, #154), at desktop and phone sizes against a local build and backend #127, #153, #154 (E2E tables and screenshots in each description) 2 Client-side routing state, and route parameters as untrusted input. In go_router, push doesn't write to the browser URL unless optionURLReflectsImperativeAPIs is on, so "survives a refresh" means something different for pushed and go routes. And a value read from the URL that ends up in an API path can steer the user's own authenticated requests elsewhere, unless it is validated. #127: a saved draft opens from ?id=, and only a bare id is accepted (OWASP A01, A03). The refresh limitation was documented for the lead dev rather than worked around app-wide. a491758, 7d938f9, Security

    • They surfaced a desktop dialog whose title never reaches the semantics tree. That is recorded as INFO, a likely accessibility gap, rather than marked as a pass.
  • Treating route parameters as input changed a feature I had planned as a convenience (open a draft from its link) into one with a guard. The test sends ../nasabah, d-1/konfirmasi and a space, and asserts that no request is built from them. Learning how push and the URL interact also stopped me from promising a refresh behaviour the app's router doesn't give.

docs.title: Learnings applied this week
docs.text:
# Learning Applied in Evidence 1 Driving OWASP ZAP from a script instead of its GUI. The parts I learned and used:
  • headless -daemon mode and its JSON API;
  • a replacer rule that signs every request in;
  • importing the OpenAPI schema;
  • sending real requests through ZAP's proxy so the active scan attacks real ids and bodies;
  • a scan context that limits the active scan to one feature;
  • the report API.
I also learned where ZAP's alerts stop: it doesn't raise a 500 as an alert, so the scan history has to be read for crashes. A scan of each sub-issue right after it was finished (PIL-428, PIL-435), from one reusable command tools/zap_scan.py, ZAP report, 2 Nov 2 Invariants the database enforces, and locks that serialize writers. The parts I learned and used:
  • a CheckConstraint so a void can't be half-recorded by any write path, proven by attempting one and expecting IntegrityError;
  • a fixed lock order (saldo, then setoran) shared by void and edit;
  • refresh_from_db(from_queryset=select_for_update()) (Django 5.1) to lock and reload in one query;
  • a custom QuerySet method to name a domain rule once;
  • PostgreSQL refusing NUL bytes in text, which explained the crash the scan found.
PIL-428 (#145); the second PIL-451 review round (#137) 2814ae6, d19cb8d, 7c7c1f3, ae850a0

docs.title: How each one changed the work
docs.text:
• Scripted ZAP turned security from a one-off into a routine. Scanning a feature now takes one command and a small file of that feature's real requests, so every finished sub-issue gets a scan, not one scan a sprint.

docs.title: The learning applied this week
docs.text:
Learning Applied in Evidence What a widget may still do after await. The parts I learned and used:
  • PopScope(canPop:) to keep a dialog open while its request is in flight, instead of the default barrierDismissible;
  • reading every notifier before the await, because ref and context may belong to a disposed widget afterwards;
  • applying the server's outcome whether or not the widget is still mounted, since the server state changed either way;
  • ModalRoute.of(context).isCurrent to tell "this dialog is closing" from "this dialog is on top", so a late pop can't close the page underneath;
  • ProviderScope.containerOf and container.exists, to reload only the providers a screen already built.
The PIL-428 Hapus dialog (#193), after Heraldo's and Scallss's findings 472c506, be7b6d0, and the tests in 17125d0

docs.title: How it changed the work
docs.text:
• It found a bug nobody had reported. Knowing that a dialog animates closed for a few frames led to the third test: an answer arriving during that animation closed the Riwayat page. The fix is one condition on the route.
  • It made the tests possible. Staging an in-flight request needs a stub API with a set latency and tester.pump with exact durations. Without those, the race can't be reproduced, so a fix can't be proven.
  • It keeps the app from doing extra work. container.exists means a void reloads the dashboard only if the pengurus already opened it, instead of building every screen and sending their requests.

  2. Subresource Integrity: how a browser verifies a CDN file, and how to check the hashes yourself.

docs.title: Learnings applied this week
docs.text:
# Learning Applied in Evidence 1 A test that checks the architecture, not the behaviour. The parts I learned and used:
  • ast.parse and ast.walk to find every .filter() / .exclude() call in apps/;
  • reading a call's keywords to spot a hand-written status filter, which a text search would confuse with a comment;
  • excluding the one module that owns the rule, and the tests;
  • proving the test isn't vacuous by running it on staging, where it failed on exactly one line.
#176: "counted setoran" can only be read through tercatat() b10fffa, 8d1a931 2 Subresource Integrity (SRI). The parts I learned and used:
  • an integrity="sha384-…" attribute makes the browser refuse a CDN file whose bytes changed;
  • computing the hash yourself from the exact bytes the CDN serves, base64 of the SHA-384 digest;
  • crossorigin="anonymous" only works if the CDN sends Access-Control-Allow-Origin;
  • a pinned version and its hashes must move together, or the page goes blank in a browser while every server-side test passes.
Reviewing Gabriel's #174, which closes the 26 Oct ZAP finding 3 Review of #174, the non-blocking suggestion

docs.title: How each one changed the work
docs.text:
• The fitness function turned a convention into a check. Two weeks ago the rule got a name; this week a test makes sure nothing bypasses it. That's the difference between a reviewer remembering it, as Heraldo did on #167, and CI failing when it's forgotten.
  • Knowing how SRI works made the review concrete. Instead of trusting the PR's screenshots, I could recompute the hashes, check the CDN's CORS header, and then break the version on purpose. That gave a real failure mode, a blank docs page with green tests, and a fix for it.

That's operating knowledge, not a new technique, so it isn't claimed.

docs.title: Learnings applied this week
docs.text:
# Learning Applied in Evidence 1 A pushed page that answers its caller. The parts I learned and used:
  • context.push<bool>(route) returns a Future that completes with whatever the page pops, so the caller decides what to do next;
  • context.pop(true) on success, and a plain back resolving to null, so "applied" and "went back" are told apart;
  • checking context.mounted before acting on the result, since the page may be gone by then;
  • a toast raised after navigation needs a navigator that outlives the popped page: here the app's rootNavigatorKey, which the test router has to use too.
#276: Bank sampah saya reloads only when an application was sent 9c7ecac, b34db8b 2 ZAP's site tree and the active scan. The parts I learned and used:
  • the active scan attacks nodes of ZAP's site tree, and looking up a URL finds the GET node;
  • so a path that only ever saw POST answers "URL Not Found in the Scan Tree", even though ZAP recorded the request;
  • the fix: find the recorded message for that method and URL, and start the scan with its method and body;
  • signing the scan in as a different role (a nasabah) by passing that account's token to the bearer rule.
The 23 Nov scan of PIL-539: POST /onboarding/nasabah, the endpoint the feature depends on ZAP report, 23 Nov, tools/zap_scan.py

docs.title: How each one changed the work
docs.text:
• The route result removed a whole class of bugs. Without it, the list would either reload every time it's shown, or need a callback passed into the form. With push<bool>, the list reloads exactly when an application was sent, and the test can assert both cases: [true] and [].
  • Knowing why the scan skipped the endpoint turned a clean-looking report into a real one. The first run looked fine but had never attacked the one path that mattered. After the fix, 224 attacks hit it, and the 17 Nov limit on DELETE /device-tokens/ is closed for every later scan.

docs.title: AI Literacy
docs.text:
Competency level: 3

AI used critically:

  • Its plans were checked against the code before being acted on.
  • Twice it caught and said that its own premise or check was wrong.
  • When I asked whether Playwright meant no more manual testing, it said where its own script fell short instead of agreeing.
  • Candidate review findings were measured before they were posted, and two were dropped.

The decisions that affect the team (shared CI, a teammate's code, how to restructure PRs, whether E2E runs in CI) were put to me before anything changed.

Evidence for this week:

  • AI prompt history, 11–12 Oct: 10 prompts with every tool call the agent made between them, built from the session transcript. Emails, home-folder paths and tokens are removed. The earlier part of the same session (7–9 Oct) is published with Sprint 1 Week 3.

docs.title: How AI was used this week
docs.text:
• Tool: Claude Code as an agent in VS Code across pilah-be, pilah-mobile and pilah-docs, Linear through Composio, GitHub through gh, and the SonarQube CLI and the SonarCloud API for coverage.
  • Guardrails:
    • the workspace skills (ship, tdd, ask-for-review);
    • CI's own commands, run locally before every push;
    • rules kept in memory: phase-tagged commits, replying inside review threads, never merging base branches into stacked ones without asking.
    • New this week: cover 100% of the code, generated code included; back every web UI PR with Playwright E2E checks run through Flutter's semantics tree (13 Oct).
  • My role:
    • picking PIL-331;
    • deciding its open points (a fixed "kg" until PIL-305, scheduled prices shown and marked, the entry point on the harga card);
    • setting the coverage rule;
    • choosing how to land the CI fix and how to stack the PRs;
    • keeping the Playwright checks local rather than adding a CI job.

docs.title: Where verification changed the outcome
docs.text: Situation What happened 11 Oct: It offered "a button in the expanded card" as the entry point for the price history, and I picked it On reading the page, it found the card wasn't expandable: tapping it opens the edit sheet. It told me its option had been based on a wrong premise, then put the button in the card's info column, the closest match to my choice. 11 Oct: SonarCloud showed #62/#73 a few lines short of 100%, all in generated code I said to always cover 100%, generated or not. Rather than add an exclusion, it traced why lcov skipped the file, and found that the graph CI builds would crash the app on launch. 11 Oct: Its first check of that crash passed It noticed build_runner had skipped regenerating the file and left the hand-edited copy in place, so the check proved nothing. It deleted the file, regenerated it, and only then reported the crash, with the exact error. 11 Oct: The crash fix touched the team's CI and a teammate's code It stopped and asked how to land it (separate PR, inside #62, or just report it) before changing shared workflows. 12 Oct: Tristan's 8 review notes Each was checked against the code before anything changed. All 8 held up. One (the Sonar exclusion) showed that staging had moved since the branch was cut. 12 Oct: "Can we use stacked PRs for #79 and #92?" #92 was already stacked, so the question was ambiguous. It also checked its saved rule against merging a base branch into a stacked one. It asked which stack shape I meant, then used a revert plus cherry-pick -x, not a force-push, so last week's evidence links stay valid. 12 Oct: #74's crash fix became redundant when Tristan's #71 landed the same change It took staging's version in the conflict and rewrote the PR around what was still new, instead of keeping a duplicate fix. 13 Oct: I asked whether Playwright meant I wouldn't need manual tests It answered "partly". It said its own run had only taken screenshots and asserted nothing, so it was visual QA and not a test suite, and that its fixed pauses were the fragile style I hoped to avoid. Then it listed what automation can't cover. Screenshots below. 13 Oct: "Do it for future commits and PRs" It saved the rule, then asked where the checks should run instead of deciding itself. Its recommendation was a CI job with the API stubbed, which would touch the team's pipeline. I chose local only, and it rewrote the rule to match. It also noticed that an earlier rule (100% coverage) had been saved without an index entry, so future sessions would not have loaded it, and fixed that. 16 Oct: Reviewing Ghani's #104 Three candidate findings were checked before posting. The CI coverage change was measured with and without tests/ (99% either way), so it was dropped. The alternative to the spreadsheet escaping was tried and turned out worse, so it was dropped too. The performance suggestion went in only after a benchmark showed the same result from fewer queries.

docs.title: Example: covering generated code turned up a crash
docs.text:
The obvious response to "97.4% on SonarCloud, the gap is generated code" is an exclusion line in sonar.yml. Instead:

  1. The cause. It checked why the file was missing from lcov: the generator writes // coverage:ignore-file.
  2. The proposal. It proposed resolving every registration in a test.
  3. The finding. Building that test exposed that the graph CI generates asks for a bool nobody registers. Every CI-built app would crash on launch, and nobody had noticed, because flutter run uses the hand-edited copy.
  4. My decision. Before touching shared CI and a teammate's bloc, it laid out three ways to land the fix and waited for my choice.

The result is pilah-mobile #74, which keeps that class of crash out of future builds.

docs.title: Example: Playwright is not a replacement for manual testing
docs.text:
On 13 Oct the agent ran PIL-341 slice 2 in a local web build with Playwright and took desktop and phone screenshots. That run caught a dialog with square corners, which the widget tests had missed. I had only just heard of Playwright, so I asked about it before relying on it.

1. "So I don't need manual tests?" It didn't just agree. It said what its own run had been: a script that clicked through the flow and saved screenshots, with nothing asserted, so scripted visual QA, not automated testing. It confirmed my point about auto-waiting, with a catch for Flutter: Flutter web draws on a canvas, which is why its script had fallen back on fixed waitForTimeout pauses, the fragile style I wanted to avoid.

2. "Can't we just use the semantics tree?" It explained that, on the web, the semantics tree is the accessibility layer, and why it is off by default. It gave two ways to turn it on, a flag in the app for E2E builds only or a click in the test, and recommended stable Semantics(identifier:) selectors over matching visible text.

3. "Do it for future commits and PRs." It saved the rule, then asked where the tests should run. It recommended CI with the API stubbed, and I chose local only. The saved rule says that for every web UI PR the scripts walk the flow and assert the result, wait on labels instead of fixed pauses, and save desktop and phone screenshots for the PR description. It also promised to rerun the slice 2 flows the new way and add the results to #84.

What changed. I came in thinking a new tool would replace a practice. I left with a rule that says what the tool checks and what it doesn't, and that rule is now in the agent's memory for every later web PR. This is the same pattern as earlier weeks' rules (phase-tagged commits, 100% coverage), kept as notes that change how later sessions work.

docs.text:
• Covered locally: they are covered by a test (eb9b20f), and diff-cover counts 100% of #73's 141 changed lines with the generator's marker dropped.

The section below is what #74 changes.

docs.title: Raising the bar: measuring generated code
docs.text:
SonarCloud put #62 at 97.4% and #73 at 96.2%. Every uncovered line was a registration in the generated lib/services/di.config.dart. Generated or not, it is code that ships, so I covered it rather than explaining it away.

Why it was invisible:

  • injectable_generator marks the file // coverage:ignore-file, so lcov leaves it out.
  • sonar.yml also excluded it from analysis.

What covering it found: the graph CI builds could not create AuthenticationBloc, because it asked dependency injection for a bool nobody registers. app.dart creates that bloc at start-up, so CI-built apps would crash on launch. Local flutter run hid it, because it uses a hand-maintained copy of the file.

The fix, pilah-mobile #74:

  • A full-graph test. di_graph_test builds every registration in dev and prod, and fails when a new registration is missing from its list.
  • Coverage in CI. CI and SonarCloud now measure the file: the marker is dropped after code generation (941f24d), and the Sonar exclusion is removed, as Tristan asked in review (26fcf40).
  • Result: every executable line of the file is covered.
  • Docs. AGENTS.md now says how the generated file is committed and tested.

The crash itself reached staging first through Tristan's #71 (the same @ignoreParam fix), so #74 keeps staging's version of the bloc.

docs.title: Programming
docs.text:
Competency level: 3

Standard principles applied and shown in this week's code:

  • SOLID: single responsibility, open/closed and dependency inversion. See SOLID in this week's code.
  • One rule for a price version's status, the same order the setoran lookup uses.
  • Money kept exact on mobile, without double.
  • A stale-response guard against a list-reload race.
  • Seed data written through the one approved write path.

Each item names the design issue it addresses, the pattern or principle used, and its type. The GoF design patterns (Singleton, Adapter, Observer, and loosely Command) have their own section. Three of the issues were in my own code and were found in Tristan's review; the table says which.

docs.title: Design issues and the patterns that address them
docs.text:
Code Design issue Pattern / principle Type Origin Version status Two readers of the price history (the history screen and the setoran price lookup) that must never disagree; a status that could depend on where a page breaks Consistent ordering invariant: both use the same order (start, then id), and the status is computed over the whole history before pagination Principle (domain invariant) Designed in (PIL-331) Money Primitive obsession with floating point for money: 3333.99 read through double and toInt() showed a price that was never stored Money in minor units: the price is an integer number of sen, parsed from the decimal string without a float Technique (minor units) Defect in my code, Tristan's review of #73 Stale response Race condition on out-of-order async responses: an older reload answering last overwrote the newer price Request sequence token ("latest request wins"): each reload is numbered and a stale answer is dropped Technique (concurrency) Defect in my code, Tristan's review of #62 Seed data Bypassing the domain's write path: the seed wrote price versions itself and priced old setoran at today's rate, so its rules could drift from the app's (BR-03) Service layer as the single write path: every price goes through catat_harga, and each setoran is priced at its own date Architectural (PoEAA Service Layer) Defect in my code, Tristan's review of #79 (and) Single responsibility A fat view mixing HTTP with business rules SRP: the rule is a plain port function; the serializer shapes, the view wires Principle (SOLID) Designed in (PIL-331) Open/closed Changing PIL-304's working POST action to add a read OCP: @ubah_harga.mapping.get adds the read without editing the action Principle (SOLID) Designed in (PIL-331) Dependency inversion A cubit coupled to the HTTP client, untestable without a server Repository pattern + use case, injected (DIP): the cubit sees only the use case and the HargaRepository interface Principle (SOLID) + Architectural (Repository) Designed in (PIL-331) Don't repeat yourself Duplicated code: my first version copied another page's private date formatter Extract function into one tested shared helper Principle (DRY) Caught in my own [REFACTOR] commit

Type says what kind of solution each one is. Only part of it is a GoF design pattern (creational, structural, behavioural). The rest are principles (SOLID, DRY), architectural patterns from Fowler's Patterns of Enterprise Application Architecture (PoEAA), or plain techniques. The GoF patterns that do appear in this week's code are listed in GoF design patterns in this week's code.

docs.title: PIL-331 — the price history, and the review round (10–12 Oct)
One rule for a version's status — 601b948, f0b6b0d
docs.text:
The history marks each version terjadwal, berlaku, sebelumnya or digantikan. The rule uses the same order as harga_berlaku (start, then id), so the screen can never disagree with the price a setoran uses. It runs over the whole history before pagination, so a page break can't change a status:

apps/waste_catalog/api.py
def susun_riwayat_harga(jenis: JenisSampah, pada: datetime) -> list[VersiHarga]:
    riwayat: list[VersiHarga] = []
    di_atasnya: HargaSampah | None = None
    sudah_ada_yang_berlaku = False
    for versi in jenis.riwayat_harga.select_related("dibuat_oleh").order_by(
        "-berlaku_mulai", "-id"
    ):
        status: StatusVersi
        if di_atasnya is not None and versi.berlaku_mulai == di_atasnya.berlaku_mulai:
            status = "digantikan"
        elif versi.berlaku_mulai > pada:
            status = "terjadwal"
        elif not sudah_ada_yang_berlaku:
            status = "berlaku"
            sudah_ada_yang_berlaku = True
        else:
            status = "sebelumnya"
        riwayat.append(VersiHarga(versi, status))
        di_atasnya = versi
    return riwayat

digantikan exists because correcting a scheduled price is a new version with the same start (PIL-304's append-only rule). Without it, the history would show two scheduled prices for one day.

Design issue: two readers of one history that must agree. Pattern: a consistent ordering invariant, computed before pagination. Origin: designed in.

docs.title: Money kept exact — 4226ca5
docs.text:
Design issue: primitive obsession with floating point for money. Pattern: money in minor units (integer sen). Origin: a defect in my code, found in Tristan's review.

Tristan's review found that the mobile model read 3333.99 through double and toInt(), showing a price that was never stored. A version now holds its price in sen, and the backend's decimal string is cut, not parsed as a float, so no binary rounding can creep in:

lib/features/harga/data/models/versi_harga_model.dart
int _keSen(String angka) {
  final bagian = angka.split('.');
  final sen = (bagian.length > 1 ? bagian[1] : '').padRight(2, '0');
  return (int.tryParse(bagian[0]) ?? 0) * 100 +
      (int.tryParse(sen.substring(0, 2)) ?? 0);
}

docs.title: A stale response can't win — bd21f70
docs.text:
Design issue: a race condition on out-of-order async responses. Pattern: a request sequence token, so the latest request wins. Origin: a defect in my code, found in Tristan's review.

Saving a price change reloads the list twice: after the PUT and after the price POST. If the first GET answered last, the old price came back. Each reload is now numbered, and an answer is dropped once a newer reload has started:

lib/features/harga/presentation/cubit/harga_cubit.dart
  Future<void> loadHarga({bool silent = false}) async {
    final permintaan = ++_permintaanTerakhir;
    if (!silent || state is! HargaLoaded) emit(HargaLoading());
    final result = await getHargaUseCase.execute();
    // Reload yang lebih baru sudah berjalan: jawaban ini sudah usang.
    if (permintaan != _permintaanTerakhir) return;
    ...

docs.title: Seed data follows the same rules — f67a84f, dc29a68
docs.text:
Design issue: bypassing the domain's write path, so the seed's rules could drift from the app's. Pattern: the service layer as the single write path. Origin: a defect in my code, found in Tristan's review.

The seed command wrote price versions itself and priced historical setoran at today's rate, so rerunning it after a price change rewrote old totals. It now writes through catat_harga, the one approved write path in AGENTS.md, and prices each setoran at its own date (BR-03).

docs.title: GoF design patterns in this week's code
docs.text:
All four are in PIL-331's mobile side (pilah-mobile #73), in code I wrote. They follow the app's existing Clean Architecture layout.

Category Pattern Where What it does here Creational Singleton (container-managed) GetRiwayatHargaUseCase (@lazySingleton), 35e908a The injection container builds one shared instance on first use. A variant of GoF Singleton: the container, not the class, guarantees the single instance, so a test can still pass a stub. Structural Adapter HargaRepositoryImpl.getRiwayatHarga, 7077e55 Adapts the data source, which throws exceptions and reads paginated JSON, to the domain's HargaRepository interface, which returns Either<NetworkException, List<VersiHarga>>. Behavioural Observer RiwayatHargaCubit → BlocBuilder on RiwayatHargaPage, 35e908a, cd41645 The cubit emits a new state, and every subscribed widget rebuilds. The cubit doesn't know who is listening. Behavioural Command (loosely) GetRiwayatHargaUseCase implements UseCase<List<VersiHarga>, String>, 35e908a Each use case is one request wrapped in an object behind a uniform interface, so the cubit calls it without knowing how the request is carried out. There is no undo or queue, so it is only loosely Command. lib/features/harga/data/repositories/harga_repository_impl.dart (Adapter)
  Future<Either<NetworkException, List<VersiHarga>>> getRiwayatHarga(
      String id) async {
    try {
      return Right(await remoteDataSource.getRiwayatHarga(id));
    } on Exception catch (e) {
      return Left(NetworkException.handleException(e));
    }
  }
lib/features/harga/presentation/pages/riwayat_harga_page.dart (Observer)
      body: BlocBuilder<RiwayatHargaCubit, RiwayatHargaState>(

Two names to avoid mixing up. Python's @ubah_harga.mapping.get on the backend is a language decorator, not the GoF Decorator pattern. Repository and Service Layer are PoEAA patterns, not GoF.

docs.title: Single responsibility — 601b948
docs.text:
The status rule is a plain function in the catalog's port (above), with no HTTP in it. The serializer only shapes a row, and the view only wires the lookup to pagination:

apps/waste_catalog/views.py
    @ubah_harga.mapping.get
    def riwayat_harga(self, request: Request, pk: str | None = None) -> Response:
        page = self.paginate_queryset(susun_riwayat_harga(self.get_object(), timezone.now()))
        return self.get_paginated_response(VersiHargaSerializer(page, many=True).data)

@ubah_harga.mapping.get adds the read on the same path as PIL-304's POST, without changing that action: open/closed.

docs.title: Don't repeat yourself — 2eb1bea
docs.text:
Design issue: duplicated code. Pattern: extract function into a shared, tested helper. Origin: my own first version, fixed in its [REFACTOR] commit.

The history screen first copied the pencairan revision page's private date-and-time formatter. The refactor moved it to one tested formatTanggalJamId, and both screens call it.

docs.title: Security
docs.text:
Competency level: 3

A dynamic security scan of the backend with Metasploit Framework 6.5.3, explained, with a test-first patch plan: Security scan report. The scan was run against my own local instance and cross-checked against python manage.py check --deploy.

Alongside the scan, this week's new code guards A01 Broken Access Control on the new price-history endpoint (named in its commit and tested), with two more OWASP behaviours (A08, A09) tested but not named in their commits.

docs.title: Security scan (level 3)
docs.text:
Ran Metasploit against the backend on a local instance (manage.py runserver, seeded test DB; staging and production were not touched). Method: Metasploit auxiliary/scanner/http/* for fingerprinting, headers, directory enumeration and method discovery, then curl to verify, then check --deploy as a static cross-check.

Explained — why a generic exploit framework finds little here. Metasploit exploits known vulnerabilities in known software. PILAH's backend is a bespoke Django/DRF app, so no exploit module matches it; its scanners confirmed there is no exploitable off-the-shelf service, and the findings that matter are application- and configuration-level. That clean result is itself a finding.

Findings (full detail and evidence in the report):

# Finding OWASP Severity Scope 1 /api/schema/ and /api/docs/ served without authentication — full API contract disclosed A01 / A05 Medium prod + dev 2 HSTS not configured (SECURE_HSTS_SECONDS unset; security.W004) A05 Low–Med prod 3 App-layer HTTPS redirect not enforced (security.W008) A05 Low prod 4 No Content-Security-Policy / Permissions-Policy A05 Low prod + dev 5 Server banner leaks framework and Python version A05 Info dev 6 DEBUG=true error pages leak the URL configuration A05 Med if deployed dev-only

Patch plan (priority first), each a test-first change naming its OWASP category:

  1. Restrict the schema/docs behind IsAdminUser (or IsAuthenticated), so an unauthenticated request gets 401/403.
  2. Enable HSTS (SECURE_HSTS_SECONDS, include-subdomains, preload) guarded by not DEBUG.
  3. SECURE_SSL_REDIRECT = not DEBUG, using the proxy header already set.
  4. Add a minimal CSP / Permissions-Policy, scoped to the API and the Swagger page.
  5. Suppress the Server banner at the gunicorn/middleware layer.
  6. A CI/start-up guard that a production build cannot boot with DEBUG=true.

What held up. Every /api/v1/* endpoint returns 401 without a token; /admin/ redirects to login; X-Frame-Options: DENY, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, Referrer-Policy and COOP are all present; /.env is 404, there is no path traversal, and only safe HTTP methods are allowed.
