docs.title: A01 · Broken Access Control
docs.text:
PIL-331's GET /jenis-sampah/{id}/harga exposes every past price of a jenis — business data — so I checked it against the two ways it could leak:

apps/waste_catalog/test_riwayat_harga.py (excerpt)
        self.auth_as(pengurus_lain)
        self.assertEqual(self.riwayat(jenis["id"]).status_code, 404)
        self.auth_as(nasabah)
        self.assertEqual(self.riwayat(jenis["id"]).status_code, 403)

The action reuses the viewset's bank-scoped get_object and IsActivePengelola, so the test passed when written. I proved it guards something by swapping in an unscoped lookup, seeing another bank read the prices and the test fail, then restoring the code. The commit names the category: "(OWASP A01, BR-01)".

docs.title: Also tested this week
docs.text:
• A08, data integrity. Each seeded setoran must keep the price of its own date (BR-03). The red test recorded a price change taking effect now and reran the seed; a historical snapshot went from 3,500 to 99,999. The fix prices each setoran at its stored tanggal.
  • A09, audit trail. The price history makes dibuat_oleh readable to the pengurus (null for prices backfilled by the migration).

docs.title: Test Driven Development
docs.text:
Competency level: 4

Level 3 met: PIL-331 was built test-first on both sides, with [RED]/[GREEN]/[REFACTOR] in every commit subject. Every review finding Tristan raised was fixed the same way, with a failing test first. Changed lines are 100% covered in every MR, generated code included, and each behaviour is tested with positive, negative and corner cases.

Level 4: advanced testing methods in the commits:

  • Mocks, stubs and fakes for isolation: mocktail, Completers that decide which request answers first, and a fake backend at the HTTP boundary.
  • Mutation checks: tests that passed when written were proven to guard their code by breaking the code and watching them fail.
  • Full-graph test: a test builds the app's whole generated dependency graph in both environments.

docs.text:
• Controlled ordering with Completers (#62). The race test hands the cubit two pending requests, answers the newer one first and the older one last, and checks the newer price stays.
  • A fake backend at the HTTP boundary (#73). StubApi replaces Dio's adapter, so the real data source, repository, use case and cubit run against canned responses. Failures are injected at the transport level (api.fail).
  • Mutation checks (#92, #73).

docs.title: Team Development Management
docs.text:
Competency level: 3

Two detailed reviews of teammates' merge requests, each with feasible improvement suggestions:

  • Gabriel's PIL-354 (pilah-be #97, 13 Oct). Two inline suggestions. Gabriel took both, and built a source-level guard on the first one.
  • Ghani's PIL-248 (pilah-be #104, 16 Oct). One performance suggestion, measured against the current code before posting: same result, 5 queries down to 3, 91 ms down to 34 ms.

The other side of reviewing is here too:

  • Tristan's 8 findings on my merge requests: each verified against the code, fixed test-first and answered in its thread.
  • A crash that every CI-built app would have hit on launch, found and raised.

docs.title: Review given: Gabriel's pilah-be #97 (PIL-354), 13 Oct
docs.text:
PIL-354 fixes CORS for the web dashboard. It allows the Idempotency-Key request header and exposes Content-Disposition, so browser downloads get their filename. Gabriel added a registry of custom headers in shared_kernel/http_headers.py, which both the CORS settings and the views are meant to read from.

Review (approved) · inline: registry constant, test that can't fail

Before commenting, I checked that the registry covers everything that crosses origins. Idempotency-Key is the only custom header the API reads, and pilah-mobile sends nothing outside the default allowed set. Content-Disposition is written in four places, and the one exposed header covers all of them, including the draft-pencairan export that my PIL-341 web work uses.

Suggestion Why it matters What Gabriel did (14 Oct) Use the registry constant where the header is written. The docstring says the CORS setting and the code share one value. That held for Idempotency-Key, but the four writes of Content-Disposition still spelled the name out (ledger/views.py L151, L372, L384, nasabah/home.py L243) It makes the docstring's claim true for both lists, and gives the next response header an obvious place to be registered All four writes switched to CONTENT_DISPOSITION (e50d237). He went further, with a guard that fails if a registered name is spelled out anywhere else (67db001). It went red on exactly those four lines before the fix (reply) A test assertion that cannot fail. django-cors-headers never echoes requested headers back, so assertNotIn("x-pilah-tidak-terdaftar", allowed) passes whatever the settings are. Only the next assertion, no *, guards anything A test should say what it actually protects Renamed as suggested, and the vacuous assertion became set equality against the allowed list, which also catches one stray header (0213cdf). He checked it fails both ways (reply)

Both suggestions were marked as nits, so they didn't block the approval. #97 merged with both changes in.

docs.title: Review given: Ghani's pilah-be #104 (PIL-248), 16 Oct
docs.text:
PIL-248 adds an operational summary to the activity feed (count, weight, deposits, payouts, period balance) and a combined Excel export of deposits and payouts. Ghani asked me and Heraldo to review. Tristan had already flagged two issues (member filter, consistent snapshot) and Gabriel one (formulas without cached values), so I reviewed the head after those fixes, without repeating their points.

Review · inline: database aggregates for the summary

The suggestion: compute the summary in the database. The feed now builds the summary on every page request, and it streams every total_nilai and nominal in the filtered range into Python to round each one down. With periode=semua that is the bank's whole history, read again on every scroll. Rounding down is Floor for non-negative amounts, so the same per-event rounding fits in Sum(Floor(...)), with the counts folded into the same queries. Before posting it, I ran a throwaway benchmark against the PR's own function (20,000 setoran and 5,000 pencairan, SQLite, best of 5):

Queries Time Result Current operational_summary 5 91 ms — Database aggregates 3 34 ms identical dict

The comment says what wasn't measured (PostgreSQL), and when Floor would differ from the current rounding: negative amounts, which a CheckConstraint could rule out. It also points out that the feed parses its filters twice, in two calls that could drift apart.

Checked and not raised. The review also records what I checked and why it isn't a finding:

  • Formula escaping. The leading apostrophe is visible in Excel. A typed text cell would hide it, but re-saving the file as CSV would then write the raw =... back out, so the current fix is the safer one.
  • The CI coverage change. I measured the coverage gate with and without tests/: 99% either way. The 80% gate already counted the test modules under apps/, so the change doesn't loosen it.
  • The durable transaction. It can't fire in production, because nothing wraps requests in atomic.

Gabriel's thread was still open, so the review is a comment, not an approval yet.

docs.title: Review received and answered: Tristan on #79, #62, #73 and #74, 11–12 Oct
docs.text:
Tristan reviewed four of my MRs on 11 Oct (and approved #92). I checked every finding against the code before changing anything; all 8 held up. Each fix went in test-first, and each thread got a reply with the commits.

MR Finding What I did Reply #79 The seed writes price versions itself, outside the approved write paths Routed it through catat_harga (dc29a68) thread #79 Rerunning the seed reprices historical setoran at today's rate Red test showed 3,500 becoming 99,999. Each setoran is now priced at its own date (857735b → f67a84f) thread #79 The filter allow-list is outside PIL-304 Reverted here and re-applied unchanged as #96, stacked on #92 thread #62 A partial save is reported as a failure The sheet now says the other fields saved and the price didn't, and stays open; retrying is safe (5a80375 → f1ea8d9) thread #62 An older list reload can overwrite a newer one Reloads are numbered and a stale answer is dropped (ece524b → bd21f70) thread #73 toInt() drops a price's sen Prices are held in sen and parsed without double (de18bfc → 4226ca5) thread #73 Versions past the first 100 disappear The history follows next to the last page (9ad13dd → 510f02a) thread #74 The Sonar exclusion still hides the DI graph, plus a merge conflict Removed the exclusion (26fcf40). Merged staging and took Tristan's identical bloc fix from #71 thread, comment

Two findings had a cheaper but worse fix that I chose not to take, and the replies say why:

  • #62, the partial save. Making the two writes atomic would need a backend endpoint that takes both. The API keeps the price separate on purpose, so that every change is a version. So the fix makes the state explicit and the retry safe instead.
  • #79, the filter split. Force-pushing #79 would have broken last week's evidence links. A revert plus cherry-pick -x keeps the history intact.

docs.title: Raising a team-wide problem: CI-built apps would crash on launch, 11 Oct
docs.text:
While covering the generated dependency graph, I found that the graph CI and CD build could not create AuthenticationBloc, which app.dart creates at start-up. It had been that way since PIL-334. The next staging APK or web build would have crashed on launch; local flutter run hid it.

  • Reproduced first. I regenerated the graph, built the bloc from it in a test, and got the exact error before reporting it.
  • Asked before touching shared code. The fix touches the team's CI and a teammate's code, so I asked how to land it, then opened #74 against staging.
  • Outcome. The same one-line fix also reached staging through Tristan's #71. #74 kept what was still new: a test that builds every registration, so this class of crash fails CI instead of the app.

docs.title: IR Part B Sprint 2 Week 2
docs.text:
Evidence for the individual review (IR), organised by competency. Each page states the competency level and the dated evidence behind it, with commit and PR links.

Part B — Hardskills: Best Practice, for Sprint 2 week 2.

What this page covers

Sprint 2 Week 1 claims work up to 16 Oct. This page covers 17–23 Oct, and mainly the two QA fixes on pencairan (21 Oct):

  • PIL-374, pilah-mobile #153: a general Nominal above a nasabah's saldo now warns and asks for confirmation, without blocking.

docs.title: Example: a QA "Fail" that was a rule, not a bug
docs.text:
QA marked draft pencairan "Fail – High": a nasabah had about Rp 19 rb saldo, the tester set Jumlah Pencairan to Rp 50.000 and a Rp 3.000 potongan, and the draft still paid out. My first guess was a missing balance check, and I suggested a warning.

1. "Check on this finding." It did not start with my fix. It found that the tester had used the general Nominal, which is a ceiling: anyone with less saldo is paid their whole saldo. Two tests pin that on purpose, and a per-nasabah nominal above saldo is already blocked. So the bug was that nothing told the Pengurus. It agreed with a warning, and argued against blocking with the team's own PIL-301 note.

2. The team decided, then I refined it. The proposal went to the team as a doc. We chose to warn without blocking, and Pascal asked for a confirmation dialog on Terapkan. While it built that, I added a correction: list the affected nasabah when there is more than one. It took the correction mid-task and went on test-first.

3. "Even 1, and state the name." After seeing the one-nasabah dialog, I asked for the list every time. It changed the test first (red), then the code, and reran the Playwright checks for both one and two nasabah.

What changed. A "Fail – High" that looked like a missing validation became a small UX fix the team agreed on: pilah-mobile #153 (PIL-374). It shows a note under the Nominal, a confirmation that names every affected nasabah and their saldo, and a line on each capped card. The rule the tests pin stayed as it was, and the reason behind it is now on screen.

docs.title: An issue found and fixed before review

On 21 Oct, after the confirmation dialog and its list went into #153, SonarCloud reported:

Rule Severity Where Opened Closed dart:S3776 Cognitive Complexity Critical _terapkan in draft_editor_page.dart: "reduce its Cognitive Complexity from 17 to the 15 allowed" 21 Oct, 20:30 WIB 21 Oct, 21:24 WIB, fixed

docs.title: From QA finding to merged fix
docs.text:
Both fixes went through the same steps, each recorded where the team can see it:

  1. Checked before it was called a bug. I traced each QA finding to the code. The first was a deliberate ceiling with no explanation on screen. The second was a deliberate lock that looked unlocked.
  2. The decision went to the team. For PIL-374 I wrote a short proposal: warn, block, or warn and confirm. The team chose to warn without blocking, and Pascal suggested the confirmation.
  3. Tracked in Linear. I opened PIL-374 under CPBI-22 and PIL-375 as a sub-issue of PIL-327, where the lock came from. Each has the cause, the tasks, the tests, and a note for QA. When a scope changed, I updated the issue the same day.

  5. Review, then merge. I requested Pascal and Aldo through the team's ask-for-review skill (GitHub reviewer plus a Discord ping). I merged only after approval, with green CI and SonarCloud.

docs.title: Programming
docs.text:
Competency level: 3

Standard principles applied and shown in the two QA fixes:

  • SOLID: single responsibility and open/closed. See SOLID in this week's code.
  • Information Expert: the "is this nasabah short?" rule lives next to the ceiling it describes.
  • A derived flag computed from state, never stored.
  • Command–query separation, reached through an Extract Method refactor.
  • One lock flag driving every locked field through the same enabled convention.

Each item names the design issue it addresses, the pattern or principle used, its type and where the issue came from.

docs.title: Design issues and the patterns that address them
docs.text:
Code Design issue Pattern / principle Type Origin melebihiSaldo Duplicated business rule: the screen needs "is this nasabah short?", and recomputing it in the UI would duplicate hitung's ceiling, so the two could drift Information Expert (GRASP): JumlahUmum, which owns the ceiling, answers the question Principle (GRASP) Designed in (PIL-374) dibatasiSaldo Stale state: a stored "capped" flag would go out of date the moment the pengurus types a nominal Derived state / single source of truth: a query method computes it from the applied Nominal and the item Technique (derived state) Designed in (PIL-374) _setujuSaldoKurang Long method mixing a question with an action: _terapkan both built the confirmation and applied the settings, at cognitive complexity 17 of 15 Extract Method (Fowler) towards command–query separation: one method answers "may this be applied?", the other applies Refactoring + principle Tool finding on my own code (SonarCloud S3776) isi: slot Changing a shared dialog to add one caller's content Open/closed via composition: showPencairanKonfirmasi already takes an isi widget, so the list is passed in and the dialog is unchanged Principle (SOLID OCP) Designed in (PIL-374) enabled Inconsistent locked state: one flag (_terkunci) disabled the Nominal, while the Tanggal only ignored taps and still looked active One flag through a uniform interface: the field takes enabled, as Material's own fields do, and _terkunci drives both Technique (consistency) QA finding (PIL-375)

The GoF patterns these changes sit on are listed in GoF design patterns in this week's code.

docs.title: The rule lives with the ceiling — 0511e1b
docs.text:
hitung already caps a fixed rupiah at the saldo. The question "will this nasabah get less than asked?" is the same rule seen from the other side, so it sits right below it, in the same class:

lib/features/draft_pencairan/domain/model/draft_pencairan.dart
int hitung(int saldo) {
  switch (jenis) {
    case JumlahJenis.persen:
      return _persenDari(saldo, nilai);
    case JumlahJenis.rupiah:
      final tetap = nilai.floor();
      return tetap < saldo ? tetap : saldo;
  }
}

/// Whether a nasabah with [saldo] gets less than this asks for: a fixed
/// rupiah above their saldo, so [hitung] pays them their whole saldo.
bool melebihiSaldo(int saldo) =>
    jenis == JumlahJenis.rupiah && valid && nilai.floor() > saldo;

The note under the field, the confirmation, its list and each card's line all ask melebihiSaldo. None of them compares amounts itself. The reviewer checked the edge case: a saldo exactly equal to the Nominal is paid in full, and isn't warned about.

docs.title: A derived flag, not a stored one — bcde54e
Asking and applying, split — 450bf39
docs.text:
SonarCloud flagged _terapkan (S3776, complexity 17 of 15) once it held both the confirmation and the apply. Extracting the question gives each method one job:

lib/features/draft_pencairan/presentation/pages/draft_editor_page.dart
/// True when there is nothing to confirm or the pengurus says yes.
Future<bool> _setujuSaldoKurang(JumlahUmum? jumlah) async {
  final kurang = _jumlahKurang(jumlah);
  if (jumlah == null || kurang == 0) return true;
  return showPencairanKonfirmasi(
    context,
    icon: Icons.warning_amber_rounded,
    judul: 'Terapkan Nominal ${rupiah(jumlah.nilai.floor())}?',
    pesan: _pesanKurang(kurang, jumlah),
    isi: _DaftarSaldoKurang(
      items: [
        for (final item in _items)
          if (jumlah.melebihiSaldo(item.saldo)) item,
      ],
    ),
    jawaban: const KonfirmasiJawaban('Ya, terapkan'),
    nada: KonfirmasiNada.peringatan,
  );
}

Future<void> _terapkan() async {
  final jumlah = _jumlahBerubah ? _jumlah : null;
  if (!await _setujuSaldoKurang(jumlah) || !mounted) return;
  context.read<DraftEditorCubit>().terapkanUmum(
        metode: _metodeBerubah ? _metode : null,
        jumlah: jumlah,
        potongan: _potonganBerubah ? _potongan : null,
      );
  // …
}

The behaviour didn't change, and the same tests stayed green. SonarCloud closed the issue on the next analysis.

docs.title: The dialog extended, not edited — b5c6b79
docs.text: The confirmation is the shared showPencairanKonfirmasi, which already accepts an isi widget between its message and its buttons. The list of affected nasabah, with name and saldo, is a small _DaftarSaldoKurang widget passed into that slot. The dialog function is untouched. The other screens that use it (konfirmasi pembayaran, batalkan, buang perubahan) can't be affected.

docs.title: One lock flag, the same convention — 6e15f8c
docs.text:
Edit Pencairan already had one rule for "this pencairan's amount and date are fixed": _terkunci => potongan > 0. It disabled the Nominal field, but the Tanggal only had a guard inside its tap handler, so it still looked editable. Now the same flag drives both, through the same enabled parameter Material's fields use:

lib/features/pencairan/presentation/widgets/pencairan_form_fields.dart
InkWell(
  key: const Key('tanggal-field'),
  onTap: enabled ? onTap : null,
  child: InputDecorator(
    decoration: appInputDecoration(
      suffixIcon: const Icon(Icons.calendar_month, color: AppColors.grey100),
      errorText: errorText,
    ).copyWith(enabled: enabled),
    // …
lib/features/pencairan/presentation/pages/edit_pencairan_page.dart
TanggalPencairanField(
  tanggal: _tanggal,
  onTap: _pickTanggal,
  errorText: state.fieldErrors['tanggal'],
  enabled: !_terkunci,
),

enabled defaults to true, so the field's existing callers are unchanged.

docs.title: SOLID in this week's code
docs.text: Principle Where How Single responsibility _setujuSaldoKurang / _terapkan One method decides whether to proceed (and asks), the other applies. Each changes for one reason. Open/closed showPencairanKonfirmasi(isi:), TanggalPencairanField(enabled:) New behaviour arrives through a slot and a defaulted parameter. The shared dialog and the field's existing uses are not modified. Dependency inversion (kept) The editor's cubit The saldo checks are plain domain methods. The cubit still depends on the DraftPencairanRepository interface, which is why the tests mock it.

docs.title: GoF design patterns in this week's code
docs.text:
• Observer: the cubit emits states and BlocBuilder rebuilds the editor. That is how the note, the cards and the totals follow the applied Nominal without being told.
  • Strategy: showPencairanKonfirmasi goes through showAdaptiveConfirmation, which picks the presentation (a sheet on a phone, a dialog in a browser) from the window width. The caller's code is the same either way.

docs.title: Security
docs.text:
Competency level: 1

This week's work guards and names two OWASP Top 10 categories in its commits, A01 Broken Access Control and A03 Injection. Both come from one guard in PIL-341 slice 3 (#127, 17 Oct).

The two QA fixes are UI changes with no security surface, so I don't claim anything for them. Level 2 needs at least five categories named in commits, and level 3 a scan with a patch plan; this week has neither. The Metasploit scan and its patch plan were claimed in Sprint 2 Week 1 and aren't counted again.

docs.title: OWASP guards in this week's code
docs.text: OWASP category Guard Commits Named in the commit A01 Broken Access Control A draft link only opens a bare draft id, so a crafted link can't steer the pengurus's own authenticated requests to another endpoint a491758 → 7d938f9 yes A03 Injection The same guard: input from the URL is never pasted into a request path unless it is a bare id the same pair yes

docs.title: A01 and A03: the draft link
docs.text:
PIL-341 slice 3 lets a saved draft open from /draft-pencairan/editor?id=<draftId>. The editor builds its requests by appending that id to a path:

  • GET draft-pencairan/<id>
  • PATCH the same path
  • POST draft-pencairan/<id>/konfirmasi and POST draft-pencairan/<id>/batalkan

So a crafted link such as ?id=../nasabah or ?id=d-1%2Fkonfirmasi would have sent the Pengurus's own authenticated requests to a path the editor never meant to call. That is user input injected into a request path (A03), used to reach past the intended access path with the victim's credentials (A01).

The guard, 7d938f9: DraftEditorArgs.fromRoute accepts an id from a link only if it matches ^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}$, the shape of a UUID or a slug. Anything else sends the user to the draft list.

The test, red first, a491758: it visits ?id=..%2Fnasabah, ?id=d-1%2Fkonfirmasi and ?id=%20. For each it asserts that the user lands on the draft list, and that no request to a draft path is built from the link. It failed before the guard, because the editor opened.

Checked end to end. A Playwright run against a local build and backend confirmed it: ?id=..%2Fnasabah lands on the list on desktop and phone, and a real UUID still opens its draft.

docs.title: Test Driven Development
docs.text:
Competency level: 4

Level 3 met: both QA fixes were built test-first, one behaviour per [RED] → [GREEN] pair, with the phase in every commit subject and [REFACTOR] commits after green. Every changed line is covered (100% on SonarCloud for both MRs). The tests cover the positive case, the negative case (nothing shown or applied) and the corner cases (exactly one affected nasabah, Persen instead of Nominal, a hand-typed nominal).

Level 4: advanced testing methods in the commits:

  • Mocks for isolation:
  • Viewport-driven tests: the test view is resized to phone and desktop, so one test drives each adaptive layout.
  • Proven guards: a test that passed when written is shown to guard its code, and a changed test is shown red before the code follows.
  • E2E through Flutter's semantics tree: Playwright, at desktop and phone sizes, against a local build and backend.

docs.title: 153's tests run the real DraftEditorCubit on a mocktail _MockRepository, a fake DraftPencairanRepository, so no server is involved and the tests assert what the cubit holds.
154's tests use a mocked PencairanUseCases, and verify(… captureAny()) captures the request to check that a locked pencairan still sends its nominal and tanggal exactly as recorded.
Coverage proof at a glance

MR Work SonarCloud new-code coverage Local diff coverage pilah-mobile #153 PIL-374: saldo warning and confirmation 100% of 56 lines, screenshot 100% of 56 changed lines pilah-mobile #154 PIL-375: locked Tanggal 100% of 5 lines, screenshot 100% of 5 changed lines

docs.title: PIL-374: warn when a general Nominal is above a nasabah's saldo — pilah-mobile #153
docs.text:
The QA finding was "a Rp 50.000 Nominal paid a Rp 19 rb saldo". The ceiling that does that is intended and stays. These tests make it visible.

Behaviour Red Green A note under the Nominal says how many nasabah it holds to their saldo: none at Rp 40.000, one at Rp 100.000, none for Persen; Terapkan stays enabled 3794f95 0511e1b After Terapkan, only the capped nasabah's card says "Saldo tidak cukup untuk …"; a hand-typed nominal clears it b99dff3 bcde54e Terapkan asks first; Batal applies nothing, "Ya, terapkan" applies 86427cb 416ac45 The confirmation lists the affected nasabah by name and saldo, and only them b49e031 b5c6b79 Review feedback: list them even when there is only one 6e5b9d5 d90af9d

Refactor after green:

  • 42dd487 put a doc comment back on the method it describes.

docs.title: Review given: Ghani's pilah-mobile #162, 23 Oct
docs.text:
Ghani's PR removes the Ekspor action (PDF and Excel) from the draft pencairan editor. It changes one line of the header and removes the _export handler, three imports and the export widget tests. It adds eight tests asserting that no export action exists on a new, saved, confirmed or cancelled draft, at phone and desktop width. The description calls it the first stage of a removal.

Review

Verified before commenting, on the PR head 38dc9cf:

  • The suite passes: flutter test test/features/draft_pencairan gives 413 passing tests.
  • Mutation check: I restored staging's editor page, with the Ekspor button, and ran the new draft export is unavailable group. 8 of 8 failed. The new tests really guard the removal; they don't pass by default.
  • No unrelated coverage lost: only export tests were removed from draft_editor_view_test.dart.
  • No remaining entry point: I searched the PR head, and nothing in the app reaches the export path any more.
  • No decision on record: Linear has no issue for removing it. The feature was delivered under PIL-316, which is Done.
Point Why it matters Suggestion 1. Which decision removes this? (question) A feature delivered and closed in PIL-316 disappears with no linked decision. QA or the sprint review could read it as a regression. Link the standup or PO decision, or open a Linear issue for the removal. 2. Track the follow-up cleanup After the PR, ExportMenuButton, DraftPdfPreviewPage, simpanBerkasDraft/bagikanBerkasDraft, DraftEditorCubit.export with EditorPhase.exporting and canExport, the repository's exportDraft, and the backend's draft_export.py are unreachable, but still compiled, tested and counted by Sonar. canExport still reads as if export were possible. A Linear issue with that list, each item linked to its line on the PR head, so the second stage isn't forgotten. 3. Show the RED in history The description walks through RED, GREEN and REFACTOR, but it is one feat commit, so only the mutation check above shows that the tests went red first. Separate [RED], [GREEN] and [REFACTOR] commits, as on the other pencairan PRs.

I posted this as a comment rather than an approval: the code is right, but (1) is a product decision that should be on record first. None of the points blocks the change itself.

docs.title: AI Literacy
docs.text:
Competency level: 3

AI used critically:

  • Its claims were checked against the code, a clean staging checkout or a control build before anything changed.
  • Its own wrong turns were caught and reported, not smoothed over: a wrong test expectation, a skill step that dirtied tracked files, a redaction pass that broke a script, a scan report that came out empty.
  • One claim it made was shown incomplete by human reviewers: the race fix on #137. It's recorded that way, along with the fix that followed, proven by a test that really races.

Decisions with team or outside impact were put to me: where to point a pen test, whether to create a Linear issue, and how to post a review.

Evidence for this week:

docs.title: Where verification changed the outcome
docs.text: Situation What happened 26 Oct: QA suggested a back button that resets the chosen role on the phone Before agreeing, it traced the role to the server: saved the moment Lanjutkan is tapped, and pinned by a backend test. It said a phone-only reset couldn't work and rated the finding High rather than Critical, with reasons. It created the Linear issue only after I said yes. 26 Oct: Its first test expected 400 for a forbidden role The mutation check showed the API's handler answers 422 {"errors": …}. It fixed the test to the project's convention, not the code, and said the assumption was its own. 26 Oct: The ship skill's ".agents copy" step In these repos .agents is tracked, so copying the outdated canonical copy dirtied two tracked files in the new worktree. It spotted that in git status, restored them, and later wrote a worktree script that skips the copy when .agents is tracked. 26 Oct: 5 backend and 25 mobile tests failed locally It didn't call them pre-existing until it had run them on a clean staging checkout, where they fail the same way, because of Windows paths. 26 Oct: The design lints can't run on Windows Instead of skipping them, it counted their patterns by hand against the baselines and caught its own breach: a hard-coded font size over the allowed count. Fixed before CI. 26 Oct: SonarCloud showed 97.1% where local said 100% It found that a PR's CI runs only the changed test files, and that two pre-existing methods counted as new lines. It added the two tests rather than explaining the number away. 26 Oct: "The conditional UPDATE closes the race" This claim was incomplete. Tristan and Pascal showed that a registration already past its role check can still link a bank afterwards. The AI's own race test had pre-linked the bank, so it never exercised that order. On 29 Oct it accepted the finding without arguing, wrote a test that really races (two threads on PostgreSQL) and watched it fail on all three paths, including accept_invite, which the review hadn't named. Then it fixed all three with a shared row lock and answered each thread. 29 Oct: Making the race test fully covered The fix left one line of the test that only runs while the bug exists. It reworked the test, then re-ran it against the pre-fix code to prove it still fails there, instead of assuming the change was harmless. 26 Oct: Pen test target An active scan sends thousands of attack requests. It asked whether to scan local or staging and listed the trade-offs. I chose local only. 26 Oct: ZAP reported 17 Medium It triaged each one against the production nginx.conf and the real servers, separating local artifacts from real findings. It reproduced the 500 with curl, and found the same crash in terbitkan, which ZAP had missed. 26 Oct: Its own tooling misled it twice The ZAP report came out empty (a wrong site separator in its call), and the E2E script showed 4 "failures" (Django 6 prints a banner before the output). It noticed both were its own mistakes, fixed them, and reran. Neither became a reported bug. 29 Oct: A redaction pass for the Linux handover Its automatic secret filter rewrote a harmless local test login in a copied script, which would have broken it. A byte-for-byte comparison against the originals caught it, and the filter was narrowed to CLI output only. 29 Oct: Reviewing #178 It expected the CDN script to be blocked, but the browser reported eval. It traced the real cause into the dependency's source, proved the regression against a control build, and, in the review, didn't claim an untested alternative (pdfrx) would work.

docs.text:
Rule Severity Where Opened Closed dart:S3776 Cognitive Complexity Critical CompleteProfileScreen.build: "reduce its Cognitive Complexity from 17 to the 15 allowed" 26 Oct, 20:48 WIB 26 Oct, 22:00 WIB, fixed

The role note had added an Authenticated check and a three-part condition to a build method that was already near the limit. I didn't suppress the rule or ask for the threshold to be raised. 87f2f0d extracts the rule into _changeableRoleTitle, a named query, and build only places the note when it gets a title. docs.text:
SonarCloud's first run on #174 reported 97.1%, with one uncovered line each in auth_remote_data_sources.dart and auth_repository_impl.dart. Both were the @override entry lines of existing methods, getMe and saveToken. They sit right below the changeRole methods I inserted, so the diff counted them as new.

docs.title: A design-lint breach, caught by hand
docs.text:
The team's test/design/* tests limit hard-coded colours and font sizes per file, against *_baseline.json. On Windows, 19 of them always fail: the baseline is keyed with / paths and Windows yields \, so every file reads "allowed 0". They fail the same way on a clean staging checkout, so a local run can't tell me anything.

So I checked them by hand. I grepped every line this MR adds for the lints' patterns, and counted per file against the baselines.

  • My new role note's TextStyle(fontSize: 13, …) raised complete_profile_screen.dart from its allowed 1 hard-coded font size to 2, which would have failed CI.
  • 00fec19 switched it to AppTextStyle.small, which brought the count back to 1.
  • A final scan found no other lint pattern in the added lines. CI agreed: "Format, analyze, tests & build" passed.

docs.title: Example commit messages
docs.text:
feat(onboarding): [GREEN] refuse a role change once onboarding has started (PIL-451, OWASP A04, A01)

change_role is now one conditional UPDATE: it only touches the row
while the profile is incomplete, there is no bank sampah (pending
included) and no linked membership. Otherwise 409 role_locked, and the
role stays.

Design issue: check-then-act. Reading the state, then saving, leaves a
window where a bank registration commits in between and is left under a
role it no longer matches.
Pattern: guarded state transition, done as a conditional UPDATE, so the
database re-checks the row as it writes it (the same technique as
_reactivate_rejected_membership). Origin: designed in.

The UPDATE does not run User.clean, so the membership condition is part
of the filter itself. The refusal is a clean 409, not the 500 that
clean's ValidationError gave (OWASP A01), and the onboarding state
machine is enforced on the server, not trusted to the client (OWASP A04).

test(onboarding): [RED] add failing test for changing role from Lengkapi Profil (PIL-451)

QA suggested a way back from Lengkapi Profil to the role choice. The
profile step must:

- name the role being registered ("Mendaftar sebagai Pengurus Bank
  Sampah") with a "Ganti peran" link that opens the role page on top,
  so back returns to the form;
- hide the link once a bank sampah exists for the account, and when
  joining through an invite (the backend refuses those anyway);
- redraw for the new role once the session switches to it: a nasabah
  gets "Pilih Bank Sampah" as step two, not "Data Bank Sampah".

Fails: there is no label or link. And with the label assertion
removed, the redraw check still fails, because the screen only listens
to the auth state and keeps drawing the old role's stepper.

The full subject lists read as a sequence of phases. Mobile, oldest first:

test(onboarding): [RED] add failing test for changing role through the data layer (PIL-451)
feat(onboarding): [GREEN] change role through PATCH onboarding/role and keep its session (PIL-451)
test(preview): cover the preview session's changeRole (PIL-451)

docs.title: Programming
docs.text:
Competency level: 3

Standard principles applied and shown in PIL-451's two MRs:

  • All five SOLID principles, each with the code it applies to. See SOLID in this week's code.
  • Concurrency handled explicitly. A conditional UPDATE came first; when review showed it was half the race, a row lock shared by every writer of the invariant replaced it, reached across contexts through a port.
  • An append-only audit log for a privilege change.
  • Session renewal when the privilege level changes.
  • One page serving two entry states, decided once.
  • A single source of truth for role titles.
  • Extract Method, once from a SonarCloud finding and once on my own initiative.

Each item names the design issue it addresses, the pattern or principle used, its type and where the issue came from.

docs.title: Design issues and the patterns that address them
docs.text: Code Design issue Pattern / principle Type Origin change_role Check-then-act across two writers: the role change and each registration check the account, then write later, so either can slip in between First a guarded state transition (one conditional UPDATE), then a pessimistic row lock shared by every writer: SELECT … FOR UPDATE on the account row before deciding Technique (concurrency) The UPDATE was designed in. It was incomplete: my own defect, found in review (Tristan's P1). Fixed with the lock in df45397 lock_for_onboarding A cross-context concern: bank_sampah must take a lock that authentication owns, without reaching into its services A port (hexagonal / ports and adapters): the authentication context exposes the lock through apps.authentication.api Architectural Designed in, following the project's existing ports UserRoleChangeLog (from role) A double tap could log a transition that never happened First a compare-and-set on the role read; since the lock, a second change waits and reads the role the first left Technique (serialization) Designed in, simplified by the lock UserRoleChangeLog No accountability for a privilege change Audit Log (Fowler): an append-only row per change, written in the same transaction, same shape as BankSampahApprovalLog Architectural Designed in (OWASP A09) _session_response A stale privilege in the token: the access token carries a role claim Renew the session on a privilege change (OWASP Session Management) Principle (security) Designed in (OWASP A07) The role page A create-only screen: the role page could only create an account, so a role saved on the server had no way back from the client One page, two entry states, decided once in initState; submit and listener branch on it, with no second page duplicating the cards Technique QA finding (PIL-451) on PIL-180's design titleFor Duplicated knowledge: Lengkapi Profil needs the role's display title, which the role page's options already define Single source of truth (DRY): a static query over the same _roleOptions the cards are drawn from Principle Designed in ref.watch A stale screen: after a role change, go_router returns to the same /complete-profile State, which still drew the old role's form Observer: the screen subscribes to the auth state and rebuilds when it changes GoF Behavioural (via Riverpod) Found by the red test in 9e83120 _changeableRoleTitle A long method mixing layout with a business rule: build at cognitive complexity 17 of 15 Extract Method (Fowler): a query method that names the rule Refactoring Tool finding on my own code (SonarCloud S3776) _submit A nested ternary choosing between two actions inside onPressed Extract Method Refactoring My own [REFACTOR]

docs.title: A guarded transition, then a shared lock — 52f087f, df45397
docs.text:
A role may change only while onboarding has committed nothing for it.

First version (52f087f): the conditions were part of one conditional UPDATE … WHERE, so the database re-checked the row as it wrote. It also replaced a 500: User.clean used to be the only thing stopping a linked member from changing role, and its ValidationError escaped unhandled.

The defect review found. Tristan (P1), with Pascal confirming the other side, showed it was only half the race:

  • register_bank_sampah checks user.role, then saves user.bank_sampah later;
  • register_nasabah and accept_invite have the same gap;
  • a role change committing in between still slipped through, because the UPDATE only saw links that were already committed.

The fix (df45397): every writer of this invariant takes the same row lock before deciding.

apps/authentication/services.py
@staticmethod
def lock_account(user: User) -> None:
    """Lock the account row for the caller's transaction and reload it.

    A role change and every onboarding write that checks the role
    (PIL-451) lock this same row, so they run one after the other: a bank
    or a membership is never linked under a role that changed after its
    check, and a role change sees whatever a finished registration
    linked. Call inside ``transaction.atomic()``.
    """
    User.objects.select_for_update().only("pk").get(pk=user.pk)
    user.refresh_from_db()
apps/authentication/services.py (change_role)
with transaction.atomic():
    OnboardingService.lock_account(user)
    if user.is_profile_complete or user.bank_sampah_id or user.keanggotaan_nasabah.exists():
        raise AuthServiceError(
            "Peran tidak dapat diganti setelah pendaftaran berjalan.",
            code="role_locked",
            status_code=409,
        )
    previous = user.role
    if previous != role:
        User.objects.filter(pk=user.pk).update(role=role, updated_at=timezone.now())
        UserRoleChangeLog.objects.create(user=user, from_role=previous, to_role=role)
apps/bank_sampah/services.py
@staticmethod
@transaction.atomic
def accept_invite(user: User, token: str) -> tuple[BankSampah, str]:
    lock_for_onboarding(user)
    # … the role check and the link to the inviting bank now see the locked row

bank_sampah reaches the lock through the authentication context's port, apps.authentication.api.lock_for_onboarding, not its services. The architecture test, which allows only apps.<bc>.api across contexts, still passes.

docs.title: The log cannot lie — 2c591c5
docs.text:
The audit row follows the project's existing approval logs: append-only, written only by the service, in the same transaction as the change. Because of the row lock, a second change waits for the first and reads the role it left. So a logged from_role is always the role the account really had.

apps/authentication/models.py
class UserRoleChangeLog(models.Model):
    """A role an account switched away from during onboarding (PIL-451).

    Written only by AuthService.change_role, in the same transaction as the
    change; rows are never edited.
    """

    id = models.UUIDField(primary_key=True, default=uuid.uuid4, editable=False)
    user = models.ForeignKey(User, on_delete=models.CASCADE, related_name="role_change_logs")
    from_role = models.CharField(max_length=20, choices=User.Role.choices)
    to_role = models.CharField(max_length=20, choices=User.Role.choices)
    created_at = models.DateTimeField(auto_now_add=True)

docs.title: A new session for a new privilege — 13c1a44
docs.text:
The endpoint answers with the same session payload as a Google login, built by the existing AuthService._session_response. So the new access token names the new role, and the client routes on next_step exactly as it does after registering.

Pascal noted that the old tokens aren't revoked: the access token lasts 24 h and the refresh token 30 d. Nothing reads a role from the token today, so it's harmless, but my PR description overstated it. I corrected the description to "the new tokens carry the new role" and stated the limit.

docs.title: One page, two entry states — 9517dbd
docs.text:
The role page served only a fresh Google registration, holding a registration token. Rather than copying its role cards into a second page, it decides once which kind of visit this is:

lib/features/authentication/presentation/pages/role_selection_page.dart
@override
void initState() {
  super.initState();
  final state = ref.read(authenticationProvider);
  _registration = _registrationFrom(state);
  if (_registration == null &&
      state is Authenticated &&
      state.authEntity.nextStep == 'complete_profile') {
    _account = state.authEntity;
    _selectedRole = GoogleRegistrationRole.values
        .where((role) => role.wireValue == state.authEntity.role)
        .firstOrNull;
  }
}

A success returns as a new Authenticated session, which the page's existing listener already routes through locationForAuthStep. A refusal comes back as a message, so the notifier never replaces the signed-in state with a failure state.

docs.title: Role titles from one place — a1b49bd
docs.text:
lib/features/authentication/presentation/pages/role_selection_page.dart
static String? titleFor(String? role) => _roleOptions
    .where((option) => option.value.wireValue == role)
    .firstOrNull
    ?.title;

docs.title: The screen follows the session — a1b49bd
docs.text: Lengkapi Profil used to only listen to the auth state, to catch a logout. After a role change, go_router returns to the same /complete-profile page with its State intact. So the screen now also watches the auth state, and redraws the new role's stepper and fields. The red test proved this before the change, with the label assertion removed.

docs.title: A rule out of a build method — 87f2f0d
docs.text:
SonarCloud flagged build (S3776, complexity 17 of 15) after the role note added an Authenticated check and a three-part condition. The rule now has a name:

lib/features/onboarding/presentation/pages/complete_profile_screen.dart
/// The title of the role this account registers as, while it may still be
/// changed (PIL-451): the role was saved on the role page and stays
/// changeable until a bank sampah is registered for it. An invite fixes the
/// role, so it gets none. Null when the note should not show.
String? _changeableRoleTitle(AuthenticationStates state) {
  if (_isInviteMode || state is! Authenticated) return null;
  if (state.authEntity.bankSampahStatus != null) return null;
  return RoleSelectionPage.titleFor(state.authEntity.role);
}

build now only places the note when it gets a title. In the same spirit, 2589b0b moved the role page's register-or-change choice out of onPressed into _submit.

GoF design patterns in this week's code
docs.text:
Category Pattern Where + commit What it does Behavioural Observer (via Riverpod) ref.watch(authenticationProvider) in Lengkapi Profil, a1b49bd (mine). It joins the role page's ref.listen, which Tristan's Riverpod migration introduced (efd6748, #160, 24 Oct) One state change, a new session, reaches every subscribed screen. The other structures this work builds on aren't GoF, so they're labelled as what they are:

  • Repository (Architectural, PoEAA): AuthRepository dates from the 2024 template (d2c9eb3). This week extends it.

docs.title: Security
docs.text:
Competency level: 3

Level 3: a scan, explained, with a patch plan. This week's security work includes a dynamic scan with OWASP ZAP 2.17.0: ZAP scan report, 26 Oct.

  • How it ran: signed in, against my own local backend and web build, with every documented endpoint imported from the OpenAPI schema.
  • Explained: every alert type is traced either to a real finding or to an artifact of the local setup, with the reason given.
  • A patch plan for each real finding, test-first.

The commits also guard and name four OWASP Top 10 categories: A01, A04, A07 and A09, each with tests. That's one short of level 2's five, so the level rests on the scan, not on the count.

docs.title: The ZAP scan
docs.text:
0 High. Four real findings, each with a planned fix (full detail in the report):

# Finding OWASP Severity Planned fix 1 tarik and terbitkan crash (500) on a missing or malformed id. I reproduced it by hand; ZAP only caught tarik A04 Low–Medium Load through the bank-scoped get_object() (404), test-first 2 The backend CSP allows any HTTPS origin (script-src 'self' https: and three more directives) A05 Medium default-src 'none' for JSON; exact origins for the docs page and the OAuth popup 3 Swagger UI loads @latest from jsDelivr with no SRI A08 Low (debug-only) Pin it and add hashes, or serve it locally 4 The web app shell has no script-src A05 Low–Medium In progress as Pascal's #178; my review found one regression in it

Explained, not just listed. Of 15 alert types, the missing clickjacking and nosniff headers and the version-leaking Server header are local artifacts. Production nginx already sends those headers, and production doesn't run the dev servers. The report says why for each one, so the patch plan holds only real work.

docs.text: OWASP category Guard Tests Commits A01 Broken Access Control Only registering roles may change a role; superadmin can be neither left nor reached; a linked member can't leave the bank's scope Anonymous 401, superadmin 403, asking for superadmin 422, linked member 409 (once an unhandled 500) e227286, 52f087f, cafba5a. The superadmin guards are mutation-proven A04 Insecure Design The onboarding state machine is enforced on the server; role changes and registrations serialize on the account row A completed profile, a pending bank or a linked membership gets 409; a two-thread race test on PostgreSQL for the bank, membership and invite paths e227286, 52f087f, bf3a529, f4b663d, df45397 A07 Identification and Authentication Failures A role change answers with a new session, so new tokens carry the new role The token's role claim is checked after the switch a23ba21, 13c1a44 A09 Security Logging and Monitoring Failures Every role change is written to user_role_change_log (account, from, to, when) in the same transaction One row per real change, none for a refusal or a re-pick 62e79e1, 2c591c5

docs.title: What review changed
docs.text:
• The A04 guard was incomplete, and is now fixed. Tristan's P1 showed that a registration whose role check ran before the role change could still link a bank afterwards. The fix (df45397) makes every writer lock the account row; accept_invite turned out to have the same gap and got the same fix (details).
  • The A07 guard is about new tokens only. The old access token (24 h) and refresh token (30 d) still carry the old role. Pascal noted it's harmless today, because nothing reads a role from the token. My PR description had overclaimed it, and now states the limit. Blacklisting the old refresh token is offered as a follow-up.

docs.title: Test Driven Development
docs.text:
Competency level: 4

Level 3 met: both PIL-451 MRs were built test-first, one behaviour per [RED] → [GREEN] pair, with the phase in every commit subject and [REFACTOR] commits only after green. Every changed line is covered: 100% on SonarCloud for both MRs, 48 and 68 new lines. The tests cover the positive case, the negative cases (each refusal) and the corner cases (a stale account object, re-picking the same role, a malformed response).

Level 4: advanced testing methods in the commits:

  • Mocks and fakes for isolation:
    • the mobile data layer runs the real AuthRepositoryImpl on mocktail mocks of its remote and local data sources;
    • captureAny captures the stored tokens to prove the new session is the one saved.
    • The notifier tests run the real AuthenticationNotifier on a mocked LoginWithGoogleUseCase. Page tests use a fake notifier that records changeRole and answers with a configured refusal or session.
  • A real race, made deterministic: a TransactionTestCase on PostgreSQL runs each registration in one thread, pausing right after its role check, and a role change in another. It's been checked both ways: all three paths fail without the row lock, and pass with it.
  • Guards proven by mutation: two tests passed when written. For each, I broke the code it guards, watched it fail, and reverted.
  • E2E with database assertions: Playwright drives the web build through Flutter's semantics tree at desktop and phone sizes, then checks the backend's database for the stored role and the audit row.

docs.title: Backend: pilah-be #137
docs.text:
Behaviour Red Green The red failed on An unfinished account switches role, and the new access token names the new role a23ba21 13c1a44 404: no route yet The role stays (409 role_locked) once the profile is complete, a bank sampah exists (pending included), or a membership is linked e227286 52f087f Two cases switched with 200. The linked member hit User.clean's ValidationError, an unhandled 500 Each change is recorded in user_role_change_log; a refusal or a re-pick of the same role writes nothing 62e79e1 2c591c5 'User' object has no attribute 'role_change_logs' Review P1: a role change during a bank registration, a membership application or an invite acceptance waits for it, then refuses (role_locked) f4b663d df45397 All three paths: {'changed': True, 'waited_for_registration': False}. The role flipped under a registration, which then linked a bank to a nasabah, or hit an unhandled ValidationError (membership)

Refactor after green: fe17440 makes the race test record its outcome on both paths. The "change went through" branch could only run while the bug existed, so diff-cover showed the test at 98.6%. I re-ran the reworked test against the pre-fix services, and all three cases still fail there.

Guard tests, proven by mutation. Both passed when written, so there was no red phase. I mutated the code, watched each test fail, then reverted. The mutations are recorded in the commit bodies:

  • cafba5a, who may change a role: anonymous gets 401, superadmin 403, and asking to become superadmin 422.
    • With IsAuthenticated in place of IsRegistrationRole, the test failed with 200: the superadmin had switched itself to nasabah.
    • With every role allowed in the serializer, it failed with 200: a nasabah had become superadmin.
  • bf3a529, the race. The account is loaded, then a bank sampah is registered, then the role change runs on the stale object. A check-then-save version failed with "AuthServiceError not raised": the pengelola was switched to nasabah.
apps/authentication/test_role_change.py
def test_a_bank_registered_after_the_account_was_loaded_still_keeps_the_role(self) -> None:
    user = self._fresh(User.Role.PENGELOLA)
    # Loaded by this request before a parallel one registered a bank sampah.
    stale = User.objects.get(pk=user.pk)
    bank = BankSampah.objects.create(
        nama="Bank Baru",
        alamat="Depok",
        no_hp_pic="+628111111111",
        status=BankSampah.Status.PENDING,
    )
    User.objects.filter(pk=user.pk).update(bank_sampah=bank)

    with self.assertRaises(AuthServiceError) as refused:
        AuthService.change_role(stale, User.Role.NASABAH)

    self.assertEqual(refused.exception.code, "role_locked")
    user.refresh_from_db()
    self.assertEqual(user.role, User.Role.PENGELOLA)

A wrong assumption in my own test, corrected. I first wrote that asking for superadmin returns 400. This API's exception handler answers validation errors with 422 {"errors": …}, so I fixed the test to the project's convention. The code was right.

What review added. Tristan showed that this test proves only one side of the race. It pre-links the bank, so a registration whose role check ran before the role change was never exercised. The P1 race test above does exercise it, with real threads and row locks:

tests/regression/identity/test_role_change_race.py
with patch.object(owner, method, paused):
    a = threading.Thread(target=registration, name="registration")
    a.start()
    self.assertTrue(reached.wait(WAIT), "registration never reached its write")
    b = threading.Thread(target=role_change, name="role-change")
    b.start()
    b.join(1.0)
    outcome["waited_for_registration"] = b.is_alive()
    proceed.set()
    a.join(WAIT)
    b.join(WAIT)

Thread A's registration pauses inside its write, after the role check. Thread B's role change must still be blocked a second later, which is only possible if both take the same row lock. Then A finishes, and B must come back with role_locked.

His P2 asked for success tests for every Google role, not just nasabah. d83b0c1 switches to each registration role from a different one. It passed as written, so I proved it with a mutation: with pengelola_induk removed from the serializer, its case failed with 422.

docs.title: E2E (Playwright)
docs.text:
Run on 26 Oct against flutter build web --profile and a local backend from #137, with a fresh account for each run. The demo login's email was rewritten in flight, so the backend asks for a role as it would for a new Google account. All 14/14 checks pass at 1440×900 and 390×844:

  1. A new account is asked for a role. It taps Pengelola Bank Sampah Induk, and the role is saved.
  2. Lengkapi Profil reads "Mendaftar sebagai Pengelola Bank Sampah Induk".
  3. "Ganti peran" opens the role page for the signed-in account, without "Ganti akun".
  4. Switching to Pengurus shows the Pengurus form ("Data Bank Sampah").

docs.title: Team Development Management
docs.text:
Competency level: 3

A detailed review of Pascal's pilah-mobile #178, which adds HSTS and a real Content-Security-Policy to the web image. It answers the check his description asked for, a signed-in click-through, which he couldn't do himself:

  • verified signed in under the PR's exact headers, against a control build without them: 8 pages clean;
  • one regression found (the draft PDF preview on web) and traced to its cause in a dependency;
  • three feasible fixes for it, cheapest first, and one hardening suggestion with the concrete change.

The other side of reviewing is here too: Tristan's and Pascal's reviews of my #137. Each finding was checked against the code, fixed test-first, and answered in its own thread with the fix linked.

docs.title: Review given: Pascal's pilah-mobile #178
docs.text:
The PR replaces the web image's frame-ancestors-only CSP with a full policy:

  • strict script-src, with no inline scripts or eval;
  • 'wasm-unsafe-eval' for CanvasKit;
  • Google Sign-In allowed;
  • 30 days of HSTS.

Its description says only the login page was tested, and asks someone to sign in and click through the app.

Review

Verified before commenting, on the PR head 4480886:

  • Same headers as production: I built the PR for web and served it with the exact add_header lines parsed from its nginx.conf. The only change was a local connect-src entry standing in for *.fly.dev.
  • Signed in: as the seeded demo Pengurus.
  • Recorded: each violation, through the browser's own securitypolicyviolation event.
  • Control: the same build, served without the CSP.
  • Read the config: no location block sets its own add_header, so nginx's inheritance quirk doesn't drop the headers on any path.
  • CI really runs the tests: the Docker-based header tests run in CI (ci.yml, line 71).
Page Violations with the PR's CSP Login and sign-in, Beranda, Nasabah, Jadwal, Harga, Laporan, Draft Pencairan list, Profil 0 Draft editor → Ekspor → PDF 1, script-src blocked eval. The preview never renders With the PR's CSP Same build, no CSP

Traced to its cause, not guessed. I expected the CDN script to be the problem, but the browser reported eval. The PDF library's (printing 5.14.3) web code runs window.eval('typeof pdfjsLib …') before it loads anything (printing_web.dart L57-L63). After that it would also load pdf.js from unpkg. So allowing unpkg wouldn't help, and adding 'unsafe-eval' would break the PR's own test.

Point Why it matters Suggestion 1. The draft PDF preview breaks on web Pengurus can reach it on web today, and it would spin forever after this deploys The CSP is right, so change the app instead. Cheapest first: (a) merge Ghani's #162, which removes draft export, before #178; (b) on web, skip the preview and download directly; (c) render with pdfrx, already a dependency, whose WASM loads from the same origin (not yet tested under the CSP). Add a browser check, so the next CSP change can't break it silently 2. connect-src https://*.fly.dev https://*.run.app It trusts every app on two shared hosting domains, and anyone can deploy one, so an XSS could send data out The image is the official nginx:1.28-alpine, which fills in /etc/nginx/templates/*.template with envsubst at startup, substituting only variables that are actually set, so $uri is safe. Move the config there with ${PILAH_API_ORIGIN}, set per environment

I posted it as a comment, not a change request. Point 1 goes away if #162 merges first, so the ask is to agree on the merge order. Point 2 was marked as a follow-up.

Reply Tristan, P2 The only success test is pengelola → nasabah. The issue asks for every Google role Correct. He quotes the test list I wrote in PIL-451 myself, "untuk tiap peran Google". I didn't follow my own spec Fixed, d83b0c1: each role is reached from another, and the test is mutation-proven. Reply Pascal, nit "No token keeps naming the old role" overstates it: the old access token (24 h) and refresh token (30 d) aren't revoked Correct. Harmless today, since request.user comes from the database, but the description overclaimed Fixed: the description now says "the new tokens carry the new role", with the limit stated. Blacklisting was offered as a follow-up. Reply

Each finding was answered in its own thread, linking the commit or change that fixes it. The PR's tests, security and validation sections were updated to match. Pascal's suggested approach, a lock then a re-check, plus a two-thread test, is what went in, credited in the reply.

docs.text:
Competency level: 3

AI used critically:

  • Claims checked before acting: by running the code, a clean staging checkout, a scratch test or a screenshot. That applies to teammates' code under review, and to its own E2E failures before blaming the app.
  • Its own wrong turns reported, not smoothed over: three E2E script mistakes in a row, a test-data side effect, and code it merged that SonarCloud then flagged.
  • Discipline kept where it's easy to drop: review fixes kept out of merge commits so each gets its own red/green pair, and an untestable branch removed rather than covered with a contrived test.

Decisions with product or team impact were put to me: the three PIL-428 design choices, which issue to take next, and which PRs to review.

Evidence for this week:

  • The PRs, reviews and replies linked below, each of which records the checks described here.

It starts after the PIL-428 build, when the context was summarised, and runs from the PR conflict check through the reviews, these docs and the ZAP scans. Before publishing, I scanned it for emails, tokens, JWTs, student and Discord IDs, webhooks and home-folder paths: none found. The only matches were three fake phone numbers from test fixtures.

Programming
docs.text:
Competency level: 3

Standard principles applied and shown in this week's code:

  • A void as an audited state change, not a delete, so the ledger stays append-only. A database check constraint means it can't be half-recorded.
  • Concurrency handled explicitly: the void locks the saldo, then the setoran, in the same order as an edit. On PIL-451, one more writer now joins the shared account lock.
  • A domain rule named once: "a voided setoran counts toward nothing" is a QuerySet method rather than nine copies of a filter.
  • A hardcoded release toggle read through a configured widget, so closing or reopening a feature is one edit.
  • Extract Method twice from SonarCloud findings, and once more as my own refactor.
  • All five SOLID principles, each with the code it applies to. See SOLID in this week's code.

Each item names the design issue it addresses, the pattern or principle used, its type and where the issue came from.

docs.title: A void is a state change, not a delete — 638cb3f, 966c7ba
docs.text:
apps/ledger/services.py
@staticmethod
def batalkan_setoran(user: User, transaksi: Transaksi, alasan: str) -> Transaksi:
    """Void a setoran: keep the row, mark it cancelled, take its total out of the saldo.

    `transaksi` comes from the caller's bank-scoped queryset; it is re-read under lock.
    """
    saldo = Saldo.objects.select_for_update().get(nasabah_id=transaksi.nasabah_id)
    transaksi = TransactionService._kunci_tercatat(transaksi)
    saldo_baru = bulatkan_rupiah(saldo.total_saldo - transaksi.total_nilai)
    sesudahnya = TransactionService._geser_pencairan(transaksi, -transaksi.total_nilai)
    if saldo_baru < 0 or any(cair.saldo_sesudah < 0 for cair in sesudahnya):
        raise SaldoTidakCukup(
            "Setoran ini tidak bisa dibatalkan karena sebagian saldonya sudah dicairkan"
        )
    transaksi.status = Transaksi.Status.DIBATALKAN
    transaksi.alasan_batal = alasan
    transaksi.dibatalkan_oleh = user
    transaksi.dibatalkan_pada = timezone.now()
    ...
  • Fixed lock order: the saldo row is locked first, then the setoran is re-read under lock. edit_setoran takes the same two locks in the same order, so a void and an edit can't deadlock or see each other half-done. _kunci_tercatat also refuses a setoran voided meanwhile, which is what makes a void final.
  • Paid-out money: a void is an edit by −total, so it reuses _geser_pencairan to shift every later pencairan's snapshot. Then it refuses if any of them would have been paid from money that no longer existed, even when the final saldo stays positive.

docs.title: A domain rule named once — ae850a0
docs.text:
While writing this page, I counted the void's "leave it out" rule written as filter(status=Transaksi.Status.TERCATAT) in nine places: saldo replay, saldo-after, ringkasan, export, operational summary, dashboard stats, trends and the statement. A tenth report would have to remember it. So it now has a name:

apps/ledger/models.py
class TransaksiQuerySet(models.QuerySet["Transaksi"]):
    def tercatat(self) -> "TransaksiQuerySet":
        """Setoran that still count: everything but a void (PIL-428).

        Saldo, laporan, exports and summaries read through this, so a new
        report cannot forget to leave voided setoran out. The riwayat feeds
        list voided rows on purpose and do not.
        """
        return self.filter(status=Transaksi.Status.TERCATAT)


class Transaksi(TimestampedModel):
    objects = TransaksiQuerySet.as_manager()
apps/reporting/statement.py
setoran = Transaksi.objects.tercatat().filter(
    nasabah=member, bank_sampah=member.bank_sampah
)

As the default manager's queryset, it also reaches related managers (nasabah.transaksi.tercatat()). One lookup across a relation (DetailTransaksi by transaksi__status) keeps the field filter, and the commit says so. There's no behaviour change: the full suite gives the same result, strict mypy is clean, and diff coverage is 100% of 348 lines.

docs.title: Security
docs.text:
Competency level: 3

Level 3: a scan, explained, with a patch plan. Each sub-issue finished this week, PIL-428 and PIL-435, got its own OWASP ZAP 2.17.0 scan right after the work was done. Both ran signed in, against my own local instances, and were limited to the feature's endpoints. Report: ZAP scans per sub-issue, 2 Nov.

  • 0 High. No alert on the features' own endpoints across about 15,000 attack requests.
  • Every alert explained: each Medium and Low ZAP raised is either a known finding from the 26 Oct scan, still open on staging, or an artifact of the local servers. The report says which, and why.
  • Beyond ZAP's alerts: reading every response in the scan history found a real crash ZAP doesn't flag. A NUL byte in ?search= gives a 500 on six list endpoints. Reproduced by hand, with a test-first patch plan, plus two debug-only crashes.
  • The void's input tested by hand: injection payloads stored verbatim as data; a NUL byte, an over-long alasan or a blank one rejected with 422.

The commits also guard and name four OWASP categories: A01, A04, A08 and A09. That's one short of level 2's five, so the level rests on the scan, not on the count.

docs.title: Test Driven Development
docs.text:
Competency level: 4

Level 3 met: every behaviour this week was built test-first, one behaviour per [RED] → [GREEN] pair, with the phase in every commit subject and [REFACTOR] commits only after green.

  • Every changed line is covered: 100% on SonarCloud for all five MRs touched this week.
  • The tests cover the positive case, each refusal and the corner cases (see the table).
  • Tests that pass when written are labelled as coverage tests and committed without a phase tag.

Level 4: advanced testing methods in the commits:

  • The database as a test oracle: a check constraint is proven by attempting three half-recorded voids and expecting IntegrityError for each.
  • A real race, made deterministic: a two-thread TransactionTestCase on PostgreSQL pauses a Google login right before it saves a membership, and runs a role change in between.
  • Mocks, stubs and fakes for isolation:
    • mobile notifiers run on mocktail mocks of their use cases;
    • page tests run on a StubApi that answers per route;
    • the role page uses a fake notifier that records its calls.
  • E2E with database assertions: Playwright drives the web build through Flutter's semantics tree at desktop and phone sizes, then reads the void's status, alasan, author and saldo from the backend database.

The constraint test, which uses the database itself as the oracle:

apps/ledger/test_setoran_void.py
def test_database_refuses_a_void_without_who_when_and_why(self) -> None:
    setengah: list[dict[str, Any]] = [
        {"status": Transaksi.Status.DIBATALKAN},
        {"status": Transaksi.Status.DIBATALKAN, "dibatalkan_oleh": self.pengelola},
        {"alasan_batal": "x", "dibatalkan_pada": timezone.now()},
    ]
    for fields in setengah:
        with self.subTest(fields=fields), self.assertRaises(IntegrityError):
            with transaction.atomic():
                Transaksi.objects.filter(pk=self.transaksi.pk).update(**fields)

.update() skips the service and the serializer, so only the database can refuse these.

docs.title: Review given: Rifqi's pilah-be #144, 2 Nov
docs.text:
The PR adds ?urutan= ordering to the customer list (PIL-442) and hardens the list endpoint:

  • validated, bounded query inputs;
  • duplicate-key rejection;
  • a per-user throttle;
  • private, no-store responses;
  • sanitized rejection logs.

Review

Verified before commenting, at 774cb4a:

  • checked out and ran apps.nasabah on Postgres 16: 87 tests, all pass;
  • confirmed the tie-breaker is safe: nomor is unique per bank (unique_together (bank_sampah, nomor)), so pages can't overlap;
  • traced every caller of GET /api/v1/nasabah in the app: the Nasabah page and the setoran picker, both with a 300 ms debounce;
  • wrote a throwaway test (never committed) that makes get_queryset raise ProgrammingError, then captured every log record.
STATUS 503 {'error': 'Daftar nasabah sementara tidak tersedia. Silakan coba lagi.'}
LOG apps.nasabah.security WARNING Customer list rejected: status=503  exc_info=False
LOG django.request ERROR Service Unavailable: /api/v1/nasabah        exc_info=False
Point Why it matters Suggestion 1. A query bug becomes a 503 with no traceback On staging, the same bug is a 500 that Django logs with its traceback. Here it reads as a temporary outage that can't be diagnosed, which undercuts the PR's own A09 goal Keep the 503 only for OperationalError/InterfaceError, log the exception with exc_info, and let real bugs stay 500s. Code given, plus an assertLogs test to pin it 2. docs.title: Review given: Gabriel's pilah-mobile #202, 2 Nov
docs.text:
The PR takes the Pengumuman entry points from "disabled but visible" (Tray's #158) to not drawn at all, as CPBI-31's "tidak ada menu mati" asks. It keeps the old URLs as redirects and leaves lib/features/pengumuman/ untouched so the feature can be restored.

Review

Verified before commenting, at 6ad6ba2:

  • checked out and ran every suite the PR touches, plus all of test/features/pengumuman: 389 pass;
  • grepped lib/ for any remaining way in (Profil, notifications, the shell): none. Only the DI registration and the session-reset cleanup remain, which is right for a restorable feature;
  • compared the deleted route builders and tests with staging.
Point Why it matters Suggestion 1. The restore path lost its guards The PR rests "still restorable" on the feature's own tests. The route-level guards were deleted, though: the state.extra fallbacks for stale links, and the keanggotaan_id a nasabah with two banks needs. So were the two tests that pinned them Keep the four original routes as an unregistered pengumumanRoutes list in the feature, derive the redirect paths from it, and move the two tests to mount it. Reopening becomes one line. Code given 2. The Nasabah question the PR raised The description flags removing the Nasabah Beranda section as beyond the ticket CPBI-31's criteria say "Fitur pengumuman tidak tampil di aplikasi" for everyone, so it's in scope. Quote it to settle it Positive: the redirect target Redirecting through the dashboard re-enters the role redirect, so a nasabah lands on their own home —

I also pointed out the same dead-control pattern in the greyed "Pencairan" menu item, which belongs to PIL-434, for whoever takes that issue.

docs.title: AI Literacy
docs.text:
Competency level: 3

AI used critically:

  • Claims checked before acting: by writing the failing test first, by sending an attack by hand, and by running the same check on a clean staging.
  • Results not trusted when the run was broken: a scan on a full disk was redone rather than reported, and every 5xx was classified before any was called a finding.
  • Work stopped rather than guessed at when the cause couldn't be confirmed (PIL-475, the Gmail finding).
  • Its own mistake owned: the leaked webhooks in this week's scan evidence, caught on 13 Nov, are written up, not quietly removed.

Decisions with product or team impact were put to me: which issue to take, what PIL-481 should keep, and when to merge.

Evidence for this week:

  • The PRs, reviews and reports linked below, each of which records the checks described here. The prompts themselves aren't published.

docs.text: Situation What happened 4 Nov: Writing the test for Heraldo's dialog finding A third test, written to stage the race, found a bug nobody had reported: an answer arriving during the dialog's exit animation closed the Riwayat page underneath. It was fixed in the same pair. Then it undid each fix in turn to check that exactly one test failed each time. 4 Nov: Scallss's stale-screens finding It found that edit has the same gap on staging, and didn't widen the PR to fix it, since Scallss agreed it's a separate follow-up.
