docs.title: Programming
docs.text:
Competency level: 3

Standard principles applied and shown in this week's code:

  • One named rule, applied at the right boundary. "What still counts" is Transaksi.objects.tercatat(). This week it reached the two seed commands that bypassed it, and every riwayat list. The shared lookup that detail, edit and void read stays unfiltered, so a voided row is still reachable for audit.
  • UI state that follows the server, not the widget. The Hapus dialog reads what it needs before the request, applies the server's answer whether or not it is still open, and only pops itself while it is the route on top.
  • One owner for "what reloads after a setoran changes": a helper that the single void uses now, and edit and bulk can reuse.
  • A report that stops publishing an internal key, with the tests first decoupled from it.
  • All five SOLID principles, each with the code it applies to. See SOLID in this week's code.

Each item names the design issue it addresses, the pattern or principle used, its type and where the issue came from. The same three lines are in each commit body.

docs.title: The design issues in brief
docs.text:
• A rule that two writers didn't follow. "A voided setoran doesn't count" had one name, tercatat(), but two seed commands summed the raw table, so re-seeding after a void put the money back. Fix: the seeds call the same method as the reports.
  • One query, two different needs. The riwayat lists must hide a void, but detail, edit and void must still find it, and filtering the shared query would make a voided setoran's detail a 404. Fix: each list filters; the shared lookup doesn't.
  • UI state tied to the widget, not to the server. If the Hapus dialog was closed mid-request, the app skipped the refresh, although the server had voided the setoran, and a late pop could close the wrong page. Fix: read what's needed before the request, always apply the server's answer, and close the dialog only if it's still on top.
  • Each action refreshing its own list of screens. The single void reloaded one screen, the bulk void four. Fix: one helper owns what reloads after a setoran changes, and reloads only screens already open.
  • An internal key in a user's report. The export showed a database id no pengurus reads, and two tests depended on it. Fix: the tests check visible data first, then the column goes.
  • Text describing an old rule. The dialogs said a void stays in the riwayat, which stopped being true. Fix: change the text next to the flow it describes, and pin it with a test.

docs.title: Before and after
docs.text:
What each design change did, compared with the code before it.

What Pattern Before After The difference it made Seed commands (#145) Query Object / Specification (PoEAA) Transaksi.objects.filter(...) summed every setoran, voided ones included Transaksi.objects.tercatat().filter(...), the method the reports use Re-seeding after a void no longer puts the voided money back into a saldo Riwayat lists (#167) Query Object / Specification (PoEAA), applied at each list; the lookup kept apart (ISP) activity_sources started from Transaksi.objects.filter(bank_sampah=bank), so a void stayed listed, labelled Dibatalkan It starts from Transaksi.objects.tercatat(). On the nasabah side, activities(member).tercatat() at the two list call sites, while the lookup returns everything A Hapus now reads as a delete in every list, as the UAT asked, yet a voided setoran's detail still answers 200 with who, when and why Hapus dialog (#193) No design pattern: a technique for Flutter's async lifecycle (guard on the route, not mounted) Any tap outside or back closed it mid-request. Everything after the request sat behind if (!mounted) return; PopScope(canPop: !_saving), notifiers read before the await, the server's answer always applied, and the pop guarded by route.isCurrent A void that succeeds always refreshes the feed, and a late answer can no longer close the Riwayat page underneath Reload after a void (#193) Facade (GoF, structural): one call in front of four notifiers; Observer (GoF, behavioural, via Riverpod) redraws the screens The single void reloaded Riwayat only, so the dashboard, recent activity and nasabah saldo stayed stale. The bulk void reloaded four screens its own way One helper, reloadAfterSetoranChange, owns the list and checks container.exists Every screen already open shows the new totals, and no request is sent for a screen never opened Export (#168) No design pattern: a principle (SRP) 14 columns (A:N), the last an internal id; two tests counted rows through it 13 columns (A:M); the tests count rows that carry a value The pengurus's report holds only what they read, and no internal record id leaves the system in a forwarded file

docs.title: Design issues and the patterns that address them
docs.text: Code Design issue Pattern / principle Type Origin Seed commands A second write path that bypasses a named rule: the seeds rebuilt the saldo from the raw table, voided setoran included Reuse the named query (Specification-style QuerySet method) instead of a second ad-hoc filter Architectural (PoEAA Query Object) Review defect (Heraldo, #145) activity_sources One shared query serving a rule it was never given: the feed's source query never read through tercatat() Single source of truth at the shared query, so every consumer inherits it Principle (DRY, OCP) Reversal of a PIL-428 design decision, asked for by the UAT List boundaries vs the lookup One helper serving two needs: activities() and get_queryset back both the lists and the detail lookup, so filtering inside them would turn a voided detail into a 404 Filter at each list call site, keep the lookup as is Principle (ISP, SRP) Designed in, while tracing PIL-481 BatalkanSetoranDialog._hapus UI state tied to the widget's lifetime: a dialog closed mid-request skipped the refresh, and a late pop closed the wrong route Capture dependencies before the async gap; apply the outcome unconditionally; guard navigation on the route, not on mounted Technique (Flutter async lifecycle) Review defect (Heraldo, #193), plus the exit-animation case I found writing its test reloadAfterSetoranChange Each write path refreshing its own subset of views: the bulk void reloaded four, the single void one One helper owns the reload set; screens never opened are not built Principle (SRP, DRY) Review defect (Scallss, #193) Export columns An internal surrogate key in a user-facing report, and tests coupled to it Assert on visible data, not on a surrogate key; the export lists only what a pengurus reads Principle (SRP) UAT finding (PIL-480) Hapus copy User-facing copy describing a backend rule that PIL-481 reversed Change the copy next to the flow it describes, pinned by a widget test Technique Found by tracing PIL-481, not named in the issue

docs.title: The named rule reaches two more writers — abcafa3
docs.text:
Last week's refactor named the rule once. Heraldo found that two seed commands, one of them run on every production demo seeding, still summed the raw table:

api/management/commands/seed_play_demo_accounts.py
# A voided setoran stays in the table but not in the saldo (PIL-428).
setoran = Transaksi.objects.tercatat().filter(
    ...
)

Both seeds now read through the same method the reports use. I checked every other place that sums setoran outside the tests: these two were the only gap.

docs.title: Lists filter, the lookup does not — 6995649, c3606b5
docs.text:
The riwayat feed has one source query, so the rule goes there and every consumer inherits it:

apps/ledger/activity.py
def activity_sources(...):
    """One authorization/filter policy for history, totals and exports.

    A voided setoran is not part of any of them (PIL-481): the riwayat does not list it,
    and it counts toward nothing. The row itself stays, as the audit trail.
    """
    deposits = Transaksi.objects.tercatat().filter(bank_sampah=bank)

On the nasabah side the same helper backs the lists and the detail lookup, so the rule goes at the two list call sites instead:

apps/nasabah/home.py
def activities(member: Nasabah) -> TransaksiQuerySet:
    """Every setoran of the member, voided ones included: the detail lookup needs them.

    The lists read ``activities(member).tercatat()`` instead (PIL-481).
    """
    ...

"aktivitas_terbaru": activities(member).tercatat()[:5],

Returning TransaksiQuerySet rather than a plain QuerySet[Transaksi] is what lets the callers ask for .tercatat(). The pengurus side does the same: the /transaksi list and the dashboard's recent list filter, while TransaksiViewSet.get_queryset, which detail, edit and void also read, does not.

docs.title: A report without an internal key — 9dbfcf2, 2b1fba9
docs.text: The UAT found the "ID Aktivitas" column useless to the Pengurus. Two tests used it to count rows, so they were refactored first to count rows that carry a value. Then the column went, with the title merges and widths moved from A:N to A:M. "ID Nasabah", the member number a pengurus does read, stays.

docs.title: The dialog follows the server's answer — 472c506
One owner for what reloads — be7b6d0
Copy that follows the rule — ff86f6f
docs.text: The single and bulk Hapus dialogs said the setoran "stays in the riwayat, marked dibatalkan". After PIL-481 that's false. The copy now says it is hidden from the riwayat and no longer counted, next to the flow it describes, with a widget test that pins it.

docs.title: SOLID in this week's code
Patterns, labelled as what they are
docs.text:
• Query Object / Specification (PoEAA): TransaksiQuerySet.tercatat(), now reused by the seeds and every list.
  • Observer (via Riverpod): the screens listen to their providers, so a reload of the notifier redraws the dashboard and the nasabah list without the dialog knowing about them.
  • Facade (GoF, structural): reloadAfterSetoranChange is one call in front of the Riwayat, dashboard, recent-activity and nasabah notifiers. The dialog, and later edit and bulk, call it without knowing which screens exist. It's a function-level Facade, not a class.
  • The dialog fix is a technique for Flutter's async lifecycle, not a design pattern, and is labelled that way in the commit.

docs.title: Security
docs.text:
Competency level: 3

Level 3: a scan, explained, with a patch plan. Each sub-issue finished this week, PIL-481 and PIL-480, got its own OWASP ZAP 2.17.0 scan right after the work was done (9 Nov). Both ran signed in, against my own local instances, and were limited to the feature's endpoints. Report: ZAP scans per sub-issue, 9 Nov.

  • 0 real High. ZAP raised three High alerts (SQL injection, Server Side Include, Padding Oracle). Each was checked by hand and is a false positive. The "SQL injection" on the void's alasan was disproved by sending both payloads myself.
  • A new finding behind two of them: a malformed nasabah_id on GET /transaksi is a 500, while /aktivitas answers 422. Reproduced by hand, given a test-first patch plan, and filed as PIL-482. It was fixed in Sprint 3 Week 3.
  • Every 5xx in ZAP's history read and classified, not only its alerts: 268 in the PIL-481 scan and 5 in PIL-480, sorted into real, debug-only and local.
  • A broken run replaced, not trusted. The first run hit a full disk and an out-of-memory database, so both scans were run again once the disk was freed. The report uses the second run.

The commits name seven OWASP categories, but only three are genuine guards with a test behind them: A04, A08 and A09. The other four labels are weak (see below). Three is short of level 2's five, so the level rests on the scan.

docs.title: The "SQL injection" on alasan, disproved by hand
docs.text:
Request Result alasan = John Doe' AND '1'='1' -- 200, voided alasan = John Doe' AND '1'='2' -- 200, voided the same setoran voided again 409

Both payloads behave the same, and the stored alasan is the payload text. ZAP's "different pages" came from a state change: the first request voided the setoran (200), and every attack after it hit an already-voided one (409). The ORM parameterises the value.

docs.title: What went wrong: the evidence leaked two webhooks
docs.text:
Finding 4's debug page also held two Discord webhook URLs from the dev machine's environment. I had redacted the computer name and my user name from the saved report files, but not these, and they were published with the report on 9 Nov. GitHub's secret scanning found them, and Discord revoked both.

This was caught and fixed on 13 Nov (Sprint 3 Week 3), in pilah-docs 2197468:

  • the two files now carry [REDACTED];
  • the scan script refuses webhooks, GitHub, Google and Slack tokens, and database URLs with a password;
  • the report's false claim that I had "grepped for secrets" is corrected.

From the 17 Nov scans on, the backends start with an empty environment, so no secret can reach a debug page. It's recorded here because the mistake was made in this week's work.

docs.title: OWASP guards in this week's code
docs.text:
OWASP category Guard Tests Commits A04 Insecure Design Re-seeding can't put voided money back into a saldo. A void in flight can't be dismissed half-done, and a successful void always refreshes the UI. Hiding a void is a filter, not a delete Reseed tests per seed command; three in-flight dialog tests; "still reachable by id" guards 743ed1c, abcafa3, 17125d0, 472c506, 7d0922d A08 Software and Data Integrity Failures Every list and total reads the same tercatat() subset, so the summary can't disagree with the list it sums. The export's 13 columns and their order are pinned Summary totals asserted unchanged after a void; the export header and max_column == 13 8143807, 3d83377 A09 Security Logging and Monitoring Failures Hiding a void never loses the audit trail: the row, who voided it, when and why stay, and its detail by id still shows them, to the pengurus and the nasabah test_a_voided_setoran_stays_reachable_by_its_id_with_its_void, test_nasabah_can_still_open_the_voided_setoran_by_its_id 7d0922d, 4401e4e

Labels I don't count. The PIL-481 and PIL-480 commit bodies also name:

  • A01: "a nasabah only ever sees their own membership's rows". True, but that scoping predates this change, which reads through the existing /me endpoints, and no new test asserts another member's rows are left out.
  • A02: "no staff-only void fields are added to the nasabah DTO", "no internal record ids in a forwarded file". That is data minimisation, closer to A01 than to cryptography.
  • A03: for a filter on a fixed status value, there's no untrusted input to inject.
  • A05: "no new query flag or toggle", "the sheet layout is pinned". That's the absence of a change, not a guard.

They are honest descriptions of what the change doesn't break, but not controls, so they aren't claimed here.

docs.title: Test Driven Development
docs.text:
Competency level: 4

Level 3 met: every behaviour this week was built test-first, one behaviour per [RED] → [GREEN] pair, with the phase in every commit subject. A refactor came first where it made the change one edit (#168), and after green where cleanup was useful (#193).

  • Every changed line is covered: 100% on SonarCloud for every MR with lines to cover. #238 changes only copy and comments, so it has no coverable lines; its copy is pinned by a widget test.
  • The tests cover the positive case, the refusals and the corner cases (see the table).
  • Tests that pass when written are labelled as such, never tagged [RED].

Level 4: advanced testing methods in the commits:

  • A stub API with latency, to make a race deterministic: the page tests run on a StubApi that answers per route, and a one-second latency holds the void in flight while the test taps outside, presses back, or closes the dialog by other means.
  • Mutation checks on the review fixes: on #193, undoing any one of the three dialog fixes makes exactly one test fail, so each test pins its own fix.
  • Provider state asserted directly: the tests read the Riverpod ProviderContainer after the void, including that screens never opened were never built.
  • E2E with database checks: Playwright drives the PIL-481 web build at desktop and phone sizes and reads the result back from the backend: 24/24.

docs.title: Mocks, stubs and fakes in this week's tests
docs.text:
A test double stands in for a real collaborator so that a test controls it. A stub gives fixed answers, a mock is a generated stand-in for an interface, and a fake or spy is a small working version that also records what was done to it. Each double below has one job, and the code under test around it is real.

Double Kind Replaces Why it's needed Used in StubApi Stub, at the HTTP boundary (Dio's HttpClientAdapter) The backend It answers each METHOD path with fixed JSON, and with latency set it delays every answer. The real network service, data sources, repositories, use cases and notifiers all still run, so only the server is fake. The one-second latency holds a void in flight while the test taps outside, presses back or closes the dialog The three in-flight dialog tests and the reload tests on #193 _Feed Fake and spy (a subclass of RiwayatAktivitasNotifier) The Riwayat feed It starts with fixed rows and counts its load() calls. That lets a test assert the feed reloads exactly once after a void (expect(feed.loads, 1)), even when the dialog closed before the answer arrived The #193 dialog tests _MockGetAktivitas, _MockExport Mocks (mocktail) The two use cases the feed is built with _Feed never calls them, but its constructor needs them. A mock fills the slot without a network The #193 dialog tests dashboardProvider.overrideWith(...), recentActivityProvider.overrideWith(...) Riverpod provider overrides, built on StubApi The real wiring of the dashboard and recent-activity notifiers The test decides which screens exist in the container, so it can check that open screens reload and that a screen never opened is never built "a void also reloads the dashboard, recent activity and nasabah", "a void does not load screens that were never opened"

Where nothing is faked, on purpose. The backend tests (#145, #167, #168) run on a real test database through Django's test client. What they check lives in the queries themselves: which rows a list returns, what a seed sums, what columns an export writes. A mocked ORM would only test the mock.

docs.title: PIL-428, the final review round (4 Nov)
docs.text:
Committed on Wed 4 Nov, 17:20–20:36.

Finding Red Green What the red asserts Re-seeding after a void puts the voided money back into the saldo (Heraldo, #145) 743ed1c abcafa3 For each seed command, test_reseed_leaves_a_voided_setoran_out_of_the_saldo: seed, void a seeded setoran, seed again, and the saldo still equals the counted setoran only The Hapus dialog can be closed while the void is in flight, then skips the refresh (Heraldo, #193) 17125d0 472c506 Three tests, below A void leaves the dashboard, recent activity and nasabah list stale (Scallss, #193) 6979612 be7b6d0 "a void also reloads the dashboard, recent activity and nasabah", and "a void does not load screens that were never opened"

Refactor after green: b815354 replaces a bare 12 with AppSpacing.md (Scallss's nit).

A third bug, found by writing the test. Heraldo found two problems; the red commit has three tests. The third came from writing the second: if the server answers while the dialog is still animating closed, the dialog's Navigator.pop closes the Riwayat page underneath it. The green guards the pop on the route still being on top.

test/features/transaksi/presentation/widgets/batalkan_setoran_flow_test.dart
testWidgets(
    'while the void is in flight, a tap outside or back keeps the dialog',
    (tester) async {
  api
    ..latency = const Duration(seconds: 1)
    ..on('POST', _batalkan, json: _dibatalkan());
  await pumpFeed(tester);
  await openHapus(tester);
  await tester.enterText(
      find.byKey(BatalkanSetoranDialog.alasanKey), 'Dobel');
  await tester.tap(confirm());
  await tester.pump(const Duration(milliseconds: 100));

  await tester.tapAt(const Offset(5, 5));
  await tester.pump(const Duration(milliseconds: 300));
  await tester.binding.handlePopRoute();
  // Past any dialog exit animation, before the answer arrives.
  await tester.pump(const Duration(milliseconds: 300));

  expect(find.text('Hapus Setoran?'), findsOneWidget);
  await tester.pumpAndSettle(const Duration(seconds: 1));
  expect(find.text('Hapus Setoran?'), findsNothing);
  expect(feed.loads, 1);
  expect(find.byType(AktivitasListView), findsOneWidget);
});

The latency on the stub API is what makes this deterministic. Without it the answer would arrive in the same frame as the tap, and the race could not be staged.

docs.title: E2E (Playwright)
docs.text: PIL-481, 24/24 checks, run against flutter build web --profile and the #167 backend, at 1440×900 and 390×844. Each run creates two fresh setoran and voids one through the UI. It checks the dialog wording, that the voided row leaves the riwayat while the other stays, and that no row is labelled Dibatalkan. Then, through the API and the database, it checks who voided it, the saldo, that the lists omit it, and that its detail by id still answers with the void. The screenshots are in the #238 description.

docs.text:
Evidence for the individual review (IR), organised by competency. Each page states the competency level and the dated evidence behind it, with commit and PR links.

Part B — Hardskills: Best Practice, for Sprint 3 week 3.

What this page covers

docs.title: AI Literacy
docs.text:
Competency level: 3

AI used critically:

  • Claims checked before acting: a teammate's tests were mutated rather than trusted, hashes recomputed rather than read off a screenshot, and a PR's "server-side" claim tested with a real request.
  • Failures not papered over: a scan attempt that ran the machine out of memory was discarded and rerun one scan at a time. A secret leaked by its own earlier work was redacted, the false claim in its report corrected, and the check that missed it extended.
  • Limits kept: no admin bypass of a teammate's open change request; no shared-CI change without an issue; no rewrite of git history to hide the leak.

Decisions with product or team impact were put to me: how to plan the week's PRs, whether to post reviews as comments or approvals, and the rule for review comments after an approval.

Evidence for this week:

  • The PRs, reviews and reports linked below, each of which records the checks described here. The prompts themselves aren't published.

docs.title: Programming
docs.text:
Competency level: 3

Standard principles applied and shown in this week's code:

  • Validation at the boundary, in one place: a shared_kernel helper turns a raw query parameter into a UUID or a keyed 422, so no view hands untrusted text to the ORM.
  • Validate first, then query: two uniqueness checks now run on the validated value instead of the raw body, one moved into its serializer and one after validation in its view. That fixed a NUL crash and a padded-duplicate bypass together.
  • A narrow serializer the wider one extends, so DELETE validates exactly what it reads.
  • A domain rule guarded by a test, not by memory: an architecture test makes tercatat() the only way to say "counted setoran".
  • One lock for every writer of an invariant: profile completion became the fifth writer to take the shared account lock.
  • A navigation policy reused, not rewritten, and Extract Method from a SonarCloud finding.
  • All five SOLID principles, each with the code it applies to. See SOLID in this week's code.

docs.title: The design issues in brief
docs.text:
• One input check written three times, with two copies missing. nasabah_id reached the database unchecked on two lists, so a typo was a server error. Fix: one validator in the shared kernel that every list calls.
  • A rule kept only by memory. tercatat() names "counted setoran", but nothing stopped a new query from writing the filter by hand, and one did. Fix: a test that reads the source and fails on any hand-written copy.
  • Checking one value and saving another. The duplicate-kode check read the raw request before validation, while the save used the cleaned value, so a NUL byte crashed the check and " HDPE " slipped past it. Fix: check after validation, in the serializer.
  • Two verbs validating one field two ways. POST validated the device token properly; DELETE had a hand-written check that missed the NUL byte. Fix: a small serializer for DELETE that the POST one extends.
  • A writer that skipped the shared lock. Profile completion changed the account without the lock the other four writers take, so it could answer with a stale role. Fix: it takes the same lock_account.
  • A page with no way back on web. The role page was pushed, and a push isn't in the browser history. Fix: reuse the onboarding steps' existing back policy, then extract it from build when SonarCloud flagged the complexity.
  • One message worded three ways. The single dialog, the bulk dialog and the toast described a void differently. Fix: one named constant per message.

docs.title: A boundary validator in the shared kernel — 5c2f7fc, b85819a
docs.text:
shared_kernel/parameter.py
"""Validasi parameter query berupa UUID (PIL-482).

Nilai mentah yang bukan UUID membuat ORM memunculkan ValidationError Django,
yang tidak ditangani DRF dan berakhir 500. Seperti `search`, `periode` dan
`tipe`, nilai yang tidak valid dijawab 422 dengan kunci parameternya.
"""

from uuid import UUID

from rest_framework import serializers


def validasi_uuid(nilai: str, *, kunci: str) -> UUID:
    try:
        hasil: UUID = serializers.UUIDField().run_validation(nilai)
    except serializers.ValidationError as exc:
        raise serializers.ValidationError({kunci: exc.detail}) from exc
    return hasil
apps/ledger/views.py
qs = qs.filter(nasabah_id=validasi_uuid(nasabah_id, kunci="nasabah_id"))

The refactor after green moved /aktivitas, which had its own try/except, onto the same helper. All three lists now answer the same 422 for the same input, and a fourth list adds one call rather than another copy. The module sits beside shared_kernel/pencarian.py, which does the same job for search.

docs.title: A rule enforced by a fitness function — b10fffa, 8d1a931
docs.text:
Two weeks ago the counted-setoran rule was named once, as TransaksiQuerySet.tercatat(). A name only helps if every read uses it. Heraldo's re-review of #167 listed waste_categories among the tercatat() paths, although it spelled the filter out by hand. So the rule now has a test that reads the source:

tests/test_architecture.py
TERCATAT_RULE_HOME = APPS_ROOT / "ledger" / "models.py"

def _spelled_out_tercatat_filters(path: Path) -> list[int]:
    lines: list[int] = []
    for node in ast.walk(ast.parse(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"), filename=str(path))):
        if not (
            isinstance(node, ast.Call)
            and isinstance(node.func, ast.Attribute)
            and node.func.attr in {"filter", "exclude"}
        ):
            continue
        for keyword in node.keywords:
            if _names_transaksi_tercatat(keyword.value) or (keyword.arg or "").endswith(
                "transaksi__status"
            ):
                lines.append(keyword.value.lineno)
    return lines

The fix uses the idiom DashboardService.stats already uses:

apps/reporting/services.py
counted = Transaksi.objects.tercatat().filter(
    bank_sampah=bank,
    tipe=Transaksi.Tipe.SETORAN,
    tanggal__range=(start_dt, end_dt),
)
... DetailTransaksi.objects.filter(transaksi__in=counted) ...

Gabriel's review (17 Nov) pointed out that counted now repeats the selection operational_trends builds. That selection was already written twice before this PR, so extracting it is left for a separate change.

    if (
        nomor
        and JenisSampah.objects.filter(bank_sampah=current_bank(request), nomor=nomor)
        .exclude(id=instance.id)
        .exists()
    ):
        return Response({"errors": {"kode": ["Kode sampah sudah digunakan"]}}, status=422)
    return super().update(request, *args, **kwargs)

A NUL byte reached PostgreSQL through that query (500). A padded " HDPE " passed it and was then stripped and saved over another item's kode. The rule now runs in the serializer, after DRF's field validators:

apps/waste_catalog/serializers.py
def validate_kode(self, value: str) -> str:
    value = value.strip()
    # Edit: validator field DRF (termasuk penolak NUL) sudah berjalan, jadi
    # nilai ini aman dipakai untuk cek kode ganda di bank yang sama.
    jenis = self.instance
    if (
        value
        and isinstance(jenis, JenisSampah)
        and JenisSampah.objects.filter(bank_sampah_id=jenis.bank_sampah_id, nomor=value)
        .exclude(pk=jenis.pk)
        .exists()
    ):
        raise serializers.ValidationError("Kode sampah sudah digunakan")
    return value

With the override gone, the viewset is back to the inherited update, so PUT and PATCH follow the same rule. The nasabah edit keeps its check in the view, but now runs it after validation, on the validated kode, next to the view's own no_hp and email checks.

docs.title: A narrow serializer the wider one extends — 1a765f9
docs.text:
apps/notification/views.py
class ForgetDeviceTokenSerializer(serializers.Serializer[Any]):
    # CharField brings DRF's NUL validator, so a crafted token is a 422 and
    # never reaches PostgreSQL.
    token = ...


class DeviceTokenSerializer(ForgetDeviceTokenSerializer):
    platform = ...
apps/notification/views.py
data = ForgetDeviceTokenSerializer(data=request.data)
data.is_valid(raise_exception=True)
DeviceToken.objects.filter(
    user=current_user(request), token=data.validated_data["token"]
).delete()

DELETE asks for the token only. POST adds the platform. Both validate the token with the same field, where the hand-written check had missed the NUL byte.

docs.title: A fifth writer under the shared lock — 51a631e
docs.text:
apps/authentication/services.py
# A completed profile commits the account to its role, so this takes
# the role-change lock too (PIL-451). The reload also means the
# checks below, and the role the caller answers with, are the
# account's current ones, not those of the object the request loaded.
OnboardingService.lock_account(user)

This is the fifth writer of "a completed profile or a linked membership locks the role". The other four already go through lock_account, so the lock policy stays in one method, and every writer depends on that method rather than on its own select_for_update.

docs.title: A reused navigation policy, and Extract Method — ef55977, a363412
One home for each message — 77e612e
SOLID in this week's code
docs.text: Principle Where How Single responsibility validasi_uuid; validate_kode; lock_account The helper only turns a raw parameter into a UUID or a keyed 422, and the views keep only their query. The serializer owns field rules, so the view no longer validates. The lock policy lives in one method. Open/closed validasi_uuid; tercatat(); handleOnboardingStepPop A new list adds a call, not another try/except. A new counted status changes tercatat() only, and the fitness test makes sure nothing bypasses it. The step-pop policy is reused unchanged. Liskov substitution DeviceTokenSerializer(ForgetDeviceTokenSerializer); the jenis sampah viewset The wider serializer is the narrow one plus platform, so it validates a token exactly as DELETE does. With the update override gone, the viewset honours the inherited ModelViewSet contract again. Interface segregation ForgetDeviceTokenSerializer DELETE asks only for the token, not for the platform it doesn't use. Dependency inversion Every writer of the role invariant → OnboardingService.lock_account The writers depend on the one lock abstraction, not on a hand-written select_for_update. The race tests drive them through it.

docs.title: Patterns, labelled as what they are
docs.text:
• Query Object / Specification (PoEAA): tercatat(). Its enforcement by a test is a fitness function, from evolutionary architecture, not a GoF pattern.
  • Pessimistic lock (PoEAA, Pessimistic Offline Lock, here as a row lock inside a transaction): lock_account.
  • Template Method (GoF, behavioural): DRF's run_validation is the template, and it calls the validate_<field> hooks after the field validators. Moving the duplicate-kode check into the validate_kode hook is what makes it run on the cleaned value, after the NUL check.
  • Plain inheritance between DRF serializers: DeviceTokenSerializer extends the narrow one and adds a field. No design pattern is claimed for it.
  • Extract Method (Fowler): _backToProfile.

docs.title: Security
docs.text:
Competency level: 3

Level 3: a scan, explained, with a patch plan. Each new PR this week, #175, #176 and #177, got its own OWASP ZAP 2.17.0 scan, run one at a time after the first attempt ran out of memory. They ran signed in, against my own local instances, with fresh seeded databases and backends started with an empty environment. Report: ZAP scans per sub-issue, 17 Nov.

  • 0 High and no new finding. Every alert is one already on record, and the report says which.
  • The 9 Nov finding verified fixed, not assumed: ZAP sent 965 malformed nasabah_id values to /transaksi and /pencairan. All 965 got 422, none 500, where the 9 Nov scan had 226 500s. The two false High alerts they caused didn't come back.
  • Every 5xx in the three backend logs read and classified: the only 500s were the known debug-only browsable-API crash.
  • A limit reported, not hidden: DELETE /device-tokens/ couldn't be actively scanned (ZAP has no GET node for it). Its NUL case is covered by the drive module and #177's tests, and the tooling fix is in the plan.

Level 2 is also met by the commits: five OWASP categories are genuinely guarded, each with a test or a check behind it: A03, A04, A05, A08 and A09.

My own leak, found and fixed (13 Nov): two Discord webhooks in my 9 Nov scan evidence were redacted, and the scan script now refuses to finish when it finds a secret.

docs.title: My own leak, and what changed (13 Nov)
docs.text:
The 9 Nov scan caught a Django debug page that lists the whole environment of the dev machine, and that environment held two Discord webhooks (DISCORD_REVIEW_WEBHOOK_URL, DISCORD_QA_WEBHOOK_URL). I had redacted the computer and user names from the evidence, not these, and the report said I had grepped for secrets, which wasn't true for webhooks. GitHub's secret scanning found them, and Discord revoked both.

2197468 (pilah-docs):

  • The evidence: the two PIL-481 files carry [REDACTED], and the JSON stays valid. The other credentials in the dump were already masked by Django. The other reports' evidence is clean.
  • The check: tools/zap_scan.py now refuses to finish on Discord and Slack webhooks, GitHub, Google and Slack tokens, and database URLs with a password, not only bearer tokens and JWTs. I confirmed it flags the original file and none of the current evidence.
  • The cause: from the 17 Nov scans on, each backend starts with an empty environment (env -i plus only the variables it needs), so no secret of the machine can reach a debug page.
  • The record: the report's false claim is corrected, and the leak is in its "What went wrong" section. The old commit still holds the dead URLs, since history wasn't rewritten.

docs.title: OWASP guards in this week's code
docs.text:
OWASP category Guard Test or check Commits A03 Injection Untrusted input is validated before it reaches a query: a nasabah_id must be a UUID, and a kode or device token can't carry a NUL byte into PostgreSQL 3 endpoints × 3 malformed ids → 422; a NUL in kode on two edit paths and in the token → 422 5699fff, 5c2f7fc, 04ab0bb, d3b1bea, 1a765f9 A04 Insecure Design Malformed input is a client error, not a crash. A completed profile and a role change can't interleave: profile completion takes the same account lock as every other writer of the invariant The 422 tests; a two-thread race test on PostgreSQL, and the reverse ordering single-threaded 9424d9f, 870224d, 51a631e A05 Security Misconfiguration No secret of the machine reaches published evidence: the scan backends run with an empty environment, and the scan fails if a secret pattern appears in its output The scan script flags the original leaked file and passes the current evidence 2197468 (pilah-docs) A08 Software and Data Integrity Failures Every total reads the same counted subset, enforced by a test that reads the source. A padded duplicate kode can no longer slip past the uniqueness check and overwrite another item's kode The architecture test (fails on any hand-written filter); the padded-duplicate tests on both edit paths b10fffa, 8d1a931, a56eba9, e7ef617 A09 Security Logging and Monitoring Failures The role-change audit trail holds only changes that happened: a role change refused under the lock writes no UserRoleChangeLog row The race harness asserts no log row after a refused change 870224d, 51a631e

Labels I don't count. The commits also name:

  • A01: "the filter still runs inside the bank scope", "the delete stays limited to the caller's tokens". That scoping is unchanged code, and no new test asserts it.
  • A07: "the logout path that forgets a push token cannot be made to crash". That's a robustness fix more than an authentication control.
  • A02: in the leak fix. The control there is the A05 one above.

docs.title: Test Driven Development
docs.text:
Competency level: 4

Level 3 met: every behaviour this week was built test-first, with the phase in every commit subject. The green steps came only after their [RED] commits, and [REFACTOR] commits only after green.

  • Every changed line is covered: 100% on SonarCloud for every MR with lines to cover.
  • The tests cover the positive case, each refusal and the corner cases (see the table).
  • Guard tests that pass in their red commit are there on purpose, and the commit says so.

Level 4: advanced testing methods in the commits:

  • An architecture fitness function: a test that parses every module under apps/ with Python's ast and fails on any query that spells out the counted-setoran rule by hand. On staging it failed on exactly one line.
  • A real race, made deterministic: a two-thread TransactionTestCase on PostgreSQL pauses a profile completion inside User.save, runs a role change in between, and asserts the change waited and was refused.
  • An HTTP contract test over three endpoints: one test drives /aktivitas, /transaksi and /pencairan with the same malformed ids, as sub-tests, so a fourth list can join with one line.
  • Mutation testing in review: on Gabriel's PIL-478 pair I put code back on purpose (10 mutants, 6 caught) and reported, with the test that would catch each, the ones that got through. See Team Development Management.

docs.title: Mocks, stubs and fakes in this week's tests
docs.text:
A test double stands in for a real collaborator so that a test controls it. A stub gives fixed answers, a mock is a generated stand-in for an interface, and a spy wraps or records the real thing. Each double below has one job, and the code under test around it is real.

Double Kind Replaces Why it's needed Used in patch.object(User, "save", paused) Spy (unittest.mock) that wraps the real save Nothing: the real save still runs, only later The wrapper signals that the first thread reached its write, then waits on a threading.Event before calling the original. That gives the second thread, the role change, an exact moment to run in. Without it a race test would pass or fail by luck The #137 race test, test_a_role_change_waits_for_a_profile_being_completed client.force_authenticate(user) Stub (DRF test client) JWT authentication It signs the request in as a given user object, without issuing a token. On #137 it passes a stale user loaded before the role change, which is exactly the situation the bug needs #137 test_a_profile_saved_after_a_role_change_answers_for_the_new_role; the #175 and #177 HTTP tests TestAuthenticationNotifier Fake and spy The real authentication notifier It holds a fixed signed-in account and records every call (auth.calls). The Kembali test asserts that going back calls neither changeRole nor logout The #174 Kembali test _MockDataSource Mock (mocktail) OnboardingRemoteDataSource, the API client The onboarding notifier needs one to be built, and the test must not reach a network The #174 role-page tests pumpRouted(..., extraRoutes: ['/complete-profile', ...]) Stub routes The real Lengkapi Profil and login pages Each extra route renders a placeholder reading route:/complete-profile, so the test checks where Kembali goes without building the whole profile screen The #174 Kembali test

Where nothing is faked, on purpose. #175, #176 and #177 run on a real test database. The bugs were real database behaviour: PostgreSQL refusing a NUL byte, and the ORM raising on a malformed UUID. The architecture test in #176 reads the real source files. Faking either would hide the very thing being tested.

tests/regression/identity/test_role_change_race.py
def test_a_role_change_waits_for_a_profile_being_completed(self) -> None:
    # Review on #137 (Tristan P2): completing the profile commits the
    # account to its role, so a role change arriving mid-save must wait
    # for it and then be refused.
    user = User.objects.create_user(email="race-profile@example.com", role=User.Role.PENGELOLA)

    outcome = self._race(
        user,
        lambda u: OnboardingService.complete_profile(
            u, {"nama": "Ayu", "no_hp": "+628111111115"}
        ),
        (User, "save"),
        User.Role.NASABAH,
    )

    self._assert_role_kept(user, User.Role.PENGELOLA, outcome)
    self.assertTrue(user.is_profile_complete)

Mutant Caught? Review

Competency level: 3

AI used critically:

docs.text: Situation What happened 18 Nov: Gabriel's comments on #175 and #176, after Heraldo's approvals It applied the 12 Nov scope rule: each point was checked against the issue and answered in its thread with the reason, with permalinks to the code in question. Then the approved PRs were merged. 19 Nov: Commitment for Sprint 3 Weeks 2 and 3 The measured time came to 8 h 29 min and 9 h 32 min. It wrote level 1 for both weeks rather than rounding up, and asked me which self-reported time to add instead of assuming. 19 – 21 Nov: Checking the S3W2 and S3W3 pages and script against the sources Wrong figures were found and corrected before they were presented. Examples: a count of tests that was two, not "a dozen"; merge times given in UTC instead of WIB; an OWASP category listed as guarded in a week where nothing tested it; two names used for the same teammate; a broken anchor. 21 Nov: "Which TDD work is before the deadline?" It dated every commit and SonarCloud analysis against each week's due Tuesday, and checked whether any app commit sat outside a PR. The only one was a docs commit, and the page says so. 23 Nov: The first ZAP run ZAP reported "URL Not Found in the Scan Tree" for POST /onboarding/nasabah, the endpoint the feature depends on. It didn't report a clean scan. It scanned the path by hand, fixed the driver, rebuilt the database and reran everything. 23 Nov: Counting the attacks A first draft said 227. Recounted from the backend's own log, which sees every request ZAP sent, it was 224 attacks plus the drive's four POSTs, and the report says 224. 23 Nov: The scratch PostgreSQL stopped It owned the mistake: it had deleted the lock file of a server still in recovery. It recorded that in the report's "What went wrong" and in memory, so the next scan waits for "ready" instead. 23 Nov: Heraldo's five follow-ups on #276 Each was checked against the code and the issue's scope. None could create a wrong record, because the server refuses a duplicate, which the scan had just confirmed. So none was fixed in the PR, and each got its reason in the reply. 23 Nov: The conflict after #267 landed It kept both sides instead of picking one: staging's new onboarding layout, and #276's in-app page. Then it reran the 413 affected tests before pushing.

docs.title: Programming
docs.text:
Competency level: 3

Standard principles applied and shown in this week's code, all in pilah-mobile #276 (PIL-539):

  • One form, a layout per context: a mode parameter chooses between the onboarding step and an in-app page, and the form fields and submit button are extracted once and shared (Extract Method).
  • Show state, not absence: the bank picker gets the reason a bank is unavailable together with its id, and disables the row instead of filtering it out.
  • A narrow submit for a narrow context: applying from inside the app sends only the application, through the notifier's existing request method.
  • An existing convention reused: the list reloads when the page it pushed returns true, as the detail page's appeal already does.
  • The server stays the authority: the app drops its one-bank lock for this flow, and pilah-be #185 pins the server rules it relies on.
  • Design tokens for the spacing in the code this PR moved.
  • SOLID, each principle with the code it applies to. See SOLID in this week's code.

docs.title: The design issues in brief
docs.text:
• No way in. The backend already allowed a second membership, but an approved nasabah had no screen to apply from. Fix: "Ajukan bank baru" on Bank sampah saya.
  • One screen hard-wired to one context. The registration form was an onboarding step: its stepper, its Keluar (log out) exit and its one-membership lock would all have applied to a signed-in nasabah applying from the app. Fix: a mode parameter, with the form shared by both layouts.
  • A picker that hid things without saying why. Joined banks were silently dropped, so a nasabah looking for their own bank found nothing. A set of ids couldn't say why a bank was unavailable. Fix: pass a map from id to its status label, and disable the row.
  • One submit path shaped by onboarding. It sent the profile draft, refreshed the session and followed the onboarding redirect, which would have moved a signed-in nasabah away from the page they came from. Fix: a second, narrow submit for the in-app context.
  • Literal spacing in touched code. Fix: the spacing tokens, as the design guide asks for code being touched.

docs.title: Before and after
docs.text: What Pattern Before After The difference it made Registration form (8cb88a0) Mode parameter choosing the layout, with Extract Method (Fowler) for the shared parts RegisterNasabahScreen was only an OnboardingStepScaffold step, with a stepper, Keluar and the lock RegisterNasabahMode { onboarding, additional }. build picks _additionalPage or _onboardingStep; both use _formFields() and _submitButton() The in-app page has a back button and no lock, and onboarding is unchanged: its tests didn't move Bank picker (6a4c4ed) No design pattern: a principle (show state; Information Expert) excludedBankIds, a set of ids; joined banks were removed from the list joinedBanks, a map from id to "Sudah tergabung", "Menunggu persetujuan" or "Pernah ditolak". The row stays, greyed, with a status badge and no onTap The nasabah sees their banks and why each can't be picked again Submitting from the app (b34db8b) No design pattern: SRP (each context owns its after-submit step), DRY (one request method) One _onSubmit: profile draft, then the application, then refreshUser and the onboarding redirect In additional mode, _applyToAnotherBank calls registerNasabah only, pops true and toasts after navigation No profile resent, no session touched, and the nasabah lands back where they started Reloading the list (9c7ecac) Convention reuse (push, then refresh on true), not a new callback No entry point context.push<bool>(...).then((applied) { if (applied == true) load(silent: true); }) The new pending application appears without a spinner, and going back without applying reloads nothing Spacing (41a4434) Design tokens 24, 16, 12, 8 written as numbers AppSpacing.xl, .lg, .md, .sm. The two 20s have no step on the scale, so they stay, and the layout doesn't move The touched code follows the design guide; the 130 onboarding page tests pass before and after

docs.title: SOLID in this week's code
docs.text: Principle Where How Single responsibility The list's _applyToAnotherBank; the form's _applyToAnotherBank; _joinedLabel The list only navigates and refreshes. Each context's submit owns its own after-submit step. The screen maps a status to its label, and the sheet only displays it. Open/closed RegisterNasabahMode; PilihBankSampahBottomSheet The in-app context was added as a new mode, leaving the onboarding step and its tests unchanged. The sheet renders any label it's given, so a new status needs no change to it. Liskov substitution Both layouts of RegisterNasabahScreen Wherever the screen is used, it keeps one contract: it validates the picked bank, sends one application and reports the server's answer. Only the frame around the form differs. Interface segregation RegisterNasabahRequest(bankSampahId:) The in-app submit sends only the bank id, not the profile fields the onboarding path also carries. Dependency inversion Both submits → OnboardingNotifier.registerNasabah; the list → nasabahApprovalProvider The pages depend on the notifiers' methods, not on the API client, which is why the tests can mock the data source and fake the notifiers.

docs.title: Patterns, labelled as what they are
docs.text:
• Extract Method (Fowler): _formFields() and _submitButton(), shared by both layouts.
  • A mode parameter, not a GoF pattern: the screen chooses its layout from an enum. A Strategy object would be heavier than two layouts need.
  • Information Expert (GRASP): the screen, which holds the memberships, names their status.
  • Design tokens: AppSpacing.
  • Convention reuse: push, then refresh on true. No pattern is claimed for it.

docs.title: Security
docs.text:
Competency level: 3

Level 3: a scan, explained, with a patch plan. PIL-539 got its own OWASP ZAP 2.17.0 scan right after it was finished, on 23 Nov. It's the first scan signed in as a nasabah rather than the demo Pengurus, because the flow is the nasabah's. It ran against my own local instance, with a fresh seeded database and a backend started with an empty environment. Report: ZAP scan of PIL-539, 23 Nov.

  • 0 High and no new finding. Every alert is one already on record, and the report says which.
  • The endpoint that matters was actually attacked: 224 attacks on POST /api/v1/onboarding/nasabah, with the real body. None got a 5xx, and none created a membership: afterwards the nasabah has exactly the two rows the drive made.
  • A gap in the tooling found and fixed: the first run left that endpoint unscanned, because ZAP can't find a path that only ever saw POST. tools/zap_scan.py now scans such a path from its recorded request. This closes the limit reported on 17 Nov.
  • Every 5xx in the backend log read and classified: the debug-only browsable-API crash (already on record, now seen on the nasabah's riwayat) and the local Google sign-in, which has no client id.

The commits name what they guard: #185's tests name A01 (only the second bank's pengurus decides; a pending membership opens no saldo) and A04 (one membership per bank, enforced on the server). #276 names A04: the client sends only a bank id, and who applies comes from the session.

docs.title: The ZAP scan
docs.text:
Target staging at 80a30aa, the #185 merge, on 127.0.0.1:8539 Database Scratch PostgreSQL 16 database zap539, created fresh and filled by seed_testing_data, plus a second active bank sampah to apply to. No real user data Signed in as customer.demo@example.com, the seeded nasabah, approved at one bank Environment DEBUG=true, started with env -i plus only the variables it needs

The drive module sends the flow's real requests through ZAP's proxy, so the active scan has real ids and a real body to attack:

Request Answer GET /api/v1/nasabah/me 200, one approved membership GET /api/v1/bank-sampah 200, the directory POST /api/v1/onboarding/nasabah with the second bank 201, pending the same again; then the nasabah's own bank 400, "Anda sudah terdaftar sebagai nasabah di bank sampah ini" with bank_sampah_id: "bukan-uuid" 422 GET /api/v1/nasabah/me/saldo?keanggotaan_id=<pending> 403: a pending membership can't open its saldo

docs.text: Path Requests Answers POST /api/v1/onboarding/nasabah 228: 224 attacks and the drive's four 207 × 422, 19 × 400, 1 × 404 and one 201, the drive's own. No 5xx and no extra membership /api/v1/nasabah/me and children about 4,000 200, 403, 404, 405, 422 and 3 × 429 (the per-user throttle). 3 × 500, the known debug-only crash /api/v1/bank-sampah and children about 2,490 Every write a nasabah tried was refused: 1,926 × 403 on PUT and 6 on POST Earlier finding Status after this scan 9 Nov 3 / 2 Nov 2: the browsable API crashes on list views without a queryset Still open, debug-only. Seen again on NasabahHistoryView; it joins patch plan item 1 26 Oct 2: CSP wildcard directive Still open 17 Nov limit: a POST- or DELETE-only path can't be actively scanned Fixed in the tooling in this scan

docs.text: # Fix Test first OWASP Status (24 Nov) 1 renderer_classes = [JSONRenderer] on the nasabah history view Accept: text/html on /nasabah/me/riwayat under DEBUG=True gets 200 or 406, not 500 A05 Planned, low priority (debug-only) 2 tools/zap_scan.py scans a POST- or DELETE-only path from its recorded request Rescan: the path is attacked (224 attack requests in the log) — Done (23 Nov) — 26 Oct finding 2 As in that plan A05 Still open on staging

docs.title: What went wrong on the way
docs.text:
• The first run left the endpoint that matters unscanned. ZAP refused it with "URL Not Found in the Scan Tree". I started that scan by hand through ZAP's API with the method and body, then fixed the script to do it itself, rebuilt the database and reran everything. The report is from the rerun.
  • The driver's log line was wrong. It always said it had signed in as the demo Pengurus. It now names the account the token belongs to.
  • I stopped the scratch PostgreSQL by mistake by deleting its lock file while it was recovering. It restarted cleanly, with its log outside the data directory, before any scan request was sent.

docs.title: OWASP categories in this week's commits
docs.text:
Category Guarded by Check A01 Broken Access Control #185 b97596a, 499b32b, 2abe793 The first bank's pengurus gets 404 deciding the second bank's application; a pending membership's saldo is 403; each approved bank's saldo is its own A04 Insecure Design #185 261a571, c2014bd; #276 874d72c, b34db8b One membership per bank is enforced on the server (400 on a duplicate), and the app sends only a bank id, so removing the client's lock opens nothing

Two categories this week, both with a test behind them. Level 2 (five categories) isn't met by this week's commits alone. Level 3 rests on the scan.

docs.title: Test Driven Development
docs.text:
Competency level: 4

Level 3 met: the new behaviour this week was built test-first, with the phase in every commit subject. In pilah-mobile #276 each [GREEN] commit came only after its [RED] commit, and the [REFACTOR] only after green.

  • Every changed line is covered: SonarCloud reports 100% of #276's 72 new lines. pilah-be #185 adds tests only, so it has no lines to cover.
  • The tests cover the positive case, each refusal and the corner cases (see the table).
  • #185 has no red phase, on purpose. Its five tests pin behaviour the backend already had, for the app to rely on. They passed when written, so their subjects carry no [RED] tag, and the PR description says so.

Level 4: advanced testing methods, for test isolation:

  • A mock and two fakes (mocktail): the onboarding API client is a mock, and two request types are fakes registered as fallback values, so any() can match them.
  • Two recording test notifiers: one records each load call with its silent flag, the other each authentication call. The tests assert what was not called (no refreshUser, no logout), not only what was.
  • A real router, isolated: a GoRouter built on the app's own rootNavigatorKey, so the toast raised after navigation has a navigator, as it does in the app.

docs.title: Mocks, stubs and fakes in this week's tests
docs.text:
A test double stands in for a real collaborator so that a test controls it. A stub gives fixed answers, a mock is a generated stand-in for an interface, a fake is a working stand-in, and a spy records how it was called. Each double below has one job, and the code under test around it is real.

Double Kind Replaces Why it's needed Used in _MockOnboardingDataSource Mock (mocktail) OnboardingRemoteDataSource, the API client Each test sets the answer to registerNasabah and loadMyMemberships: a membership list, a 201, or the server's duplicate refusal. No network is reached. verify(...).captured.single shows exactly one application was sent, for the picked bank, and verifyNever(completeProfile) that no profile was register_nasabah_additional_test.dart _FakeRegisterNasabahRequest, _FakeCompleteProfileRequest Fakes (mocktail) The two request objects mocktail needs a fallback value of each type before any() can match it. Registering them is what lets one test assert that no profile request was sent register_nasabah_additional_test.dart TestNasabahApprovalNotifier Fake and spy NasabahApprovalNotifier It starts from a fixed list state and records every load, with its silent flag, in loadCalls. The test asserts [true] after a submitted application and [] after going back without one ajukan_bank_baru_test.dart TestAuthenticationNotifier Fake and spy The authentication notifier It holds a signed-in nasabah and records calls in auth.calls. Two tests assert that back and system back never call logout, and one that the in-app submit doesn't call refreshUser register_nasabah_additional_test.dart A stub route at /ajukan-bank-sampah Stub route The real registration form It shows a "submitted" button that pops true. The list page's reload is tested on its own, without building the form ajukan_bank_baru_test.dart A GoRouter on rootNavigatorKey The real router, built for the test The app's router router.push<bool>(...) returns the page's result to the test, as it does to Bank sampah saya. The app's rootNavigatorKey is needed because the "Pengajuan terkirim" toast is raised after navigation, on that navigator register_nasabah_additional_test.dart

Where nothing is faked, on purpose. #185 runs on a real test database and signs in with real JWTs. The rules it pins live in the database and the services: one membership row per bank, a pending membership's saldo refused, each bank's pengurus deciding only its own applications. Faking any of them would test nothing.

docs.text:
Competency level: 1

I didn't review a teammate's merge request this week (18 – 24 Nov). The rubric scores this competency on reviews given to other members' MRs, so the week is claimed at the lowest level. The last reviews I gave were Gabriel's PIL-478 pair and his #174, in Sprint 3 Week 3.

docs.title: AI Literacy
docs.text:
Competency level: 3

AI used critically: its claims checked against the code, GitHub and logs before being acted on, its direction corrected where it drifted from team decisions, and the prompt history published with personal data removed.

docs.title: How AI was used
docs.text:
• Tool: Claude Code as an agent in VS Code, across pilah-be, pilah-mobile, pilah-docs and Linear (through Composio): reading code, running tests and CI-equivalent checks, committing, opening PRs, replying to reviews.
  • Guardrails: the workspace skills (tdd, ship, ask-for-review), CI on Postgres, and standing rules I gave it this week and asked it to remember: phase-tagged TDD commits, replying inside each review thread, never merging branches (the lead does), and 3P updates in Bahasa.
  • My role: relaying and deciding requirements with the PO and lead, choosing between options it laid out, approving outward actions (pushes, PR comments, Linear edits), and asking "are you sure?" when a claim mattered.

docs.title: 24–28 Sep — where verification changed the outcome
docs.text: Situation What verification found The AI told me my pencairan PRs were not merged, because my commit SHAs were not on staging I asked "are you sure?". Rechecked through the PRs themselves: all six were merged that morning, squashed by the lead into one commit per repository, so my SHAs could never appear. Confirmed by content too: the staging API answers 401, not 404, on the new routes. The AI saved the rule "check PR state, not SHA ancestry" The AI's reading of the PO's "7-day" rule combined two limits (an edit window and a backdating limit) I corrected it: follow the PO's answers only. The Linear decisions were rewritten to her wording before any code was written Recording a PR comment promising to merge #19 into my stacked #32 I stopped it: merges belong to the lead. The comment was edited and the rule saved A Discord agreement to adopt a teammate's IsActiveNasabah class Checked against the code instead of taking the chat at face value: staging already had an equivalent IsNasabahRole, and JWT authentication already rejects inactive users, so the extra is_active check added nothing. The agreement was out of date before anyone acted on it Four review findings from the lead on #19 Each was reproduced before being fixed: the red tests showed history at Rp 7.001 against a stored Rp 7.000,50, a backdated payout accepted with 201, and a nasabah refused with 403 A local test failed after merging staging Diagnosed as my local .env enabling debug mode, and proved by rerunning with .env moved aside, instead of "fixing" a correct test #19's diff coverage read 97% Every uncovered line was traced with git blame to code merged in from staging by other members; the four fixes themselves are fully covered, and the page says exactly that rather than claiming 97% or 100% A production database dump pasted into the chat for migration testing The AI flagged that it held real names, emails, phone numbers and unexpired refresh tokens; it is kept out of every repository, and it is removed entirely from the published prompt history below Test counts drafted for the IR pages The AI caught its own error before publishing: the mobile baseline was 278, not 270, so PIL-230 added 16 tests, not 24 The emulator "just closed" Diagnosed from the emulator's verbose log (12 GB needed, 2.9 GB free on C:) instead of reinstalling; the invisible window was found at y = −947 and moved on screen A chat export offered as AI-literacy evidence Checked before use: it held only a startup banner from another session, so the history was built from this session's own transcript instead

docs.title: Example: challenging "your PRs are not merged yet"
docs.text:
When I asked whether I could test my features with the release APK, the AI answered confidently that my pencairan PRs were not on staging: its check looked for my own commit SHAs there and found none.

That contradicted what I knew from the team (the lead had said he was merging my stack), so I asked it directly: "Are you sure my pencairan feats not merged yet?"

Rechecking through the PRs themselves instead of through git ancestry showed:

  • All six PRs (backend #19, #32, #52 and mobile #26, #27, #33) had been merged that morning. The lead squash-merged each stack into one commit (da13b32, 41ccced), which is exactly why my original SHAs could never appear on staging.
  • The code was live: the staging API answered 401 (login required) on /api/v1/pencairan and /pencairan/:id/riwayat, where an unmerged route would answer 404.
  • The latest staging APK already contained the features, so I could test that day instead of waiting.

The AI acknowledged the mistake plainly ("I was wrong") and recorded the lesson as a standing rule: check merge state through the PR, then confirm by content, never by commit ancestry alone.

docs.title: Example: deciding instead of accepting the first design
docs.text:
PIL-230 first said only "edit pencairan". The AI's first analysis laid out three options (edit only non-money fields, correct through reversal entries as the SDS's append-only rule suggests, or edit in place) and pointed out the conflict with the SDS. I did not pick from that list on my own: I took the open questions to the PO and lead, the lead and PO disagreed on whether nasabah see old versions, and I chose the PO's version with the lead's approval. The AI then turned the decisions into a design and asked me where the answers still left room:

  • Should a backdated new payout be validated at its date, or rejected before the nasabah's last activity? I chose rejecting, which keeps every receipt exact.
  • May a pengurus edit a pencairan of a nasabah who is no longer active? I chose yes, and asked whether it could change later; the check lives in one query.
  • Should recomputed later pencairan be marked as edited? I chose no.

docs.title: Code Quality
docs.text:
Competency level: 3

Every CI quality check passes on the PIL-222 and PIL-230 PRs, and I traced why the mobile SonarQube project reports nothing at all. SonarQube found two maintainability issues on my serializer code; both were fixed test-first in pilah-be #67, now merged, and pilah-be-staging shows no open issue authored by me.

docs.title: Automated checks in CI, all passing
docs.text:
Backend (#32): ruff check, ruff format --check, mypy --strict, makemigrations --check, manage.py check --deploy, coverage ≥ 80% (91%, diff coverage 100%).

Mobile (#27): flutter analyze --fatal-infos, dart format --set-exit-if-changed, coverage and diff-coverage gates (35.3% overall, 87.5% diff).

PIL-230, backend (#52): the same checks as #32, all passing in CI on Postgres; 92% overall, 100% diff coverage.

PIL-230, mobile (#33): dart format, flutter analyze --fatal-infos clean, 294 tests; 37.8% overall, 82.8% diff coverage. Run locally on Flutter 3.38.3, the CI version.

docs.title: Quality of the change itself
docs.text:
The period filter was shared, not copied. The transaksi list already had the date-range logic, so it was generalised with a TypeVar bound to Model and reused, instead of duplicating four period branches:

_Dated = TypeVar("_Dated", bound=Model)

def apply_period(queryset: QuerySet[_Dated], request: HttpRequest,
                 default: str | None = "hari_ini") -> QuerySet[_Dated]:

All 68 pre-existing transaksi period tests still pass, which is what makes the generalisation safe to claim.

docs.title: Diagnosing the mobile SonarQube project
docs.text:
The SonarQube check on #27 failed, and the mobile dashboard showed "The main branch has no lines of code". Rather than re-running until it passed, I read the logs:

  1. The failed run never reached the server — Connect timed out on its first call to /api/server/version. A re-run passed, so that was infrastructure, not code.
  2. The passing run still analysed nothing: 210 files indexed, then 0 languages detected. The scanner only looked for Java and Docker files.
  3. The same holds on #26 and on other team members' PRs, so the mobile project has never analysed Dart. The server has no Dart analyser.

Consequence for this claim: a "0 issues" screenshot from the mobile project would be meaningless, so it is not used as evidence. The enforced static analysis for mobile is flutter analyze --fatal-infos in CI, which fails the build on infos as well as warnings. Reported to the team so the server can be fixed.

docs.title: Backend SonarQube
docs.text:
Two issues on pilah-be-staging land on my code, both rule S1192 (duplicated string literal, Maintainability, High) in api/serializers.py:

Root cause. "bank_sampah.id" and "dicatat_oleh.id" were already repeated as source paths across other members' serializers. My PencairanDetailSerializer (from #19) added one more of each, which pushed both to Sonar's threshold of 3, and Sonar reports at the first occurrence, which is my line.

Fix: pilah-be #67, merged 29 Sep.

Step Commit Pin the output first: 4 tests fix bank_sampah_id / dicatat_oleh in all five serializers that use the paths 80a1aa1 Define each path once (_BANK_SAMPAH_ID, _DICATAT_OLEH_ID) and use it at all 7 places c177fa8

The pin tests were checked to guard the change: pointing _DICATAT_OLEH_ID at the wrong field made 2 of them fail. 255 tests pass locally with ruff and format clean.

Status (29 Sep): fixed and merged. #67 was rebased onto staging after #66 fixed the unrelated seed_testing_data.py mypy errors, passed every check, and was merged at 15:25 WIB (88f4155). SonarQube's next analysis of pilah-be-staging shows no open issue authored by me: the Author facet lists only the other five team members across the 25 remaining issues.

The setup gaps I found are on the week 1 page.

docs.title: Quality of the PIL-230 change
docs.text:
• No N+1 on the list. The two new per-row fields would have added one query each per row. They are annotated on the queryset instead, and a test pins the query count (0ea7252 → 7bceb58); details on the Programming page.
  • No copied rules. Recording and editing share the nominal and tanggal validators, on both backend and mobile (PencairanValidator.nominalEdit states why the edit check is weaker: the backend replay is the authority on saldo).
  • Generated code kept out of the diff. build_runner rewrites the whole of di.config.dart on Windows. Committing that would have buried two real registrations in 68 lines of reordering, so only the two new gh.factory registrations were added.
  • Tests placed to avoid conflicts. PIL-230's backend tests are in a new api/test_pencairan_edit.py, since four other open PRs append to api/tests.py.

Heraldo reviewed all three open PRs and raised eight findings. Every one was verified against the code first, then fixed test-first and answered inside its own review thread:

PR Commits pilah-mobile #26 37ecee5 → d1c7ba8 pilah-mobile #27 8358c87 → a6cdfe6 pilah-be #32 28fca9c
