docs.title: Security scan — PILAH backend, 14 Oct 2026
docs.text:
A dynamic security scan of the PILAH backend (pilah-be) with Metasploit Framework 6.5.3, plus targeted manual verification and a cross-check against Django's own check --deploy. Run for the IR Security competency (a Metasploit-or-similar scan, explained, with a patch plan).

Scope and authorisation

Scanned my own local instance only: manage.py runserver on 127.0.0.1:8001, reached from WSL at http://172.19.64.1:8001, against the seeded test database (no real user data). The deployed staging/production hosts were not scanned. The server ran with DEBUG=true, so some findings below are dev-only and are labelled as such — they would not appear under production settings (DEBUG=false).

docs.title: Method
docs.text:
Step Tool Fingerprint, headers, robots, methods, directory enumeration Metasploit auxiliary/scanner/http/* Header and endpoint verification (full header set, auth checks, sensitive paths) curl Static configuration cross-check python manage.py check --deploy

Full Metasploit console output: metasploit-output-2026-10-14.txt.

docs.title: Why Metasploit found little, and why that is itself a result
docs.text: Metasploit is built to exploit known vulnerabilities in known software — an unpatched service, a vulnerable CMS plugin, a specific library CVE. PILAH's backend is a bespoke Django / DRF application, so Metasploit has no exploit module that matches it. Its HTTP auxiliary scanners could still do reconnaissance — fingerprint the server, read the headers, enumerate directories — and confirm there is no exploitable off-the-shelf service here. The findings that matter are application- and configuration-level, and those came from reading the headers Metasploit dumped and from targeted manual probing. A clean Metasploit result is a meaningful result: the attack surface is a custom API, not a stack of exploitable components.

docs.title: Findings
docs.text: # Finding OWASP (2021) Severity Scope 1 API schema and Swagger UI served without authentication A01 / A05 Medium prod + dev 2 HSTS not configured (SECURE_HSTS_SECONDS unset) A05 Low–Medium prod 3 App-layer HTTPS redirect not enforced (SECURE_SSL_REDIRECT unset) A05 Low prod 4 No Content-Security-Policy or Permissions-Policy header A05 Low prod + dev 5 Server banner leaks framework and Python version A05 Info dev (reduced in prod) 6 DEBUG=true error pages leak the URL configuration A05 Medium if deployed dev-only 7 Session/CSRF cookies without the Secure flag A05 — dev-only

docs.title: 1. API schema and docs are public — Medium, prod-affecting
docs.text:
GET /api/schema/ and GET /api/docs/ both return 200 with no authentication:

$ curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" http://127.0.0.1:8001/api/schema/   # 200
$ curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" http://127.0.0.1:8001/api/docs/      # 200

Both views are registered with no permission restriction:

config/urls.py
path("api/schema/", SpectacularAPIView.as_view(), name="schema"),
path("api/docs/", SpectacularSwaggerView.as_view(url_name="schema"), name="swagger-ui"),

drf-spectacular defaults to AllowAny, so the complete API contract — every endpoint, every parameter, every request and response schema — is published to anyone. For an application that handles customer PII and money movements, that is free reconnaissance: an attacker learns the whole surface without a single credential. This is not gated by DEBUG; it is in the main URL patterns unconditionally. This is the one finding I would fix first.

docs.title: 2–3. Transport hardening not set — Low–Medium, prod
docs.text:
The dynamic scan saw no Strict-Transport-Security header, and the static check agrees:

$ python manage.py check --deploy
?: (security.W004) You have not set a value for the SECURE_HSTS_SECONDS setting...
?: (security.W008) Your SECURE_SSL_REDIRECT setting is not set to True...

TLS is terminated by the hosting proxy (Cloud Run / Fly), and SECURE_PROXY_SSL_HEADER is correctly set, so traffic is encrypted. What is missing is telling the browser to insist on HTTPS (HSTS) and redirecting any stray HTTP request at the app layer.

docs.title: 4. No CSP / Permissions-Policy — Low
docs.text: For the JSON API this is minor, but /api/docs/ serves an HTML Swagger page, and that page has no Content-Security-Policy. The good headers that are present (below) cover clickjacking and MIME-sniffing; CSP and Permissions-Policy would complete the set for the one HTML surface.

docs.title: 5. Server banner — Info
docs.text:
Server: WSGIServer/0.2 CPython/3.12.10

The dev server names itself and the Python version. Production runs behind gunicorn, which still sends a Server header but less detail; suppressing it entirely is a small hardening step.

docs.title: 6–7. Dev-only, documented not actioned
docs.text:
• DEBUG=true disclosure. An unknown path returns Django's debug 404, which lists the whole URL map ("tried these URL patterns", 3.4 KB). A 500 would show a full traceback and settings. This only happens with DEBUG=true; DEBUG defaults to false and production sets it false, with PILAH_ALLOW_FAKE_GOOGLE_TOKEN guarded to refuse a non-debug boot. Real risk only if a deployment ever shipped DEBUG=true — worth a CI guard, not a code fix.
  • Cookies without Secure. CSRF_COOKIE_SECURE and SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE are not DEBUG, so they are secure in production and only unset in local dev.

docs.title: What held up
docs.text:
The scan found no way around the access controls, and the baseline posture is sound:

  • Authentication enforced. Every /api/v1/* endpoint returns 401 Unauthorized with WWW-Authenticate: Bearer realm="api" when unauthenticated; /admin/ redirects to the login page. (Cross-bank data isolation is covered by the A01 tests in the codebase.)
  • Good response headers present: X-Frame-Options: DENY, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin, Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy.
  • No low-hanging exposure: /.env → 404, /static/ → 404, no robots.txt, no path traversal, and only safe HTTP methods are allowed (GET, POST, HEAD, OPTIONS — no PUT/DELETE/TRACE at the surface).
  • Directory enumeration (Metasploit dir_scanner, default wordlist) surfaced only /admin/, which is the expected Django admin login.

docs.title: Patch plan
docs.text:
Each fix would be a test-first change on its own branch, with the OWASP category named in the commit, and re-verified with the same scan.

  1. Restrict the schema and docs (finding 1). Set SPECTACULAR_SETTINGS["SERVE_PERMISSIONS"] = ["rest_framework.permissions.IsAdminUser"] (or gate the two routes behind IsAuthenticated, or serve them only when DEBUG). Test: an unauthenticated GET /api/schema/ and /api/docs/ return 401/403; an admin gets 200.
  2. Enable HSTS (finding 2). SECURE_HSTS_SECONDS = 31536000, SECURE_HSTS_INCLUDE_SUBDOMAINS = True, SECURE_HSTS_PRELOAD = True, all guarded by not DEBUG. Test: the header is present with DEBUG=false and absent with DEBUG=true.
  3. Enforce HTTPS redirect (finding 3). SECURE_SSL_REDIRECT = not DEBUG, relying on the SECURE_PROXY_SSL_HEADER already configured. Clears security.W008.
  4. Add a minimal CSP / Permissions-Policy (finding 4). A middleware or django-csp, scoped so the API responses and the Swagger page both get a sensible policy.
  5. Suppress the server banner (finding 5). Strip or rewrite the Server header at the gunicorn/middleware layer.
  6. Guard against DEBUG=true in deploys (finding 6). A CI or start-up assertion that a production build cannot boot with DEBUG=true (partly covered already by the fake-token guard).

Findings 1–3 are the priority: finding 1 is a real contract disclosure, and 2–3 close the two warnings check --deploy already raises.

docs.title: Security scan — OWASP ZAP, 26 Oct 2026
docs.text:
A dynamic scan of the PILAH backend (pilah-be) and the web build (pilah-mobile) with OWASP ZAP 2.17.0, followed by manual verification of every finding and a patch plan. It's the follow-up to the 14 Oct Metasploit scan, run for the IR Security competency (a Metasploit-or-similar scan, explained, with a patch plan).

Scope and authorisation

I scanned my own local instances only:

  • the backend from the PIL-451 branch, under manage.py runserver on 127.0.0.1:8451, against a scratch SQLite database filled by seed_testing_data, so no real user data;
  • the web build, flutter build web --profile, served on 127.0.0.1:8452.

Staging and production were not scanned. An active scan sends thousands of attack requests and could fill a shared database with junk a week before UAT, so I chose local only. The backend ran with DEBUG=true.

docs.title: Method
docs.text:
Step How Headless ZAP zap-2.17.0.jar -daemon with its own scratch profile, API on 127.0.0.1:8090 Authenticated scanning Signed in as the seeded demo Pengurus; a ZAP replacer rule added Authorization: Bearer <token> to every backend request, so the scan reached the authenticated endpoints, not just the public ones Attack surface Imported the backend's OpenAPI schema (/api/schema/), so every documented endpoint was scanned, not only the ones a crawler finds; then spidered the API and the web build Scans The passive scan, then a full active scan of the API (the default policy, 4 threads per host, at most 60 min; it finished in about 20) Verification Every Medium, and the Low that hinted at a crash, re-checked by hand with curl and against the deployed configuration

The reports: HTML, JSON. They contain no token: I checked both for bearer tokens and JWTs before publishing.

docs.title: Results at a glance
docs.text:
0 High, 17 Medium, 125 Low, 129 Informational alert instances, across 15 alert types. Most instances repeat one header finding on every path.

Alert type Where Real or local? Why CSP: Wildcard Directive (Medium) backend, every response Real (finding 2) script-src 'self' https: and the same https: in style-src, connect-src and frame-src allow any HTTPS origin Application Error Disclosure (Low) POST /api/v1/pengumuman/id/tarik Real (finding 1) Reproduced: a 500, not a 404 Sub Resource Integrity Attribute Missing (Medium), Cross-Domain JavaScript Source File Inclusion (Low) /api/docs/ Real, debug-only (finding 3) Swagger UI loads swagger-ui-dist@latest from jsDelivr with no integrity hash CSP Header Not Set (Medium) web build Partly real (finding 4) My local static server sends no headers. Production nginx does send a CSP, but it's only frame-ancestors 'none', with no script-src Missing Anti-clickjacking Header (Medium), X-Content-Type-Options Missing (Low) web build Local only Production deploy/web/nginx.conf already sends X-Frame-Options: DENY and nosniff Server Leaks Version Information (Low) both Local only WSGIServer/… CPython/… is the dev server's banner, and Python's http.server on the web side; production runs gunicorn and nginx with server_tokens off Authentication Request Identified, Session Management Response Identified, Modern Web Application, User Agent Fuzzer, Suspicious Comments (Info) both Informational ZAP describing what it saw, not a weakness

docs.title: Findings
docs.text: # Finding OWASP (2021) Severity Whose code 1 Two announcement actions crash (500) on a missing or malformed id instead of answering 404 A04 Low–Medium apps/announcement (PIL-243) 2 The backend CSP allows any HTTPS origin for scripts, styles, connections and frames A05 Medium The CSP from pilah-be #129 3 Swagger UI loads an unpinned @latest script and stylesheet from a CDN with no SRI A08 Low (debug-only page) config/urls.py docs view 4 The web app shell has no script-src, and its CSP is only frame-ancestors A05 Low–Medium deploy/web/nginx.conf

docs.title: 1. A 500 instead of a 404 on tarik and terbitkan
docs.text:
ZAP sent the literal id where the OpenAPI schema has a UUID, and got a 500. Checked by hand as the demo Pengurus:

$ curl -X POST .../api/v1/pengumuman/id/tarik -H "Authorization: Bearer …"
500  ValueError                     # malformed id
$ curl -X POST .../api/v1/pengumuman/00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000/tarik …
500  DoesNotExist                   # well-formed id that doesn't exist
$ curl -X POST .../api/v1/pengumuman/00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000/terbitkan …
500                                 # same for terbitkan, which ZAP missed (it needs a valid body)
$ curl .../api/v1/pengumuman/00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000
404                                 # the standard detail route is fine

Cause. Both custom actions skip the viewset's get_object(): they call UUID(self.kwargs["pk"]) and then Pengumuman.objects.select_for_update().get(...) without handling DoesNotExist.

Not an access-control hole. The bank scoping is in the same .get(), so another bank's announcement fails the same way as a missing one, and the error reveals nothing about which ids exist. With DEBUG=false the body is a generic 500. The fault is error handling (CWE-755), which OWASP 2021 places under A04 Insecure Design and the 2025 list names A10, Mishandling of Exceptional Conditions.

docs.title: 2. https: in the backend CSP
docs.text:
script-src 'self' https:; style-src 'self' https:; connect-src 'self' https:; frame-src https:

A scheme source matches every HTTPS origin, so an injected <script src="https://attacker.example/x.js"> is allowed. That mostly undoes the CSP. API responses are JSON, which a browser never runs, so they need only default-src 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none'. The few HTML pages, the API docs and the OAuth popup, should list their exact origins.

docs.title: 3. Unpinned Swagger UI from a CDN
docs.text:
<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/swagger-ui-dist@latest/swagger-ui.css">

@latest with no integrity hash runs whatever jsDelivr serves that day, on a page that holds the API's schema. The page only exists with DEBUG=true, which keeps the severity low.

docs.title: 4. No script-src on the web app
docs.text: Production nginx sends Content-Security-Policy: frame-ancestors 'none' and nothing else. Since then, Pascal's pilah-mobile #178 adds a full policy. My review of it found it clean on every page but one, the draft PDF preview.

docs.title: Patch plan
docs.text:
Each fix is a test-first change, with the OWASP category named in its commit, as the earlier scan's plan was.

# Fix Test first OWASP Status (29 Oct) 1 tarik and terbitkan load the announcement through the bank-scoped get_object(), which answers 404 for a missing or malformed id For both actions: a missing UUID, a malformed id and another bank's id each get 404, never 500 A04 Planned. It's Aldo's code, so it needs a Linear issue and his agreement 2 JSON responses get default-src 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none'; the docs page and the OAuth popup list their exact origins No https: or * in any directive; the OAuth popup and docs still load A05 Planned. Offered to Gabriel first, since #129 is his 3 Pin swagger-ui-dist to an exact version with SRI hashes, or serve it locally with drf-spectacular-sidecar The docs page HTML has no @latest and an integrity attribute on each external asset A08 Fixed by Gabriel's pilah-be #174 (merged 17 Nov): swagger-ui-dist pinned to 5.35.0 with SRI hashes, and a test that fails if a tag loses its integrity. Hashes checked in my review 4 A full CSP for the web image Pascal's header tests, plus a browser check of the PDF preview A05 In progress as Pascal's #178. My review asks for the preview to be fixed or sequenced first

docs.title: How this compares with the 14 Oct scan
docs.text: The Metasploit scan listed "no Content-Security-Policy" (its finding 4). A CSP has since been added, and ZAP now shows it's too broad. That's finding 2 here: the header exists, and its directives now need tightening. Metasploit, built for known exploits in known software, had little to say about a bespoke API. ZAP's application-level checks, run signed in and driven by the schema, are what turned up findings 1 and 3.

docs.title: Security scan — OWASP ZAP per sub-issue, 2 Nov 2026
docs.text:
Two scans with OWASP ZAP 2.17.0, one per Linear sub-issue finished this week, run right after the work was done:

  • PIL-428: void ("Hapus") a setoran;
  • PIL-435: Riwayat shows setoran only.

Every finding was checked by hand, and each real one has a patch plan. Run for the IR Security competency (a Metasploit-or-similar scan, explained, with a patch plan). Since this week, every finished sub-issue gets one.

Scope and authorisation

My own local instances only. Staging and production were not scanned: an active scan sends thousands of attack requests.

Scan Backend Web build PIL-428 feature/pil-428 (#145 at ae850a0) on 127.0.0.1:8451, scratch PostgreSQL 16 database zap428 #193 on 127.0.0.1:8452 PIL-435 origin/staging at ee82c69, since PIL-435 changes no backend code, on 127.0.0.1:8453, scratch database zap435 #196 at 48f138b on 127.0.0.1:8454

Both databases were migrated and filled by seed_testing_data, so they hold no real user data. The backends ran with DEBUG=true, so findings that need it are labelled debug-only.

docs.title: Method
docs.text:
Each scan is one command: tools/zap_scan.py, with a small per-feature drive module (pil428.py, pil435.py).

Step How Headless ZAP zap-2.17.0.jar -daemon with a scratch profile, API on 127.0.0.1:8090 Signed in As the seeded demo Pengurus; a replacer rule adds the bearer token to every backend request ZAP sends Attack surface The OpenAPI schema imported, then the drive module's real requests sent through ZAP's proxy. For PIL-428: record two setoran, void one, void it again (409), void with an empty alasan (422), edit the voided one (409), read the list and riwayat. For PIL-435: the riwayat list for each tipe, with search, a custom period and the XLSX export. So the active scan attacks real ids and bodies, not schema placeholders Scans Spider of the API and web build, the passive scan, then the active scan limited to the feature: a ZAP context with /api/v1/transaksi (recursive: ids, /batalkan, PATCH) and /api/v1/aktivitas for PIL-428, and /api/v1/aktivitas and /api/v1/transaksi/export for PIL-435. Each recorded query-string variant was scanned on its own Verification Every 5xx in ZAP's history read from its response, not only ZAP's alerts; each real one reproduced with curl; the void's alasan tested by hand with attack payloads

Reports: PIL-428 HTML and JSON; PIL-435 HTML and JSON. The script refuses to finish if a report holds a bearer token or a JWT, and I grepped all four as well.

docs.title: Results at a glance
docs.text:
0 High in either scan. Every Medium and Low alert ZAP raised is either a known finding from the 26 Oct scan, still open on staging, or an artifact of the local servers:

Alert Where Status CSP: Wildcard Directive (Medium) backend, every response Known: 26 Oct finding 2, still open Sub Resource Integrity Attribute Missing (Medium), Cross-Domain JavaScript Source File Inclusion (Low) /api/docs/ Known: 26 Oct finding 3, debug-only Application Error Disclosure (Low) /api/v1/pengumuman/id/tarik Known: 26 Oct finding 1, still open CSP Header Not Set, Missing Anti-clickjacking (Medium); X-Content-Type-Options Missing (Low) web build Local only: the static test server sends no headers. Production nginx does, and Pascal's #178 adds a full CSP Server Leaks Version Information (Low) both Local only: the dev servers' banners User Agent Fuzzer, Modern Web Application and others (Info) both Informational

No alert on the features themselves:

  • The void: no injection, path traversal or error disclosure on /transaksi, /transaksi/{id}, /batalkan or PATCH. PIL-428's scan sent about 8,000 requests in scope: 5,800 on /transaksi (about 260 on /batalkan, 610 PATCH) and 2,200 on /aktivitas.
  • The riwayat list and export: none on /aktivitas or the export either. PIL-435's scan sent about 7,000 requests there.

ZAP's alerts aren't the whole story, though. Reading every response in its history turned up three 5xx that ZAP didn't raise as alerts:

# Request Response Real or local? 1 GET /api/v1/aktivitas?search=…%00… (JSON) 500, DataError: PostgreSQL text fields cannot contain NUL (0x00) bytes Real, in production too 2 GET /api/v1/aktivitas with Accept: text/html 500, AssertionError: 'ActivityHistoryView' should either include a queryset attribute… Debug-only 3 GET /api/v1/transaksi/{id} with Accept: text/html 500, AttributeError on field alasan of TransactionEditSerializer Debug-only

docs.title: Findings
docs.text: # Finding OWASP Severity Whose code 1 A NUL byte in ?search= crashes six list endpoints with a 500 instead of a 422 A04 (2021); A10 Mishandling of Exceptional Conditions (2025) Low–Medium The list views from PIL-246 onwards (Rifqi, Pascal, others); activity_sources is the riwayat's, which PIL-435 uses 2 The browsable API crashes on /aktivitas A05 Low (debug-only) ActivityHistoryView (PIL-246) 3 The browsable API crashes on a setoran's detail A05 Low (debug-only) TransactionEditSerializer (PIL-427)

docs.title: 1. NUL byte in search: a 500 on six endpoints
docs.text:
Reproduced by hand on the PIL-428 backend, as the demo Pengurus, with plain JSON requests:

$ curl -H "Authorization: Bearer …" -H "Accept: application/json" ".../api/v1/aktivitas?search=ab%00c"
500
$ # the same for /transaksi, /transaksi/export, /pencairan, /nasabah and /jenis-sampah
$ curl ... ".../api/v1/aktivitas?search=abc"
200

Cause. Each list view reads search straight from the query string (request.GET.get("search", "")) and passes it to an icontains filter. PostgreSQL refuses text containing \0, and the DataError escapes as a 500.

Request bodies don't have this problem, because they go through DRF fields. The void's alasan with a NUL byte gets 422 "Karakter null tidak diizinkan.", from CharField's built-in ProhibitNullCharactersValidator.

Impact. No data is exposed: with DEBUG=false the body is a generic 500. But it's an unhandled exception any signed-in user can trigger at will, and each one logs an error. Rifqi's open #144 already validates the nasabah list's search with a CharField, which would turn that one endpoint into a 422 once merged. The other five remain.

docs.title: 2 and 3. Browsable-API crashes, debug-only
docs.text:
config/settings.py adds BrowsableAPIRenderer only when DEBUG is on, so these can't happen in production. Locally, anyone opening the API in a browser hits a 500:

  • ActivityHistoryView is a GenericAPIView without a queryset;
  • the setoran detail renders its PATCH form from TransactionEditSerializer, whose alasan is write-only input, not a model attribute.

Both also fail on unmodified staging (checked against ee82c69).

docs.title: What held up
docs.text:
• The void's state machine: every attack POST on /batalkan got 409 (already void) or 422 (bad alasan). The database afterwards held exactly the voids the drive made, one per run, with its own alasan, so no payload voided a setoran or changed a saldo. The roughly 610 PATCH attacks on the voided setoran got 409 or 422.

  • The alasan as data, checked by hand on fresh setoran:

    Input Result <script>alert(1)</script>, ' OR 1=1; DROP TABLE transaksi;--, =HYPERLINK("http://x","y") 200, stored and returned verbatim as JSON text: the ORM parameterises it, and Flutter renders it as plain text A NUL byte 422 256 characters 422 (255 is accepted) Only whitespace 422 "Alasan pembatalan wajib diisi" An unknown or malformed id 404

    A voided setoran never appears in the XLSX or the statement PDF, so a formula in the alasan can't reach a spreadsheet. The exporter also guards user text against formulas. - Bank scoping: another bank's setoran is 404, covered by the tests in f67aa72. ZAP signs in as one user, so it doesn't test this itself.

docs.title: Patch plan
docs.text:
Each fix is test-first, with its OWASP category in the commit.

# Fix Test first OWASP Status (2 Nov) 1 Validate list query text the way bodies are: a shared helper in shared_kernel that reads search through a DRF CharField (NUL rejected, length bounded) and answers 422. All six list views use it For each of the six endpoints: ?search=a%00b gets 422, never 500; a normal search still filters A04 / A10:2025 Planned. It touches several teammates' views, so it needs a Linear issue first 2 Give ActivityHistoryView the shape the browsable API expects, or set renderer_classes = [JSONRenderer] on it With DEBUG=True overridden, Accept: text/html on /aktivitas gets 200 or 406, not 500 A05 Planned, low priority (debug-only) 3 Render the detail's browsable form without TransactionEditSerializer's write-only alasan: mark it write_only=True Accept: text/html on a setoran's detail gets 200 under DEBUG=True A05 Planned, low priority (debug-only) — 26 Oct findings 1–3 (the announcement 500, the backend CSP, Swagger SRI) As in that plan A04, A05, A08 Still open on staging; this scan re-confirmed them

docs.title: How the method improved on 26 Oct
docs.text:
The 26 Oct scan imported the schema, so ZAP attacked paths like /transaksi/id/batalkan, which can only ever 404. This time:

  • Real requests: the drive module sent the feature's real requests through ZAP's proxy, so the scan attacked a real setoran's void and edit.
  • History, not only alerts: reading every response in ZAP's history found the NUL-byte crash, which ZAP doesn't report as an alert.

Three mistakes on the way, corrected before trusting the results:

  • Git Bash rewrote --scope /api/... into a Windows path, so the first runs had nothing in scope.
  • ZAP's active-scan API can't find id paths by URL, so the script now scans each prefix recursively.
  • Its report API needs | between sites, not ;, so the first reports came out empty.

The script now refuses a non-API scope and fails on an empty report.

docs.title: Security scan — OWASP ZAP per sub-issue, 9 Nov 2026
docs.text:
Two scans with OWASP ZAP 2.17.0, one per Linear sub-issue finished today, run right after the work was done:

  • PIL-481: a voided ("Hapus") setoran is hidden from the riwayat lists;
  • PIL-480: the riwayat export no longer has the "ID Aktivitas" column.

Every High alert was checked by hand, every 5xx in ZAP's history was read, and each real finding has a patch plan. Run for the IR Security competency (a Metasploit-or-similar scan, explained, with a patch plan), as for every finished sub-issue since 2 Nov.

Scope and authorisation

My own local instances only. Staging and production were not scanned: an active scan sends thousands of attack requests.

Scan Backend Web build PIL-481 feature/pil-481 (#167 at 646c0d1) on 127.0.0.1:8451, scratch PostgreSQL 16 database zap481 #238 at ff86f6f on 127.0.0.1:8452 PIL-480 feature/pil-480 (#168 at 2b1fba9) on 127.0.0.1:8453, scratch database zap480 none: PIL-480 changes no UI

Both databases were migrated and filled by seed_testing_data, so they hold no real user data. The backends ran with DEBUG=true, so findings that need it are labelled debug-only. The web build is a static site, so ZAP could only spider its files.

docs.title: Method
docs.text:
Each scan is one command: tools/zap_scan.py, with a small per-feature drive module (pil481.py, pil480.py).

Step How Headless ZAP zap-2.17.0.jar -daemon, API on 127.0.0.1:8090 Signed in As the seeded demo Pengurus; a replacer rule adds the bearer token to every backend request ZAP sends Attack surface The OpenAPI schema imported, then the drive module's real requests sent through ZAP's proxy. PIL-481: record two setoran, void one, then read /transaksi, /aktivitas, the dashboard's recent transactions and the detail of the voided and the kept setoran. PIL-480: the XLSX export with every period, tipe, member, search and custom-range filter, plus a bad periode (400), and the riwayat list it is built from Scans Spider of the API (and the web build for PIL-481), the passive scan, then the active scan limited to the feature by a ZAP context. PIL-481: /api/v1/transaksi (recursive: ids, /batalkan, PATCH), /api/v1/aktivitas, /api/v1/dashboard/recent-transactions. PIL-480: /api/v1/transaksi/export and /api/v1/aktivitas. Each recorded query-string variant was scanned on its own Requests in scope PIL-481: 7,590 on /transaksi (444 of them on /batalkan), 3,774 on /aktivitas, 28 on the dashboard list. PIL-480: 4,835 on the export, 2,189 on /aktivitas. These are from the second run; see "What went wrong" for why there were two Verification Every High alert reproduced by hand; every 5xx in ZAP's history read from its response (not only ZAP's alerts) and sorted into real, debug-only, or caused by my machine

Reports: PIL-481 HTML and JSON; PIL-480 HTML and JSON. One alert's evidence is a Django debug page that dumps the dev machine's environment, so I redacted the computer name and my user name from the saved files. That was not enough: the dump also held two Discord webhook URLs, and they were published with the report. See "What went wrong" for how that was caught and fixed; the files now carry [REDACTED] in their place, and nothing else was edited.

docs.title: Results at a glance
docs.text:
Neither feature has a real High. ZAP raised three High alerts in the first PIL-481 run, two in the second, and none in PIL-480 either time. All are false positives; the 500 behind two of them is a real finding that was already in the code (finding 1 below).

ZAP alert Where Verdict SQL Injection (High) POST /transaksi/{id}/batalkan, parameter alasan, payload John Doe' AND '1'='1' -- False positive, see below. It did not recur in the second run Server Side Include (High) GET /transaksi?nasabah_id=<!--#EXEC cmd="dir \"--> False positive: the "evidence" is Django's DEBUG error page listing the dev machine's environment, not an executed command. The real cause is finding 1 Generic Padding Oracle (High) GET /transaksi?nasabah_id=…w1 False positive: nothing is encrypted; ZAP matched the text "Internal Server Error". Same real cause: finding 1 CSP: Wildcard Directive (Medium) backend, five paths Known: 26 Oct finding 2, still open Sub Resource Integrity Attribute Missing (Medium), Cross-Domain JavaScript Source File Inclusion (Low) /api/docs/ Known: 26 Oct finding 3, debug-only Application Error Disclosure (Low) /api/v1/pengumuman/{id}/tarik Known: 26 Oct finding 1, still open CSP Header Not Set, Missing Anti-clickjacking (Medium); X-Content-Type-Options Missing (Low) web build Local only: the static test server sends no headers. Production nginx does Server Leaks Version Information (Low) both backends and the web build Local only: the dev servers' banners Authentication Request Identified, Session Management Response Identified, User Agent Fuzzer, Modern Web Application (Info) both Informational

No alert on the features themselves: none on /transaksi, /aktivitas, the dashboard list, /batalkan or the export that points at what PIL-481 or PIL-480 changed.

docs.title: The "SQL injection" on the void's alasan, reproduced by hand
docs.text:
In the first run ZAP reported that two payloads gave different pages (the second run did not raise it again). Both payloads sent by hand, each on its own fresh setoran:

Request Result alasan = John Doe' AND '1'='1' -- 200, voided alasan = John Doe' AND '1'='2' -- 200, voided the same setoran voided again 409

Both rows are dibatalkan and the stored alasan is the payload text, character for character (the field only trims the trailing space). So the two payloads behave identically; ZAP's "different pages" came from the state change: the first request it sent voided the setoran (200), and every attack variant after it hit an already-voided setoran (409). The ORM parameterises the value, as in the 2 Nov hand test.

docs.title: The export file, checked by hand
docs.text: GET /transaksi/export?periode=semua on the PIL-480 backend returned 200 with a valid workbook: sheets Laporan, Riwayat Transaksi, Ringkasan; the raw sheet has 13 columns, headers No … Pencairan (Rp), no "ID Aktivitas", and the title rows merged over A1:M1 and A2:M2.

docs.title: ZAP's alerts aren't the whole story
docs.text:
Reading every response in ZAP's history of the second run gave 268 5xx in the PIL-481 scan and 5 in PIL-480. Sorted, with none caused by the machine:

# Request Response Real or local? PIL-481 / PIL-480 1 GET /api/v1/transaksi?nasabah_id=<not a UUID> 500, ValidationError: '…' bukan UUID yang valid Real, in production too; reproduced on the PIL-480 backend, which has staging's code for this path 226 / 0 2 GET /api/v1/transaksi, /aktivitas, /transaksi/export with a NUL byte in search 500, DataError: PostgreSQL text fields cannot contain NUL (0x00) bytes Real, known: 2 Nov finding 1, now also on the export 2 / 2 3 GET /api/v1/aktivitas and GET /api/v1/transaksi/{id} with Accept: text/html 500, AssertionError / AttributeError Debug-only, known: 2 Nov findings 2 and 3 38 / 1 4 POST /api/v1/pengumuman/{id}/tarik with a malformed id 500, ValueError Real, known: 26 Oct finding 1 1 / 1 5 GET /api/v1/auth/google/start 503, "Google OAuth client is not configured" Local only: the scratch backends have no Google client id 1 / 1

Rows 1–4 are not caused by PIL-481 or PIL-480.

docs.title: Findings
docs.text: # Finding OWASP Severity Whose code 1 A malformed nasabah_id on GET /transaksi is a 500, while the same value on /aktivitas is a 422 A04 (2021); A10 Mishandling of Exceptional Conditions (2025) Low–Medium TransaksiViewSet.get_queryset filters on the raw query value. Not changed by PIL-481, which only added .tercatat() to the list 2 A NUL byte in ?search= is a 500 on the list endpoints, now also seen on the export A04; A10:2025 Low–Medium Known: 2 Nov finding 1, still open 3 The browsable API crashes on /aktivitas and a setoran's detail A05 Low (debug-only) Known: 2 Nov findings 2 and 3 4 With DEBUG=true the 500 page lists the whole process environment A05 Low (debug-only) DEBUG is off in staging and production; this is why the report files had to be redacted

docs.title: 1. Malformed nasabah_id: a 500 on GET /transaksi
docs.text:
$ curl -H "Authorization: Bearer …" -H "Accept: application/json" ".../api/v1/transaksi?periode=semua&nasabah_id=abc"
500
$ curl ... ".../api/v1/aktivitas?periode=semua&nasabah_id=abc"
422

Cause. TransaksiViewSet.get_queryset does qs.filter(nasabah_id=nasabah_id) with the raw query value, so Django's ValidationError escapes as a 500. activity_sources (the riwayat) already validates the same parameter with serializers.UUIDField, which is why /aktivitas answers 422.

Impact. No data is exposed with DEBUG=false: the body is a generic 500. But any signed-in user can trigger an unhandled exception at will, and each one logs an error. It also made ZAP raise two of the three High alerts above, which is how it was found.

docs.title: What held up
docs.text:
• PIL-481, hiding a void: the lists leave it out and the detail by id still answers with the void, checked by the end-to-end run in #238 (24/24) and by the tests in #167. Hiding is a filter, so the audit row, who voided it, when and why are untouched.
  • PIL-480, the export: the file no longer carries any setoran or pencairan id, which is the point of A02 here: a workbook that gets forwarded by chat or email leaks no internal record ids. "ID Nasabah" (the member number) stays.
  • The void's alasan as data: stored verbatim, never executed, as in the 2 Nov hand test.

docs.title: Limits
docs.text:
• What the scans cover: the paths in scope, as one signed-in Pengurus, with DEBUG=true on a scratch database. They don't test another bank's data (that is in the unit tests) or the web build's API calls: the web build is a static site, so ZAP only spidered its files.
  • The first run was incomplete and was replaced. The machine's disk was full and the scratch PostgreSQL ran out of memory, so about 160 attack responses were local failures (see "What went wrong"). I re-ran both scans after the disk was freed. The second run had no such failure, and its results are the ones in this report.

docs.title: Patch plan
docs.text:
Each fix is test-first, with its OWASP category in the commit.

# Fix Test first OWASP Status (9 Nov) 1 In TransaksiViewSet.get_queryset, validate nasabah_id with serializers.UUIDField().run_validation, as activity_sources does, and answer 422 ?nasabah_id=abc and ?nasabah_id=<script> on /transaksi get 422, never 500; a valid id still filters A04 / A10:2025 Planned. Filed as PIL-482 (9 Nov); it touches the list view of other issues, so it is its own PR 2 Shared helper in shared_kernel that reads search through a DRF CharField (NUL rejected, length bounded) for every list view and the export For each endpoint: ?search=a%00b gets 422, never 500 A04 / A10:2025 Planned (2 Nov patch plan, item 1) 3 renderer_classes = [JSONRenderer] on ActivityHistoryView, and write_only=True on TransactionEditSerializer.alasan Accept: text/html on both under DEBUG=True gets 200 or 406, not 500 A05 Planned, low priority (debug-only) 4 Nothing to change in code: DEBUG is off in staging and production (DJANGO_DEBUG = "false" in fly.toml). Keep scan reports redacted — A05 Closed, kept for the record — 26 Oct findings 1–3 As in that plan A04, A05, A08 Still open on staging; this scan re-confirmed them — Re-run both scans once the disk was freed Zero OperationalError or No space left in the second run — Done (9 Nov)

docs.title: What went wrong on the way
docs.text:
• ZAP's first start installs its add-ons and moves its API from 8090 to 8080 and back, so the first two scan attempts failed on "connection refused" and "remote end closed". The scans were started again once ZAP listened on 8090.
  • The first full run was partly invalid. The machine's disk filled up (No space left on device on the export), and the scratch PostgreSQL ran out of memory with three backends and ZAP's four threads attacking it: 140 of the PIL-481 scan's 5xx and 19 of PIL-480's were OperationalError or OSError. I classified them as the machine's fault, not findings, and re-ran both scans after the disk was freed. The second run had none, and the alerts differed only in that the "SQL injection" on alasan did not recur.
  • Both runs' report files held a Django debug page with the dev machine's environment, so the computer name and my user name were redacted from the saved files each time.
  • A secret got through (found 13 Nov). The same environment dump held two Discord webhook URLs (the review and QA channels' DISCORD_*_WEBHOOK_URL variables, exported on the dev machine), and the PIL-481 HTML and JSON were pushed with them in commit 04c1939. My check at the time looked only for bearer tokens and JWTs, and my "grepped for secrets" did not cover webhooks. GitHub's public-repo scanning (FriendlyScanner) found them within a day and Discord deleted both webhooks, so they no longer work. The four other credential variables in the dump (DB_PASSWORD, DJANGO_SECRET_KEY, HTTP_AUTHORIZATION, PILAH_ALLOW_FAKE_GOOGLE_TOKEN) were already masked by Django. The fix: the two files now say [REDACTED]; tools/zap_scan.py now also refuses to finish on Discord and Slack webhooks, GitHub, Google and Slack tokens, and database URLs with a password, and I confirmed the new check flags the original file and none of the current ones. The OWASP category is A05 Security Misconfiguration, as in finding 4 (a debug page that dumps the environment); the old commit 04c1939 still contains the dead URLs.

docs.title: Security scan — OWASP ZAP per sub-issue, 17 Nov 2026
docs.text:
Three scans with OWASP ZAP 2.17.0, one per backend PR opened on 16 Nov for Sprint 3 Week 3:

  • PIL-482 (#175): a malformed nasabah_id on /transaksi and /pencairan answers 422, not 500. This is the fix for 9 Nov finding 1;
  • waste categories through tercatat() (#176): /dashboard/waste-categories reads counted setoran through the named rule;
  • a NUL byte in a request body (#177): kode on jenis-sampah and nasabah edits, and the device token on DELETE /device-tokens/, answer 422, not 500.

Every 5xx the backends answered was read and classified. The scans ran from 16 Nov 23:56 to 17 Nov 00:26. Run for the IR Security competency (a Metasploit-or-similar scan, explained, with a patch plan), as for every finished sub-issue since 2 Nov.

Scope and authorisation

My own local instances only. Staging and production were not scanned.

Scan Backend Database PIL-482 feature/pil-482 (#175 at b85819a) on 127.0.0.1:8482 zap482 waste-categories fix/waste-categories-tercatat (#176 at 8d1a931) on 127.0.0.1:8483 zapwaste nul-body fix/nul-in-request-body (#177 at 7b7841d) on 127.0.0.1:8484 zapnul
  • Databases: each is a scratch PostgreSQL 16 database, created fresh, migrated and filled by seed_testing_data, so none holds real user data.
  • No web build: none of the three PRs changes the UI.
  • Clean environment: each backend ran with DEBUG=true but was started with an empty environment (env -i plus only the variables it needs). So no secret of the dev machine could reach a debug page, unlike on 9 Nov.

docs.title: Method
docs.text:
The same one-command driver as on 9 Nov, tools/zap_scan.py, with one new drive module per PR: pil482.py, waste_categories.py, nul_body.py.

Step How Headless ZAP zap-2.17.0.jar -daemon with a 1 GB heap, API on 127.0.0.1:8090; one scan at a time, each with its own backend and a new ZAP session Signed in As the seeded demo Pengurus; a replacer rule adds the bearer token to every backend request ZAP sends Attack surface The OpenAPI schema imported, then the drive module's real requests sent through ZAP's proxy:• PIL-482: each ledger list with a real member's id (200) and with abc (422).• waste-categories: record two setoran, void one, then read waste-categories, the trends and the stats.• nul-body: edit a jenis and a nasabah keeping their own kode (200), with a NUL in it (422) and with another record's kode padded with spaces (422); register a device token, then forget it with a NUL token (422) and with the real one (204) Scans Spider of the API, the passive scan, then the active scan limited to each PR's paths by a ZAP context:• PIL-482: /api/v1/transaksi, /api/v1/pencairan, /api/v1/aktivitas.• waste-categories: /api/v1/dashboard/waste-categories.• nul-body: /api/v1/jenis-sampah, /api/v1/nasabah, /api/v1/device-tokens.Each recorded query-string variant was scanned on its own Requests Counted from each backend's own request log, which sees every request ZAP sent:• PIL-482: 17,059 in all, including 1,781 on the /transaksi list, 1,681 on the /pencairan list and 2,766 on /aktivitas.• waste-categories: 1,523, of which 1,056 on /dashboard/waste-categories.• nul-body: 30,674, including 231 attacks on the real jenis's PATCH and 228 on the real nasabah's Verification Every 5xx in the three backend logs read from its traceback and sorted into real, debug-only, or caused by my machine

Reports:

Scan HTML JSON PIL-482 HTML JSON waste-categories HTML JSON nul-body HTML JSON

The driver refused to finish on any bearer token, JWT, webhook, API token or database URL with a password. By hand I also searched all six files for the computer name and my user name. None of these appear, so nothing was redacted.

docs.title: Results at a glance
docs.text:
No High alert in any of the three scans, and no new finding. Every alert is one already on record:

ZAP alert Where Verdict CSP: Wildcard Directive (Medium) backend, five paths Known: 26 Oct finding 2, still open Sub Resource Integrity Attribute Missing (Medium), Cross-Domain JavaScript Source File Inclusion (Low) /api/docs/ Known: 26 Oct finding 3, debug-only Server Leaks Version Information (Low) all three backends Local only: the dev server's banner Authentication Request Identified, Session Management Response Identified, User Agent Fuzzer, Modern Web Application (Info) all three Informational

docs.title: What each PR's scan shows
docs.text:
• PIL-482, the fix for 9 Nov finding 1. ZAP sent 965 malformed nasabah_id values to the /transaksi and /pencairan lists, counting the value Django reads when a parameter repeats. All 965 got 422 and none got 500.
    • Before the fix: on 9 Nov the scan of /transaksi alone gave 226 of these 500s, and they caused two false High alerts (Server Side Include, Padding Oracle). Neither alert came back.
    • The other 422s: another 1,067 carried a valid id while ZAP attacked a different parameter (periode, tipe, dates).
    • Empty value: an empty nasabah_id= means no filter and got 200.
    • /aktivitas: its 487 malformed ids got 422, as before.

  • waste-categories. ZAP sent 1,056 requests to /dashboard/waste-categories, attacking dates, ranges and injections in each parameter:

    • 1,003 got 400 for an invalid date or range;
    • 50 got 200;
    • 3 got 404.

    There was no 5xx and no alert on the path. The PR changes which rule selects the rows, not the response, so the scan's job here was to show that nothing new opened. - nul-body. The attacks on the real jenis's and the real nasabah's PATCH were answered 200, 422 or 405, never 500. On staging a NUL or a padded duplicate kode in that body is a 500 (DataError, IntegrityError); the drive module showed both now give 422.

docs.title: ZAP's alerts aren't the whole story
docs.text:
Every 5xx in the three backend logs:

# Request Response Real or local? PIL-482 / waste / nul 1 GET /api/v1/aktivitas?… with Accept: text/html 500, AssertionError: 'ActivityHistoryView' should either include a queryset attribute… from DRF's BrowsableAPIRenderer.get_filter_form Debug-only, known: 2 Nov finding 2 and 9 Nov finding 3. The browsable renderer is only added when DEBUG is on (config/settings.py); production serves JSON only 2 / 0 / 0 2 GET /api/v1/auth/google/start 503, "Google OAuth client is not configured" Local only: the scratch backends have no Google client id 1 / 1 / 2

No OperationalError, OSError or other failure of the machine appears in any log. The three runs are complete.

docs.title: Findings
docs.text:
No new finding. The state of the earlier ones that these PRs touch:

Earlier finding Status after this scan 9 Nov 1: malformed nasabah_id is a 500 on /transaksi Fixed by #175: all 965 malformed ids got 422, none 500 (open for review; filed as PIL-482) 9 Nov 2 / 2 Nov 1: a NUL byte in search is a 500 Fixed on staging by #172 (Scallss, 16 Nov). #177 fixes the request-body case #172 left open, plus a padded duplicate kode that was also a 500 9 Nov 3: the browsable API crashes on /aktivitas Still open, debug-only; seen again here (row 1 above) 26 Oct 2 and 3: CSP wildcard, /api/docs/ without SRI Seen again on these branches, which predate the fix. Finding 3 is fixed on staging by Gabriel's #174, merged 17 Nov after these scans; finding 2 is still open

docs.title: Limits
docs.text:
• DELETE /device-tokens/ was not actively scanned. That route is only ever sent POST and DELETE, so ZAP's site tree has no GET node for it. ZAP refused the active scan ("URL Not Found in the Scan Tree") both by prefix and per method. Its NUL case is covered instead by the drive module's own request (NUL token, 422) and by #177's tests. Scanning it needs a change to how the driver starts scans; that is in the patch plan.
  • Coverage of the scans: each scan covers the paths in scope, as one signed-in Pengurus, with DEBUG=true. They don't test another bank's data, which is covered by the unit tests.
  • Many requests went to placeholder paths. Requests built from the OpenAPI schema use literal placeholders (/nasabah/id/approve), which answer 404. So the attacks that count are the ones on the real records the drive module created. Their numbers are given above.

docs.title: Patch plan
docs.text: # Fix Test first OWASP Status (17 Nov) 1 Merge #175, #176 and #177 Each PR's own tests: red, then green, in its commits A04 / A10:2025 Open for review; CI and SonarCloud green on all three (100% new coverage, 0 issues) 2 renderer_classes = [JSONRenderer] on ActivityHistoryView Accept: text/html on /aktivitas under DEBUG=True gets 200 or 406, not 500 A05 Planned, low priority (debug-only); carried from 9 Nov item 3 3 Let tools/zap_scan.py actively scan a path that has no GET node (e.g. start from the recorded message, or add the node by a GET request first) Rescan /device-tokens/: more than 0 scans start, and every response is 2xx or 4xx — Planned (tooling) — 26 Oct findings 2 and 3 As in that plan A05, A08 Still open on staging

docs.title: What went wrong on the way
docs.text:
• The first attempt on 16 Nov ran out of machine. Two full test suites, three backends and ZAP ran at the same time and used up the 16 GB machine's commit memory. PostgreSQL stopped with Windows error 1455, and later ZAP died with a native OutOfMemoryError ("malloc failed"). The disk on C: also reached 0 GB free.
    • Evidence discarded: the PIL-482 files from that attempt (zap-pil-482-2026-11-16.*) record attacks on a dead database, so they are not used or published.
    • The rerun: after the disk was freed, all three scans were run again, one at a time:
      • each database was recreated from the seed;
      • ZAP's heap was capped at 1 GB;
      • the test suites waited for the scans to finish.
  • A bug in the scan runner. It exported MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 for the whole script. In Git Bash that broke the curl -o /dev/null readiness check, so the runner waited forever. The variable is now set only on the zap_scan.py command.

docs.title: Security scan — OWASP ZAP per sub-issue, 23 Nov 2026
docs.text:
One scan with OWASP ZAP 2.17.0 of PIL-539, a nasabah who already belongs to a bank sampah applying to another one, run right after the sub-issue was finished:

  • backend: pilah-be #185 (merged 23 Nov), tests for the flow on the existing endpoints;
  • mobile: pilah-mobile #276, "Ajukan bank baru" on Bank sampah saya. It calls GET /nasabah/me, GET /bank-sampah and POST /onboarding/nasabah.

This is the first scan signed in as a nasabah rather than the demo Pengurus, because the flow is the nasabah's. Every 5xx the backend answered was read and classified. The scan ran on 23 Nov from 00:44 to 00:52, after a first run that showed a gap in the tooling (see What went wrong).

Scope and authorisation

My own local instance only. Staging and production were not scanned.

Backend staging at 80a30aa (the #185 merge) on 127.0.0.1:8539 Database Scratch PostgreSQL 16 database zap539, created fresh, migrated and filled by seed_testing_data, plus one extra active bank sampah ("Bank Sampah ZAP Kedua") so the demo nasabah has a second bank to apply to. No real user data Signed in as customer.demo@example.com, the seeded nasabah, approved at "Bank Sampah PILAH E2E" Environment DEBUG=true, started with an empty environment (env -i plus only the variables it needs), as since 17 Nov Web build None: #276 changes only native Nasabah screens

docs.title: Method
docs.text:
One command, tools/zap_scan.py, with the drive module pil539.py, and --id-token dev:customer.demo@example.com:… so the bearer rule carries the nasabah's token.

The drive module sends the flow's real requests through ZAP's proxy:

Request Answer GET /api/v1/nasabah/me 200, one approved membership GET /api/v1/bank-sampah 200, the directory POST /api/v1/onboarding/nasabah with the second bank 201, pending the same again 400, "Anda sudah terdaftar sebagai nasabah di bank sampah ini" with the nasabah's own bank 400, the same message with bank_sampah_id: "bukan-uuid" 422 GET /api/v1/nasabah/me 200, two memberships GET /api/v1/nasabah/me/saldo?keanggotaan_id=<pending> 403: a pending membership can't open its saldo

Then the spider, the passive scan, and an active scan limited to /api/v1/onboarding/nasabah, /api/v1/nasabah/me (recursive) and /api/v1/bank-sampah (recursive). The POST-only path is scanned from its recorded request, with its method and the drive's body: this is the tooling fix from this scan.

Reports: HTML and JSON. Both were checked by the script's secret patterns (none) and for the machine's and my user name (none). The clean environment meant there was nothing to redact.

docs.title: Results at a glance
docs.text:
No High alert, and no new finding. Every alert is one already on record:

ZAP alert Where Verdict CSP: Wildcard Directive (Medium) backend, five paths Known: 26 Oct finding 2, still open Server Leaks Version Information (Low) backend Local only: the dev server's banner User Agent Fuzzer (Info) POST /api/v1/onboarding/nasabah Informational. It is also the proof that the POST-only path was actively attacked this time Authentication Request Identified, Modern Web Application (Info) auth paths, /api/docs/ Informational

docs.title: What the scan shows on the feature's paths
docs.text:
From the backend's own log, which sees every request ZAP sent:

Path Requests Answers POST /api/v1/onboarding/nasabah 228 POSTs: 224 attacks and the drive's four 207 × 422, 19 × 400, 1 × 404, and one 201, the drive's own. No 5xx, and no attack created a membership: afterwards the nasabah has exactly the two rows the drive made (approved at bank A, pending at bank B). The attacks used the real body, {"bank_sampah_id": "<bank B>"}, with injection, path-traversal and header payloads in the value /api/v1/nasabah/me and children about 4,000 200, 403, 404, 405, 422 and 3 × 429 (the per-user throttle). 3 × 500, below /api/v1/bank-sampah and children about 2,490 200, 400, 403, 404, 405, 422. Every write a nasabah tried was refused: 1,926 × 403 on PUT and 6 on POST

docs.title: ZAP's alerts aren't the whole story
docs.text:
Every 5xx in the backend log:

# Request Response Real or local? 1 GET /api/v1/nasabah/me/riwayat (×3, with and without query) and Accept: text/html 500, AssertionError: 'NasabahHistoryView' should either include a queryset attribute… from DRF's BrowsableAPIRenderer.get_filter_form Debug-only. The same crash as 2 Nov finding 2 and 9 Nov finding 3, now seen on the nasabah's riwayat. The browsable renderer is only added when DEBUG is on; production serves JSON only 2 GET /api/v1/auth/google/start 503, "Google OAuth client is not configured" Local only: the scratch backend has no Google client id

docs.title: Findings
docs.text:
No new finding. The state of the earlier ones this scan touched:

Earlier finding Status 9 Nov 3 / 2 Nov 2: the browsable API crashes on list views without a queryset Still open, debug-only. Seen again on NasabahHistoryView 26 Oct 2: CSP wildcard directive Still open 17 Nov limit: a POST- or DELETE-only path can't be actively scanned Fixed in the tooling in this scan, see below

docs.title: What held up
docs.text:
• One membership per bank, on the server. #276 removed the client's one-bank lock for this flow. The duplicate rule lives in register_nasabah, and 224 attacks on the application endpoint produced no second row and no 5xx.
  • A pending membership opens nothing. Its saldo answers 403, as pinned by #185's tests.
  • The directory is read-only for a nasabah. Every PUT and POST under /bank-sampah was refused.

docs.title: Limits
docs.text:
• One account. The scan runs as one nasabah. It doesn't test another nasabah's memberships or a pengurus deciding the application; those are in #185's tests.
  • Placeholder paths. Requests built from the OpenAPI schema use literal placeholders (/nasabah/id/saldo), which answer 404. The attacks that count are on the real records the drive module created.
  • No native client. #276 is a native screen, so no web build was spidered.

docs.title: Patch plan
docs.text: # Fix Test first OWASP Status (23 Nov) 1 renderer_classes = [JSONRenderer] on the nasabah history view, as planned for ActivityHistoryView Accept: text/html on /nasabah/me/riwayat under DEBUG=True gets 200 or 406, not 500 A05 Planned, low priority (debug-only); joins 9 Nov item 3 2 tools/zap_scan.py scans a POST- or DELETE-only scope path from its recorded request Rescan: the path is attacked (User Agent Fuzzer on it, 224 attack requests in the log) — Done (23 Nov), closes 17 Nov plan item 3 — 26 Oct finding 2 As in that plan A05 Still open on staging

docs.title: What went wrong on the way
docs.text:
• The first run left the endpoint that matters unscanned. ZAP refused POST /onboarding/nasabah with "URL Not Found in the Scan Tree". It's the same limit as /device-tokens/ on 17 Nov: a path only ever sent POST has no GET node to look up. I started that scan by hand through ZAP's API with the method and body, which worked. Then I fixed zap_scan.py to do it itself, rebuilt the database and reran everything. This report is from the rerun.
  • The driver's log line was wrong. It always said "signed in as the seeded demo Pengurus". It now names the account the token belongs to.
  • I stopped the scratch PostgreSQL by mistake. It was recovering after the session's earlier shutdown, and I deleted its postmaster.pid, so it shut itself down as soon as it was ready. It restarted cleanly with its log outside the data directory, before any scan request was sent.

docs.text:
Backend first, then mobile, because the mobile form depends on the API contract.

docs.title: How it was measured
docs.text:
"My lines" are the lines changed between origin/staging and my branch (git diff origin/staging...HEAD), excluding tests and migrations. Their coverage was checked with two independent tools, which agree:

  1. diff-cover: a standard tool that reports coverage on the lines of a diff only. Report: pil-176-diff-coverage.html (111 lines, 0 missing, 100%).
  2. coverage.py JSON + the diff: executed and missing line numbers from coverage json, intersected with the diff's added lines. Same result: 111 of 111.

To reproduce, from the pilah-be worktree:

coverage run --source=api manage.py test
coverage xml -o htmlcov/coverage.xml
diff-cover htmlcov/coverage.xml --compare-branch=origin/staging \
  --exclude "*/tests.py" "*/migrations/*" \
  --format html:htmlcov/pil-176-diff-coverage.html

docs.title: Tests behind the coverage
docs.text:
11 tests in PencairanAPITests and 3 in ResetTestingDataCommandTests, written test-first (a failing test(...) commit, then the feat(...)/fix(...) commit that makes it pass):

  • Positive: a pencairan lowers the saldo exactly once; the list filters by nasabah; the detail is readable within the bank.
  • Negative: nominal above the saldo; zero, negative or decimal nominal; future tanggal; invalid metode; another bank's nasabah; an inactive, pending or rejected nasabah; outsiders get 404, superadmin 403, unauthenticated 401.
  • Corner cases: saldo history after a pencairan (API and Excel export); a setoran and pencairan at the same instant; legacy saldo with sen rounded down to whole rupiah.

docs.title: Sprint 1 Plan — PIL-176 Pencatatan Pencairan untuk Pengurus
docs.text: Item Detail Owner Vegard Linear PIL-176 (parent: PIL-140 CPBI-10) Linear branch feature/pil-176-pencatatan-pencairan-untuk-pengurus (from staging) Sprint Sprint 1 — 15 Sep → 1 Oct 2026 · UAT 29 Sep · Sprint Review 1 Oct PRD features F13 (pencatatan pencairan tunai/transfer), partially F14 (riwayat) Repos touched pilah-be (model, service, API) and pilah-mobile (pengurus form) Status Backend in review (pilah-be #19): all three review findings fixed, retargeted to staging, mergeable, 100% coverage on new code. Awaiting re-review. Mobile not started. Updated 22 Sep 2026.

docs.title: 1. Goal
docs.text:
A pengurus can record a cash-out (pencairan) for a nasabah: nominal, tanggal, metode (tunai/transfer), keterangan. The nasabah's saldo drops exactly once, never below zero, and the record can be read back later for the riwayat pencairan.

PIL-176 description:

Membuat pencatatan realisasi pencairan yang dilakukan oleh pengurus yang isinya termasuk: nominal, tanggal, metode pencairan, keterangan tambahan. Data dapat dilihat kembali oleh pengurus dan nasabah melalui riwayat pencairan.

These acceptance criteria from CPBI-10 and PRD §3.13 apply to this task:

  • Pengurus records nominal, tanggal, metode (tunai / transfer), and keterangan.
  • Pencairan is only allowed if the saldo is sufficient (validated against the membership's saldo).
  • Saldo and history update exactly once, atomically.
  • Each record stores who recorded it and when (audit).
  • Only the pengurus of that bank sampah can create or read it (data isolation).
  • No payment gateway: the app only records the payout.

docs.title: In scope (PIL-176)
docs.text:
• Backend Pencairan model, migration, and admin registration.
  • Atomic PencairanService.create_pencairan with saldo validation and row locking.
  • API: POST /api/v1/pencairan, GET /api/v1/pencairan/{id}, and a minimal GET /api/v1/pencairan list filtered by nasabah.
  • Fix the existing "saldo setelah transaksi" calculations so they subtract pencairan (see §4.3).
  • Mobile pengurus flow: entry point → form → confirmation → success sheet → saldo refreshed.
  • Backend and mobile tests that keep the CI coverage gates green.

docs.title: Out of scope (sibling or later issues)
docs.text:
Work Where Full riwayat pencairan screen for pengurus PIL-222 (unassigned) Editing a recorded pencairan PIL-230 (unassigned) Jadwal pencairan (F12) CPBI-10 AC #1, which has no sub-issue yet Nasabah-side request/approval (F13 "pengajuan nasabah") Sprint 2 per PRD. Nasabah may only view, never request or approve (§8 Q9). Nasabah-side read of riwayat pencairan In Sprint 1 scope per §8 Q9, but likely PIL-222 rather than PIL-176 — confirm the owner. WhatsApp or push notification on pencairan CPBI-14 / F16 Pencairan rows in the Excel export Follow-up; only the running balance is fixed here

The API should be designed so that PIL-222 and PIL-230 can build on it without breaking changes.

docs.title: 3.1 Backend (pilah-be, Django 6 + DRF)
docs.text:
• No pencairan code exists (model, API, or UI). The Linear notes on CPBI-10 say the same.
  • Saldo is a one-to-one row per Nasabah (total_saldo, Decimal 14,2). Nasabah is already scoped per bank sampah, so it effectively acts as the membership today.
  • Transaksi.Tipe only has SETORAN. Every setoran has DetailTransaksi items, and the list serializer, export, and dashboard all assume items exist.
  • TransactionService.create_setoran (api/services.py) is the pattern to follow: it is @transaction.atomic, uses select_for_update() on the nasabah and saldo, scopes by user.bank_sampah, and raises serializers.ValidationError.
  • Two places compute a historical balance by summing Transaksi.total_nilai only:
  • TransactionDetailSerializer.get_saldo_setelah_transaksi (api/serializers.py)
  • _saldo_after_by_transaction (api/services.py, used by the Excel export)

Once pencairan exists, both will overstate the balance for any setoran recorded after a pencairan. This must be fixed in the same PR. - Permission IsActivePengelola gates every pengurus endpoint. Superadmin is already rejected (covered by tests). - Error format comes from api/exceptions.py: validation errors become 422 {"errors": {...}}, and 404 becomes {"error": "Resource tidak ditemukan"}. - CI (.github/workflows/ci.yml on staging) runs ruff check, ruff format --check, makemigrations --check, tests with coverage ≥ 80%, manage.py check --deploy, mypy strict, and SonarQube. - ✅ Base branch resolved (20 Sep): staging is the baseline for every repo; AGENTS.md and the ship skill now say so explicitly. origin/staging is 11 commits ahead of main. - ✅ PIL-152 merged into staging on 20 Sep (ad1c1f6). Nasabah stays the per-bank membership, so the FK target was unchanged. - ⚠️ Stacked on PIL-188 (#18): both branches added an 0011_ migration from the same parent, which would have left Django with two leaf nodes. PR #19 is rebased onto #18 and renumbered to 0012_pencairan, keeping the graph linear. #18 merged on 21 Sep. GitHub does not retarget automatically while #18's branch still exists, so #19 was retargeted to staging by hand on 22 Sep; the one import-line conflict with #20 was resolved by merging staging into the branch. - ~~PIL-152 lands first:~~ PR #15 (In Review) adds migrations 0005–0010, Nasabah.user, bank hierarchy, and one-membership-per-bank. Nasabah stays the per-bank membership, so the FK target is unchanged, but the pencairan migration must be renumbered after it merges. The PR still targets main and needs retargeting to staging.

  • New features are scaffolded with the SPL CLI: dart run codegen/spl_manager.dart add <name> --state cubit. Don't hand-edit spl.yaml.

  • PilihNasabahBottomSheet is the nasabah picker and already fetches the nasabah list.
  • DetailNasabahBottomSheet shows saldo and has action buttons, which makes it a natural entry point.
  • Design system: toast, confirmation modal ("Konfirmasi pencairan" is already in the PRD's design system), and CustomPrimaryButton.

docs.title: 4.1 Decision: a separate Pencairan model, not Transaksi(tipe=PENCAIRAN)
docs.text:
Option Pros Cons A. New Pencairan model ✅ Clear fields (metode, keterangan); no fake DetailTransaksi; setoran list, export, dashboard, and WA code stay untouched; room for Sprint 2 status/request lifecycle and PIL-230 edit audit Balance-history helpers must union two tables B. Add PENCAIRAN to Transaksi.Tipe with a negative total_nilai Existing running-balance sums "just work" Every consumer that assumes items breaks (jenis_sampah_utama, total_berat_kg, export sheet, dashboard total_nilai_bulan_ini, recent activity, WA notify); negative "nilai" is confusing; hard to add status later

Recommendation: A. Confirm with the backend reviewer before writing the migration.

docs.title: 4.2 Data model (api/models.py)
docs.text:
class Pencairan(TimestampedModel):
    class Metode(models.TextChoices):
        TUNAI = "tunai", "Tunai"
        TRANSFER = "transfer", "Transfer"

    class Status(models.TextChoices):
        TERCATAT = "tercatat", "Tercatat"

    id = models.UUIDField(primary_key=True, default=uuid.uuid4, editable=False)
    nasabah = models.ForeignKey(Nasabah, on_delete=models.PROTECT, related_name="pencairan")
    bank_sampah = models.ForeignKey(BankSampah, on_delete=models.PROTECT, related_name="pencairan")
    dicatat_oleh = models.ForeignKey(User, on_delete=models.PROTECT, related_name="pencairan_dicatat")
    tanggal = models.DateTimeField(default=timezone.now)
    nominal = models.DecimalField(max_digits=14, decimal_places=2)
    metode = models.CharField(max_length=20, choices=Metode.choices)
    keterangan = models.TextField(blank=True)
    status = models.CharField(max_length=20, choices=Status.choices, default=Status.TERCATAT)
    saldo_sebelum = models.DecimalField(max_digits=14, decimal_places=2)
    saldo_sesudah = models.DecimalField(max_digits=14, decimal_places=2)

    class Meta:
        db_table = "pencairan"
        ordering = ["-tanggal"]
        indexes = [models.Index(fields=["bank_sampah", "nasabah", "tanggal"])]
        constraints = [
            models.CheckConstraint(condition=models.Q(nominal__gt=0), name="pencairan_nominal_positive"),
        ]

Notes:

  • saldo_sebelum / saldo_sesudah are receipt snapshots at record time, matching the PRD "Detail Setoran" pattern. PIL-230 will define how edits affect them.
  • status ships with the single value tercatat (§8 Q8). A recorded pencairan is final in Sprint 1; Sprint 2 adds the request lifecycle and PIL-230 adds edits. Shipping the field now keeps the payload stable for both.
  • The migration is purely additive and safe on the existing data.
  • Register it in api/admin.py, and add it to the verification counts in reset_testing_data.

docs.title: 4.3 Service (api/services.py)
docs.text:
PencairanService.create_pencairan(user, payload) -> Pencairan, wrapped in @transaction.atomic:

  1. Lock the nasabah with Nasabah.objects.select_for_update().filter(id=..., bank_sampah=user.bank_sampah, is_active=True). If none is found, return 422 on nasabah_id.
  2. Lock the saldo with Saldo.objects.select_for_update().get_or_create(nasabah=nasabah).
  3. If nominal > saldo.total_saldo, return 422 on nominal with "Saldo nasabah tidak mencukupi".
  4. Create the Pencairan with saldo_sebelum / saldo_sesudah.
  5. Run saldo.total_saldo -= nominal and save with update_fields.

The row locks serialize concurrent requests, so two quick pencairan can't both pass the saldo check.

Balance helper fix. Add one shared helper, e.g. BalanceService.saldo_at(nasabah, bank, until_dt, until_id), that returns Σ setoran − Σ pencairan up to a point in time. Use it in:

  • TransactionDetailSerializer.get_saldo_setelah_transaksi
  • _saldo_after_by_transaction (export). Subtract the pencairan per nasabah that fall inside the running window.

docs.title: 4.4 API
docs.text:
All endpoints use permission_classes = [IsActivePengelola] and are scoped to request.user.bank_sampah. Add a PencairanViewSet registered as pencairan.

POST /api/v1/pencairan

{
  "nasabah_id": "uuid",
  "nominal": "200000.00",
  "metode": "tunai",
  "tanggal": "2026-09-22T10:15:00+07:00",
  "keterangan": "Diambil pagi"
}
Field Rule nasabah_id required UUID; active nasabah of the pengurus' bank nominal required; > 0; whole rupiah, no decimals (§8 Q5); max 12 integer digits; ≤ saldo metode required; tunai or transfer (no transfer reference fields, §8 Q7) tanggal optional, defaults to now; not in the future (§8 Q4) keterangan optional; max 255 chars status not accepted on input; always written as tercatat (§8 Q8)

Returns 201 with the detail payload below. Returns 422 {"errors": {...}} on validation failure.

GET /api/v1/pencairan/{id} returns the detail:

{
  "id": "uuid",
  "nasabah_id": "uuid",
  "nasabah_nama": "Sari Rahayu",
  "bank_sampah_id": "uuid",
  "dicatat_oleh": "uuid",
  "dicatat_oleh_nama": "Ibu Sari",
  "tanggal": "2026-09-22T10:15:00+07:00",
  "nominal": "200000.00",
  "metode": "tunai",
  "keterangan": "Diambil pagi",
  "status": "tercatat",
  "saldo_sebelum": "465600.00",
  "saldo_sesudah": "265600.00",
  "created_at": "..."
}

GET /api/v1/pencairan?nasabah_id=&periode= is a paginated list. It reuses the periode filtering from TransactionFilterService.apply_period, generalized to take a date field. It is kept minimal here and extended in PIL-222.

Update reference/PILAH_API_Documentation or the README with these endpoints.

docs.text:
Scaffold the feature with dart run codegen/spl_manager.dart add pencairan --state cubit.

features/pencairan/
  data/datasources/pencairan_remote_data_source(_impl).dart
  data/repositories/pencairan_repository_impl.dart

  domain/repositories/pencairan_repository.dart

  presentation/cubit/pencairan_form_cubit.dart (+ state)
  presentation/pages/catat_pencairan_page.dart
  presentation/widgets/metode_pencairan_chips.dart
  presentation/widgets/pencairan_berhasil_bottom_sheet.dart

The screen follows PRD Gambar 5.3.29 ("Ajukan Pencairan"), adapted for the pengurus:

  1. Entry points: a "Catat Pencairan" button in DetailNasabahBottomSheet (nasabah preselected), plus an optional dashboard action next to "Setoran Baru".
  2. Pilih nasabah: reuse PilihNasabahBottomSheet and show the current saldo.
  3. Nominal: rupiah-formatted input with inline "Maksimal Rp …" validation.
  4. Metode: Tunai / Transfer chips (design-system filter chips).
  5. Tanggal: date picker, default today, future dates disabled.
  6. Keterangan: optional multiline field.
  7. Summary: saldo sekarang, dicairkan, sisa saldo.
  8. Confirmation modal: "Pencairan Rp X akan dicatat sebagai pembayaran tunai."
  9. Submit: disable the button while loading (double-submit guard). On success, show the success sheet with nominal and saldo sesudah, then refresh NasabahCubit and the dashboard.
  10. Errors: map a 422 on nominal to an inline field error, and anything else to an AppNotification toast.

Add pencairan = "/api/v1/pencairan" to core/constants/endpoints.dart and register the route in app_router_config.dart.

docs.title: Backend (api/tests.py, keep coverage ≥ 80%)
docs.text:
• Creating a pencairan reduces saldo by the nominal and stores both snapshots and dicatat_oleh.
  • A nominal equal to the saldo succeeds and leaves saldo at 0.
  • A nominal greater than the saldo returns 422, and saldo and row count are unchanged.
  • Nominal ≤ 0, a nominal with decimals, an invalid metode, or a future tanggal returns 422.
  • A created pencairan has status == "tercatat", and a status sent in the request body is ignored.
  • A nasabah from another bank sampah returns 422 (no data leak).
  • An inactive nasabah returns 422 (see open question Q3).
  • Two sequential pencairan whose sum exceeds the saldo: the second fails.
  • Superadmin gets 403, unauthenticated gets 401, pending-bank pengurus gets 403.
  • List and detail are scoped to the bank: an id from another bank returns 404.
  • Regression: a setoran recorded after a pencairan reports the correct saldo_setelah_transaksi.
  • Regression: the Excel export's "Saldo Setelah Transaksi" accounts for pencairan.
  • makemigrations --check, ruff, and mypy api config all pass.

docs.title: Mobile (keep coverage ≥ 25%)
docs.text:
• PencairanFormCubit: success, 422 mapped to a field error, network error.
  • Remote data source: request body shape and response mapping.
  • Widget test: submit is disabled while nominal is empty, 0, or above saldo; the sisa-saldo summary updates.
  • Widget test: metode chips toggle, and the future date is not selectable.
  • flutter analyze --fatal-infos and dart format pass.

docs.text:

docs.title: 8. Open questions — answered 19 Sep (PM) and 20 Sep (tech lead)
docs.text:
1. Sprint placement. ✅ Committed to Sprint 1. Linear has PIL-176 in cycle Sprint 1 under EPIC04. CPBI-10 counts as done only once pencatatan, pembaruan saldo, and riwayat all work, so PIL-222 must be picked up by someone this sprint.
  2. Base branch. ✅ staging, for every repository. The ship skill defaults to it and must never infer main. PR #15 (PIL-152) targets main only because it predates the guide.
  3. Inactive nasabah. ✅ Active only. A nonaktif nasabah cannot be paid out; the remaining saldo stays stored.
  4. Backdating. ✅ tanggal is the real payout date or the scheduled date. Since no schedule model exists yet, Sprint 1 accepts any past date and rejects future dates.
  5. Minimum nominal or rounding. ✅ > 0, ≤ saldo, whole rupiah with no decimals in Sprint 1. The column stays Decimal(14,2); the serializer rejects cents.
  6. Jadwal pencairan (F12). ✅ Belongs to CPBI-10, not CPBI-07 (which covers jadwal kegiatan/penimbangan). It still has no sub-issue, so it stays out of PIL-176. Pengurus record payouts against an existing schedule informally.
  7. Metode transfer. ✅ There is no payment gateway, so transfer handling is outside our scope. Keep metode and an optional keterangan; no reference number or bank fields.
  8. Status. ✅ New requirement: pengurus and nasabah see nominal, tanggal, metode, status, and keterangan. Sprint 1 records one value (tercatat); the Sprint 2 request flow and PIL-230 extend it.
  9. Nasabah visibility. ✅ Pencairan appears in the nasabah's riwayat aktivitas in Sprint 1, but nasabah can neither request nor approve. PIL-152 gives nasabah accounts a login, so a nasabah-scoped read is now in sprint scope — open: does it belong to PIL-176 or PIL-222?
  10. Nasabah membership. ✅ Sprint 1 keeps one nasabah in one bank sampah. "Di setiap bank sampah" means each bank sees only its own nasabah and pencairan.
  11. Immutability. ✅ Once saved, a pencairan is a valid record. Changes only happen through PIL-230, by authorized users.

docs.title: API contract
docs.text:
Extends GET /api/v1/pencairan from #19. The response shape is unchanged: paginated {count, next, previous, results}, each result being the existing pencairan detail (id, nasabah_id, nasabah_nama, dicatat_oleh_nama, tanggal, nominal, metode, keterangan, status, saldo_sebelum, saldo_sesudah, created_at), newest first.

Query parameter Values Behaviour periode hari_ini, minggu_ini, bulan_ini, bulan_lalu, custom Same vocabulary as the transaksi list. When omitted, no date filter (all time) — unlike transaksi, which defaults to hari_ini — so #19's behaviour and the per-nasabah history are unchanged. dari_tanggal, sampai_tanggal YYYY-MM-DD Required with periode=custom; missing → 422, end before start → 400, matching transaksi. nasabah_id UUID Existing filter from #19. search text, 2+ characters Nasabah name contains, case-insensitive, matching transaksi.

Scoping is unchanged: only the pengurus' own bank, IsActivePengelola.
